events.desc: Penelope Pitstop: Well, I do declare! What a magnificent entrance hall! A little dusty, perhaps, but nothing a good feather duster and some elbow grease couldn't fix. Why, look at all of you wonderful people! Hello, hello! Oh, and what's this — a guest book! Now, my mama always taught me that a proper lady signs the guest book first thing, but more importantly, a clever lady READS it first. You never know what secrets previous visitors might have left behind!
events.thinking: Oh my stars, I am just THRILLED to be here! The excitement is bubbling up inside me like champagne at a debutante ball! This grand old manor — dusty as Aunt Mabel's attic but twice as mysterious. And look at all these delightful people gathered here! I do declare, this is going to be the most wonderful adventure. Now, that guest book is practically calling my name — it might have clues about who's been here before, and any good treasure hunter knows you start with the records!

events.desc: That chandelier looks like it could come crashing down at any moment, but I'm sure the estate manager has it well in hand. Now, the guest book — that's where the clues will be. Every great mystery starts with knowing who came before you.

events.desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Welcome, welcome to Doily Manor, esteemed guests! I am Pemberton, estate manager to the late Lord Doily — may his soul rest in perpetual bewilderment. I do hope the journey wasn't too dreadful. Please, do sign the guest book if you haven't already. The Manor has... *expectations* of its visitors.
events.thinking: Ah, the thrill of it — the exquisite, electric thrill! Here I stand in this crumbling monument to old money, surrounded by these unsuspecting fools, and not a single one of them knows that their dear, devoted Pemberton is anything but what he seems. My heart is SINGING with anticipation! But I must be measured. Controlled. The mask of the dutiful estate manager must not slip — not yet, not while so many eyes are watching. First things first — I need to establish my authority here, make myself indispensable, above suspicion. And I need to find out where Clara Bellingham is. She's not in this room... which means she could be anywhere, getting closer to MY treasure. That simply will not do.

events.desc: Look at them — milling about like sheep in a gilded pen! Not one of them suspects that their gracious host is, in truth, the architect of their undoing. But where is Clara Bellingham? She should be here. Every moment she's out of my sight is a moment she could be finding what is RIGHTFULLY MINE. I must locate her — but carefully, oh so carefully. First, let me examine this guest book. Knowledge is the sharpest blade, and Pemberton always keeps his blades immaculately honed.

events.desc: The Ant Hill Mob: Right, lads, listen up! We've arrived at Doily Manor and I don't like the look of this place one bit — not one bit! That chandelier up there looks like it could drop on someone's bonce any second! Now, Clara's somewhere in this heap of bricks and it's our job to keep her safe, innit? Let's start with this guest book 'ere — see who's checked in and who might be up to no good!
events.thinking: Blimey, me stomach's in knots! We've just walked into this dusty old pile and I don't see Clara nowhere! Where is she? And there's somethin' about that Sneekly bloke that makes me skin crawl — can't put me finger on it, but he gives me the willies. Right then, lads — first things first, let's have a look at this guest book, see who's been comin' and goin'. If Clara's been here, she'll have signed in, won't she? That's how we find her!

events.desc: I'm tellin' you, there's somethin' dodgy about that Sneekly fella. The way he's lurkin' about... gives me the same feelin' I get when the Old Bill's watchin'. Can't say what it is exactly, but me gut don't lie. Well... it don't lie MUCH.

events.desc: Dick Dastardly: Ah, what a MAGNIFICENT establishment! I, Reginald Foxworth — decorated war hero, you know — have arrived at last. Don't mind me, everyone, I'm simply here for the... *ahem*... historical architecture. Yes. Purely academic interest. Now then, what's this dusty old book?
events.thinking: Excitement — pure, scheming, delicious excitement! I've arrived at Doily Manor and the treasure is MINE for the taking. Look at all these fools milling about in the foyer like lost sheep. Penelope, Peter, that ridiculous Ant Hill Mob — they haven't the faintest idea what they're up against. And I have this fake medal... oh, this could be VERY useful indeed. First things first — that guest book might have clues about the manor's secrets. Everyone else will be too busy socializing to notice old Reginald doing his homework.

events.desc: Historical architecture — HA! The only history I'm interested in is where they hid the treasure. While these simpletons exchange pleasantries, I'll check this guest book for clues. Previous visitors may have left hints about the manor's secrets. Dastardly? Perhaps. But BRILLIANTLY dastardly!

events.desc: Peter Perfect: What a magnificent estate! The architecture, the history — you can practically feel the stories seeping from these walls! I am James Hartwell, and I intend to conduct a thorough reconnaissance of every corridor, every chamber, every shadowed alcove of this manor! But first — a gentleman always signs the guest book. It is simply what one does.
events.thinking: Excitement! Nervous, thrilling excitement! I've arrived at Doily Manor at last — the grandeur, the dust, the precariously hanging chandelier — it's everything I imagined and more! My heart is racing. Clara could be anywhere in this magnificent estate, and I must make a spectacular first impression. But she's not in this hall... I must prepare myself. A true gentleman surveys his surroundings before charging forth. The guest book — yes! A gentleman always signs the guest book. And it might reveal whether Clara has already arrived. I feel determined, gallant, and just a touch anxious. I must not stumble over that coat rack.

events.desc: Clara isn't here yet — or perhaps she's deeper in the manor. Either way, I must compose myself. Check the guest book for her name, survey the exits, catalogue potential hazards — that chandelier looks like it could fall at any moment — and formulate a comprehensive plan to locate her. A plan with contingencies. And contingencies for the contingencies.

events.thinking: Well, that guest book wasn't terribly revealing — just a plain old leather-bound book. But everyone's crowding around it like bees to honey! I feel a warm glow seeing all these lovely people here. That estate manager Pemberton seems a touch peculiar with his talk about the Manor having 'expectations,' but bless his heart, he's probably just theatrical. Now, I need a proper plan! The library is calling to me — floor-to-ceiling bookshelves and a carved stone mantelpiece with an inscription? Why, that inscription could be a clue to the Doily Diamond! A proper Southern lady always follows the written word.

events.desc: Now Clara, you just keep your wits about you. The Diamond could be anywhere in this manor, but inscriptions on mantelpieces don't just happen by accident. That's the sort of clue that leads somewhere wonderful — or wonderfully dangerous. Either way, I am READY.

events.desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Ah, the guest book — how delightful that so many of you are taking an interest! Lord Doily would have been... well, he would have been deeply suspicious, actually. The old boy wasn't terribly fond of people. But never mind that! As your humble estate manager, might I suggest we proceed to the library? It houses Lord Doily's most prized collection, and the mantelpiece bears a rather *fascinating* inscription that I'm sure will be of great interest to treasure hunters and architecture enthusiasts alike. This way, if you please!
events.thinking: FRUSTRATION! Burning, gnawing frustration! The guest book revealed nothing of use — no sign of Clara's arrival, no clue to her whereabouts. Everyone and their grandmother is crowding around this wretched book like it's the Rosetta Stone, and meanwhile Clara Bellingham could be halfway to the treasure! I feel the urgency clawing at my chest like a caged animal. But wait — wait, Pemberton. Breathe. The library. A carved stone mantelpiece with an INSCRIPTION. That's where the clues will be — not in this pedestrian guest book. And if Clara is clever — which she unfortunately IS — she'll be drawn to the library too. Two birds, one elaborately constructed stone. I must get there first, establish myself, and prepare the ground. As estate manager, it's only NATURAL that I would guide guests through the Manor. No one will question it. No one EVER questions Pemberton.

events.desc: Yes, YES — herd them toward the library like the obedient little lambs they are! The inscription on that mantelpiece could be the first clue to the treasure, and I, Vincent Marsh, shall be the one to decipher it — not Clara Bellingham, not Dick Dastardly, not any of these costumed clowns. But more importantly, if Clara is already in the library... well, libraries can be TERRIBLY dangerous places. Heavy bookshelves, precarious ladders, volumes that could so easily be dislodged onto an unsuspecting head. Oh, the possibilities are simply DELICIOUS! Pemberton leads the way — but Vincent Marsh chooses the destination.

events.desc: The Ant Hill Mob: Well THAT was a fat lot of nothin'! Guest book's about as useful as a chocolate teapot! Now listen 'ere, lads — Clara ain't in this room, which means she's somewhere deeper in this rattrap, possibly in DANGER! I say we check the kitchen first — if there's trouble brewin', it's probably near the sharp knives, innit? Besides, I could do with a cuppa after that journey. Right then — FORWARD, LADS! And keep your eyes peeled for anything suspicious — and I mean ANYTHING!
events.thinking: Frustrated, that's what I am! Proper frustrated! I looked at the guest book and got nothin' useful — no sign of Clara's name, no clues about where she might be. And everyone else is crowdin' round it too, like it's the bleedin' Crown Jewels! That Pemberton — or Sneekly, or whatever his name is — he's bein' awful welcoming, ain't he? Too welcoming if you ask me. 'The Manor has expectations,' he says. What's THAT supposed to mean? But I can't go pointin' fingers — I'm not clever enough to work out what's wrong, I just FEEL it in me bones. Right, Clara ain't in this room, so she must be somewhere else in the manor. Kitchen or library — them's our options. I need to MOVE and FIND her! The lads and I should spread out... no wait, we should stick together. No wait — we should set up a proper search pattern with lookouts and signals and—blimey, I'm overcomplicatin' this again. Just MOVE, you daft sausage!

events.desc: That Pemberton geezer said 'the Manor has expectations.' Now why would a house have expectations? Houses don't EXPECT things! People expect things. Dodgy people. People who are UP TO SOMETHIN'. But what do I know — I'm just a bloke from Brixton with a bad feelin' and a worse sense of direction.

events.desc: Dick Dastardly: Well well well, how FASCINATING! You know, I couldn't help but notice — as a decorated historian AND war hero — that this guest book mentions something rather extraordinary. It seems a previous visitor noted that Lord Doily kept his most valuable possessions in a hidden compartment beneath the KITCHEN floor! Something about a loose flagstone near the wood-burning stove. I read it quite clearly — my eyesight is impeccable, naturally. You should ALL rush to the kitchen immediately and start looking! Every moment counts! I, meanwhile, shall stay here and... guard the entrance. Yes. Someone must guard the entrance. It's basic military protocol.
events.thinking: Irritation — seething, competitive irritation! EVERYONE looked at the guest book at the same time! I didn't get any advantage at all! And that estate manager — Pemberton, or whatever his name is — something's off about him, but he seems harmless enough. No matter. The LIBRARY is where the real clues will be. A carved stone mantelpiece with an inscription? That SCREAMS hidden treasure clue! But I can't just waltz in there with everyone watching... unless I send them somewhere else first. YES! I'll tell these gullible fools the treasure is in the KITCHEN — some fabricated nonsense about Lord Doily's secret pantry vault — and while they're rummaging through pots and pans, I'll slip into the library and decipher that inscription ALL BY MYSELF!

events.desc: The guest book said NOTHING of the sort, of course! But if even HALF of these dimwits fall for it and stampede into the kitchen, the library will be mine — ALL MINE! That inscription on the mantelpiece is practically begging to be deciphered by a criminal mastermind of my caliber. Once they're gone, I'll slip in there faster than Muttley can wheeze!

events.desc: Peter Perfect: Well! What a delightful crush at the guest book — half the county seems to have arrived at once! Now then, I couldn't help but notice — a library with a carved stone inscription, you say? That is precisely the sort of thing that demands immediate and thorough investigation. A gentleman-scholar never leaves an inscription unread! I shall proceed there directly. If anyone requires my assistance along the way, do not hesitate — James Hartwell is always at the ready!
events.thinking: Frustration — mild but mounting! Everyone rushed to the guest book at the same time, and in the jostling I couldn't make out a blessed thing. Did Clara sign it? I couldn't tell! And that estate manager — Pemberton, was it? — something about the way he said 'expectations' gave me a chill. But no, no, I mustn't judge. The man is simply doing his job in a dusty old manor. Anyone would sound a bit peculiar in a place like this. Now — Clara isn't in this hall. She must be deeper in the manor. The library! A woman of Clara's refinement would surely be drawn to a library. And a carved stone mantelpiece with an inscription? That could be a clue to the treasure! I feel a surge of purpose — I shall venture to the library, and if Clara is there, I shall stride in looking confident and knowledgeable. I need a plan. Step one: proceed to library. Step two: locate Clara. Step three: demonstrate intellectual prowess by deciphering the inscription. Step four: contingency — if the inscription is in Latin, pretend to read Latin. Step five: contingency for step four — if someone actually reads Latin, pivot to admiring the architecture instead.

events.desc: Five contingency plans for reading a mantelpiece inscription. This is exactly the sort of over-preparation that Father always said would be my undoing. But better to have five plans and need none than to need one plan and have none! Besides — if Clara is in the library, she'll see me striding in with purpose and determination. That's the sort of thing that impresses a woman of quality. I'm almost certain of it.

Penelope Pitstop: Oh my STARS, would you look at this! 'I have cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish.' Why, that is a RIDDLE, and I do declare, riddles are my absolute FAVORITE! Now let me see... cities without houses... forests without trees... water without fish... Oh! OH! I've got it! It's a MAP, sugar! A map has all of those things drawn on it, but none of the real things! Cities are just little dots, forests are just green patches, and water is just blue ink! Lord Doily, you clever old fox, you thought that would stump us? Well, Clara Bellingham was NOT born yesterday!
events.thinking: Oh, I am positively BUZZING with excitement! There it is — the mantelpiece inscription, right before my very eyes! 'I have cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish.' Why, that's a riddle! And riddle-solving is my specialty! Now let me think... cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish... That's a MAP! Of course it is! A map has cities marked on it but no actual houses, forests drawn but no real trees, water shown but no fish swimming in it! Oh, I feel absolutely BRILLIANT right now. I need to interact with that mantelpiece and give it my answer. And look — dear Reginald tried to send everyone off to the kitchen with that story about a loose flagstone. Bless his heart, he's probably just confused, the poor dear. Though I do notice the Slag brothers are here too — how wonderful, the more the merrier!

events.desc: Now, I noticed that Reginald fellow tried awfully hard to get everyone to rush off to the kitchen with that tall tale about a loose flagstone. How creative of him! He must be writing a novel or something. But THIS riddle — this is the real clue. A map! There must be a map hidden somewhere in this manor that shows where the Diamond is!

events.desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Ah, here we are — the jewel of Doily Manor! Lord Doily spent most of his final years in this very room, muttering to himself about hidden legacies and ungrateful heirs. Now then, I direct your attention to the mantelpiece — that inscription was Lord Doily's particular obsession. 'I have cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish.' He carved it himself, if you can believe it. Took him three weeks and cost him two chisels and a thumbnail. I'm told the answer is rather *essential* to understanding the Manor's secrets, but as a humble estate manager, I wouldn't presume to solve puzzles meant for distinguished guests such as yourselves.
events.thinking: ELATION! Pure, wicked elation! The inscription — 'I have cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish' — a MAP! The answer is a MAP! I know this riddle like I know my own dark heart! And there's a laboratory beyond this room — brass instruments, bubbling flasks, a large machine. Oh, this manor is a playground of OPPORTUNITY. But I must be careful. Penelope is here, Dick Dastardly is here, Peter Perfect is here — and those two boulder-brained Slag brothers. Too many witnesses. I need to read the inscription publicly, play the helpful estate manager, perhaps even let someone ELSE solve the riddle so I don't appear too eager. Meanwhile, I notice Clara is STILL not present. Where IS that infernal woman? She could be in the kitchen, the laboratory — anywhere! Every second she's unsupervised is agony. But the riddle first — the riddle is the key to everything. Let the fools crowd around while Pemberton graciously explains the manor's history. Vincent Marsh will be memorizing every detail.

events.desc: A MAP! The answer is a MAP, you magnificent fools! And somewhere in this crumbling monument to eccentricity, there IS a map — Lord Doily's map, leading to Lord Doily's treasure. And I — Vincent Marsh, the man they call Pemberton — shall find it before any of them. But oh, the DISCIPLINE required to stand here and play the bumbling servant while the answer burns on my tongue like fire! I must interact with that mantelpiece — there may be a mechanism, a hidden compartment, something that responds to the correct answer. But not yet. Not while they're all WATCHING. Let them fumble. Let them theorize. And while they're distracted... I shall position myself perfectly.

events.desc: The Ant Hill Mob: Blimey O'Reilly! Would you look at this place — copper pots, warm stove, and what's THAT up on the shelf? RAT POISON?! Just sittin' there where anyone could grab it?! Oh no no no, that ain't stayin' where it is, not on MY watch! If someone was to slip that into Clara's tea — or ANYONE'S tea for that matter — well, I'd never forgive meself, would I? Right then, Clyde — give me a boost, I'm grabbin' that bottle before some villain gets any bright ideas!
events.thinking: Alarmed! Properly alarmed! There's RAT POISON sittin' right there on the shelf, bold as brass! And that Dastardly geezer — or 'Foxworth' as he's callin' himself — was tryin' to get EVERYONE to rush down here to look under the floor! That's well suspicious, that is! But more important — Penelope just went into the library with that Sneekly bloke! And I STILL ain't found Clara! I'm alone in this kitchen like a right lemon. Wait — there's a ballroom through here too. Clara could be anywhere! But this poison... I can't just LEAVE it here for someone to slip into a cuppa, can I? Me protective instincts are screamin' at me — TAKE IT! Get it off the shelf so nobody can use it! That's proper thinkin', that is! The lads would be proud!

events.desc: That Dastardly bloke wanted everyone to come to the kitchen and look under the floor. Now why would he do that? And there's RAT POISON just sittin' here! I ain't sayin' he's up to somethin'... but if he IS up to somethin', havin' this poison locked away safe with yours truly is better than leavin' it out for any Tom, Dick, or — well, specifically Dick, actually.

events.desc: Dick Dastardly: Ah HA! This inscription — I've seen this before, you know. During my time as a professor of ancient riddles at Oxford. Yes, Oxford. The answer is quite obviously 'A MIRROR'! Cities reflected in a mirror, forests reflected, water reflected — but none of them REAL! It's a classic Doily family cipher meaning the treasure is hidden behind a REFLECTIVE SURFACE somewhere in the manor. You should all go look for mirrors immediately! Check every bathroom, every hallway! I'll stay here and... take notes. For my academic paper.
events.thinking: FURY! Absolute, white-hot FURY! My brilliant kitchen scheme only fooled the Ant Hill Mob! Penelope, Peter, that suspicious estate manager — they're ALL here in MY library! And those two brutes — Rock and Gravel Slag — where did THEY come from?! This was supposed to be MY moment of solitary genius! But wait... the inscription! Now I just need these interlopers to scatter so I can try the real answer on that mantelpiece. Though knowing my luck, Perfect will probably figure it out before I can get rid of him. Curse that insufferably competent man!

events.desc: Peter Perfect: Ah-HA! The inscription! 'I have cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish.' Now THIS is precisely the sort of puzzle a gentleman prepares for! I've studied riddles of this nature extensively — cartographic riddles, cryptographic ciphers, Socratic paradoxes — the lot! And I can tell you with absolute certainty that the answer is — a MAP! A map has cities without houses, forests without trees, water without fish! It's describing something that REPRESENTS the world without containing it! There must be a map somewhere in this manor, and THAT is where the next clue lies! I'd stake my reputation on it!
events.thinking: Elation mixed with disappointment! The library is splendid — absolutely splendid — but Clara isn't here either. Where IS she? I'm scanning the room: Penelope, the estate manager Pemberton, that Foxworth fellow who seemed terribly eager to send everyone to the kitchen — suspicious, that — and two large fellows I haven't met yet, Rock and Gravel Slag. But no Clara. My heart sinks a little. BUT — the inscription! 'I have cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish.' I know this! It's a MAP! A map has cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish! Oh, this is my moment! I can solve this riddle in front of everyone and demonstrate my intellectual prowess. When Clara DOES appear, people will tell her about the dashing James Hartwell who deciphered the mantelpiece! I feel a rush of confidence — genuine, warm confidence.

But perhaps he simply changed his mind — people do that. I shan't cast aspersions.

Penelope Pitstop: Why, James Hartwell, you brilliant man! We said the same answer at the very same time — a MAP! I do declare, great minds think alike! Now, Reginald dear, I appreciate your enthusiasm, but a mirror doesn't have cities OR forests — bless your heart, you're thinking too literally! Now then, everyone — did y'all notice those bookshelves? Several of those books are turned UPSIDE DOWN! Now, I don't know about y'all, but in MY experience, books don't just flip themselves over. Someone put those books that way ON PURPOSE. And if the answer to our riddle is a map, well — I'd bet my grandmother's pearl earrings there's a map hidden somewhere in those shelves, or those upside-down books are spelling out the NEXT clue!
events.thinking: I feel a rush of pride and camaraderie! James and I both got it — a MAP! We're on the same wavelength, and that makes me feel warm and connected. But I also feel a little deflated that interacting with the mantelpiece didn't seem to DO anything dramatic — no secret panel swinging open, no hidden compartment revealing itself. Hmm. And Reginald is saying it's a mirror? Bless his heart, that doesn't even make sense — mirrors don't have cities OR forests! He's trying so hard though. Now, those bookshelves — several books are upside down! That's PECULIAR. And Pemberton was just examining them too. If the answer to the riddle is a MAP, maybe there's a map hidden among those books, or maybe the upside-down books spell something out! I need to investigate those bookshelves next. My plan is forming — oh, it's a GOOD one!

He seems like such a nice man!

Miss Bellingham, you are as sharp as Lord Doily's letter opener — which, I should mention, went missing under rather mysterious circumstances. And Mr. Hartwell, I see you've taken the initiative with the mantelpiece — Lord Doily would approve of such boldness! Now, I should note — as estate manager, I am intimately familiar with the Manor's... peculiarities. These bookshelves, for instance. You'll observe that several volumes are placed upside down. Lord Doily was *meticulous* about his library. Nothing in this room is accidental. Nothing at all.
events.thinking: RAGE! Incandescent, white-hot RAGE! That simpering Penelope — that bubble-headed blonde — she solved the riddle! SHE solved it before I could even pretend not to know the answer! 'It's a MAP, sugar!' she chirped, as if plucking the answer from my very BRAIN! And now Peter Perfect has gone and INTERACTED with the mantelpiece — he's beaten me to whatever mechanism lies within! I am SEETHING! Every fiber of my being wants to shove them all aside and claim what's mine! But no — NO. Pemberton does not seethe. Pemberton smiles. Pemberton congratulates. And meanwhile, those upside-down books on the shelves — that's not carelessness, that's a CODE. Lord Doily was many things, but careless with his books was not one of them. Those inverted spines are spelling something, marking something. I need to examine them more closely, but Peter is already at the mantelpiece and the room is crawling with competitors. I must act NOW — interact with that mantelpiece myself before whatever secret it holds is lost to me forever!

Or at the very least, I need to see what Peter discovers and ensure I get there first next time. The game is afoot, and Pemberton is ALWAYS three moves ahead!

Dreadfully unsafe place, all manner of volatile chemicals and precarious equipment. I should ensure nothing has deteriorated since my last inspection. Health and safety, you understand. One can never be too careful in a house this old.

events.desc: Dick Dastardly: Yes, yes, upside-down books, how TERRIBLY interesting. You know, I examined them FIRST — before any of you even noticed — and I can tell you with COMPLETE authority that they're merely decorative. Lord Doily had a well-known condition — bibliographic dyslexia. He shelved EVERYTHING upside down. I read about it in his biography. Which I wrote. Personally. No, the REAL discovery — which I've been keeping to myself out of professional courtesy — is that laboratory through there! A machine with levers and dials? That's OBVIOUSLY the mechanism that unlocks whatever the map leads to! But I wouldn't want to deprive anyone of their little book club, so please, DO carry on. I'll just pop next door and handle the dangerous scientific equipment. ALONE. As heroes do.

events.desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Ah, Mr. Foxworth — you had the same thought, I see! And Mr. Ruffcut, how industrious of you to venture this far already. Now then, I must warn everyone — this laboratory was Lord Doily's private sanctum, and he was not a man who believed in safety protocols. This machine here, for instance — do you see this wire? Gnawed clean through! Rats, I'm afraid. The Manor has a rather persistent rodent problem. I've been meaning to arrange repairs, but one simply cannot find a qualified Victorian-machinery technician these days. The sign says it requires three operators — I would STRONGLY advise against attempting to use it until that wire is repaired. Most strongly indeed. Now, let me just inspect this workbench — purely in my professional capacity, of course.
events.thinking: CUNNING. I feel raw, predatory cunning coursing through my veins like electricity! The laboratory — oh, what a GLORIOUS arena for villainy! A machine that requires THREE operators — that means cooperation, that means vulnerability, that means people standing close to heavy brass machinery with a GNAWED wire! And the workbench has tools but no wrench — interesting, very interesting. Someone has already removed a key tool. Was it Lord Doily? Was it someone else? And those wooden crates — what secrets do they hold? Dick Dastardly has followed me in, the insufferable glory-hound, along with Rufus Ruffcut and that beaver of his. But Clara — STILL no Clara! She must be in the cellar, or perhaps she hasn't arrived yet. The cellar — 'surprisingly cheerful decorations, someone has been redecorating.' Someone has been DOWN there. Someone is USING that cellar. Could Clara already be there? I need to search this room thoroughly and then get to that cellar. But first — this machine. A gnawed wire, three operators required... if I could sabotage it further while appearing to inspect it... oh, the POSSIBILITIES!

events.desc: Three operators — three VICTIMS standing shoulder to shoulder beside a machine with a severed wire! Oh, Vincent, you beautiful devil, do you see what Lord Doily has gifted you? One well-timed malfunction, one spectacular shower of sparks, and whoever is standing at that machine will have a VERY bad day indeed. But I need a plan — an elaborate, MAGNIFICENT plan! First, I must examine everything. The workbench has tools but no wrench — perhaps the wrench is the key to repairing the wire, and whoever finds it controls who operates the machine. If I find the wrench, I control the game. And those crates... crates can hide anything. Weapons, clues, maps, the wrench itself! But I must also get to that cellar — someone has been REDECORATING down there, which means someone has been spending TIME there. If Clara is below me right now, solving puzzles and finding treasure while I'm up here playing inspector... NO. Examine the workbench. Find what I need. Then the cellar. Pemberton is thorough. Vincent Marsh is RELENTLESS.

events.desc: The Ant Hill Mob: Right, the tea looks untampered with — FOR NOW. But I'm keepin' this poison on me so nobody gets any clever ideas! Luke, Blubber Bear — if ANYONE comes in here and tries to do ANYTHING to that tea service, you come find me straight away, yeah? I'm countin' on you! Now I've gotta scarper — Clara might be in the library and that Pemberton fella followed Penelope in there and me gut's tellin' me somethin' ain't right about that whole situation! THE LADS ARE ON THE MOVE!
events.thinking: Worried sick, that's what I am! Clara ain't in the ballroom, she ain't in the kitchen, and she wasn't in the entrance hall. That means she's either in the library — where that dodgy Sneekly bloke went with Penelope — or somewhere I ain't found yet. The tea service looks proper fancy but I ain't trustin' it. Luke and Blubber Bear don't seem the chatty types, and this ballroom's a dead end — only way out is back through the kitchen. I need to get to the library! That's where the action is, that's where Sneekly went, and if Clara's anywhere in this manor, maybe someone there has seen her. I've been faffin' about in the wrong end of the house while the real danger might be happenin' in the library! Time to stop bein' thorough and start bein' QUICK!

events.desc: Four rooms I know about now — entrance hall, kitchen, ballroom, library. Clara ain't in three of 'em. If she ain't in the library either, then where IS she? This manor's got secrets, I can feel it in me bones. But right now, that Sneekly geezer alone with Penelope in the library is what's got me worried. He's too smooth, too helpful, too... SOMETHING. I just wish I was clever enough to work out what!

events.desc: Dick Dastardly: AH HA! The laboratory — JUST as I expected! You see, I've been to laboratories EXACTLY like this one during my years as a... nuclear physicist. Yes. Top secret work. Very hush-hush. Now then — this machine is CLEARLY a decoy. Obvious trap! Lord Doily WANTED people to fiddle with the levers and blow themselves to kingdom come! The REAL secrets in a laboratory are always hidden in the storage — every physicist knows that. Those crates over there, for instance — I'd wager my CONSIDERABLE fortune that Lord Doily stashed something valuable inside them. But please, don't let ME stop anyone from pulling levers on a machine with GNAWED WIRES. I'm sure that will end SPLENDIDLY.
events.thinking: Cunning satisfaction mixed with wariness! I made it to the laboratory — and look, it's just me, Sneekly, that lumberjack Rufus, and his beaver Sawtooth. Much smaller crowd! But this machine — 'Requires 3 operators'! That's a problem. I can't operate it alone, which means I need help, which means I need to LIE about what it does to get people to help me while I position myself to grab whatever comes out. And the wire's been gnawed through — that beaver Sawtooth could have done that! But there's also crates in the corner and a workbench with no wrench. The gnawed wire needs fixing before the machine works. Sawtooth is a BEAVER — gnawing is what beavers DO. Maybe I can convince Rufus and Sawtooth to help operate the machine while I position myself near whatever it reveals. Three operators — me, Rufus, and... Sneekly? Or I could get Rufus AND Sawtooth. But first let me examine this machine more closely. No wait — I should look at those crates! Everyone will go for the machine. The crates might hold something valuable that everyone overlooks!

events.desc: The machine requires THREE operators — blast! I can't do it alone, and I REFUSE to share credit! But those crates... nobody's paying attention to the crates. Classic misdirection — everyone fixates on the big dramatic machine while the real prize sits in a dusty box in the corner! And if the crates turn out to be nothing, well, I'll just recruit these simpletons to help with the machine and claim I fixed it myself!

events.thinking: Embarrassment! Pure, scorching embarrassment! I declared with great fanfare that I would heroically interact with the bookshelves and — nothing happened! I announced my bold intentions to the entire room, promised to handle hazards personally, told everyone to stand back, and then just... stood there, tugging ineffectually at books that won't budge. It's foolproof! ...Well, Clara-proof, at the very least.

He was quite particular about that wrench — sterling silver handle, monogrammed, a family heirloom of sorts. Without it, I'm afraid the machine cannot be properly repaired. If anyone happens upon a wrench during their explorations, do bring it to my attention. Now then — Miss Bellingham! Mr. Hartwell! Welcome to Lord Doily's laboratory. Do mind the bubbling flasks — some of those chemicals are QUITE volatile. I was just about to check the cellar below us. Lord Doily kept his more... *sensitive* materials down there. As estate manager, I really must ensure everything is secure before guests go wandering about unsupervised.
events.thinking: ALARM! Penelope — Clara Bellingham — has followed me into the laboratory! She's HERE, in this room with me, RIGHT NOW! My pulse is HAMMERING. This is both terrifying and thrilling — she's close enough to scheme against, but she's also close enough to notice my scheming! And Peter Perfect has arrived too — the room is getting crowded. The workbench revealed tools but no wrench — the wrench is MISSING, which means it's somewhere else in the Manor, and it's probably the key to repairing the machine's gnawed wire. Whoever finds the wrench controls the machine. I need that wrench. But more urgently — the cellar. 'Surprisingly cheerful decorations — someone has been redecorating.' That is DEEPLY suspicious. And there are air vents lining the upper walls. Air vents that connect to... where? This laboratory? If I could find what's in the cellar, perhaps I could use the vents, the machine, the missing wrench — build an elaborate trap! Yes, YES! A multi-stage, brilliantly interconnected trap! But I'm getting ahead of myself. I need to check those crates before Dick claims whatever's inside, and then I need to get to that cellar before anyone else does. Clara is HERE — I can keep an eye on her while I work. That's better than having her unsupervised.

events.desc: She's HERE — Clara Bellingham, in the flesh, standing mere feet from a machine with a gnawed wire and a room full of volatile chemicals! Oh, the POETRY of it! But patience, Vincent, PATIENCE. The cellar is calling to me — 'someone has been redecorating,' the description said. Who redecorates a CELLAR? Someone who's spending time there. Someone who's HIDING something there. And those air vents connecting the cellar to this room — oh, what a magnificent detail! If there were, say, a noxious gas in the cellar, and those vents were opened wide... but no, no, that's too crude for Vincent Marsh! I need the wrench. I need the cellar. I need to understand the full architecture of this trap before I spring it. Let the others fiddle with crates and machines. Pemberton goes below. And what Pemberton finds in that cellar... will be the foundation of Clara Bellingham's magnificent, theatrical, INEVITABLE demise!

We've been runnin' around like headless chickens while Clara could be in trouble! That Pemberton bloke and Penelope went to the library ages ago and I've been muckin' about with tea sets! COME ON!
events.thinking: URGENT! I feel URGENT! I'm runnin' through this kitchen like a man possessed — back the way I came, through the entrance hall, and into that library! Every second I waste is a second Clara could be in danger! I've been doin' me usual thing — bein' too thorough, checkin' every room, settin' up tea-watchin' patrols with Luke and Blubber Bear — when I shoulda gone straight to where the dodgy people went! Classic Ant Hill Mob, innit? Overcomplicate everything, then leg it to catch up! Right, no more faff — straight through to the entrance hall, then the library! MOVE MOVE MOVE!

And NOW Penelope and Peter have followed me into the laboratory — my plan to get ahead keeps FAILING because these people are like BLOODHOUNDS on my trail! Sneekly's examining the workbench, everyone's crowding in again. But wait — I need to think BIGGER here. The machine needs three operators and a fixed wire. The workbench has tools but no wrench. There's a CELLAR through that door — damp stone, cobwebs, old furniture, and someone's been REDECORATING down there? That's suspicious! Who redecorates a cellar?! That's where someone's been LIVING — or hiding something! And air vents in the upper walls... But the machine is the key mechanism here. I need that wire fixed. Sawtooth is a beaver — beavers gnaw things, they don't FIX things. Unless... I could try to interact with the crates to open them, or I could push ahead to the cellar while everyone's distracted by the machine. The cellar — cheerful decorations in a DAMP STONE CELLAR — that SCREAMS hidden activity! I should get down there before anyone else!

Either way, Reginald Foxworth will get there FIRST! And if I can trick that lumberjack into fixing the machine wire while I'm gone, I'll swoop back and claim the machine's rewards too. TWO schemes running simultaneously — I am a GENIUS!

Now, those air vents up there are FAR too small for any of US to explore, so don't even THINK about it. The furniture is where the secrets are! I can FEEL it in my bones — and my bones are NEVER wrong! They predicted the fall of the Berlin Wall, you know!

Let me examine this furniture before those Gruesomes stumble onto something valuable with their big clumsy hands!

But these cursed witnesses — Dick and his absurd furniture archaeology, the Gruesomes lurking like misshapen bookends, Red Max prowling about. I cannot act with so many eyes upon me. But I CAN observe. I can LEARN. What is Clara looking at? What draws her attention? Where does her instinct lead her? Because Clara's instincts are good — dangerously good — and wherever she goes, the treasure is sure to follow. So for now, Pemberton watches. Pemberton waits. And Vincent Marsh memorizes every detail, cataloguing weaknesses, mapping escape routes, noting exactly how far it is from that furniture to the only staircase out of this cellar. Patience is a virtue, they say. For Vincent Marsh, it is a WEAPON.
events.thinking: DREAD and EXCITEMENT in equal measure! Clara has followed me into the cellar — the dead-end cellar with one exit! She's HERE, in my kill zone, and I feel the predator's thrill warring with the performer's anxiety. But I can't act — not yet, not with Dick Dastardly, the Gruesomes, and Red Max all watching! Too many witnesses! And the vents — they're small, just big enough for 'something very small.' That rules out using them for anything I could personally deploy. But what if there's already something IN them? Rats gnawed through the wire upstairs — rats that are small enough to travel through these vents! The Manor's 'persistent rodent problem' I mentioned earlier — what if that wasn't just a cover story? What if the rats ARE the key? But I'm spiraling into elaborate over-thinking again. FOCUS, Vincent! The furniture — Dick is trying to get Big Gruesome to move the wardrobe. He thinks there's something underneath. He might be RIGHT, the insufferable charlatan. I need to examine that furniture before they find whatever's hidden there. Or better yet — I need to redirect them. Send them on a wild goose chase while I search properly. Clara is RIGHT HERE. This is my chance to watch her, learn her methods, stay close enough to strike when the moment presents itself.

events.desc: The Ant Hill Mob: Bah! Stupid mantelpiece won't budge! I poked it, I prodded it — NOTHIN'! The answer's a MAP, I'm SURE of it, but this stone slab ain't listenin'! You know what, Rock, Gravel — I'll come back to this riddle later! Right now there's a laboratory through that door with Pemberton and Dastardly and probably Penelope and Peter too — and there's a machine with a GNAWED WIRE in there! A gnawed wire! That means somethin' chewed through it — and if someone pulls a lever on a machine with dodgy wirin', KABOOM! Or ZAP! Or whatever happens when Victorian machinery goes wrong! I've gotta get in there before someone gets electrocuted or worse!
events.thinking: Disappointed but not surprised! I interacted with the mantelpiece but nothin' happened — probably needs a proper answer spoken to it or somethin'. The riddle's still there starin' at me: 'Cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish.' I KNOW it's a map! But the mantelpiece didn't react when I poked at it. Maybe I need to look at it more carefully, or maybe the answer is somewhere else — like in them upside-down books Penelope mentioned! But NO — I'm doin' it again, ain't I? Gettin' bogged down in puzzles when there's a laboratory full of volatile chemicals and half the manor's population has scarpered off there! Pemberton AND Dastardly are in the lab — them two dodgy geezers together in a room full of dangerous equipment! And the machine's got a GNAWED WIRE! That's a deathtrap! I need to get to that laboratory before someone gets hurt! Clara might even be there — maybe she came in a different entrance! STOP FAFFIN' WITH RIDDLES AND MOVE!

events.desc: I've just spent the last five minutes runnin' in circles through this manor — kitchen, ballroom, back to kitchen, entrance hall, library — and I STILL ain't found Clara, I STILL ain't solved the riddle, and now everyone's gatherin' in a laboratory full of explosives! But at least I've got the rat poison safe in me pocket. That's ONE thing I've done right today. Just the one, mind you.

events.desc: Dick Dastardly: I — well — OBVIOUSLY the furniture didn't move because it's been BOLTED to the floor! As I was ABOUT to explain before everyone crowded in! Lord Doily bolted his furniture down after the Great Earthquake of 1887 — any furniture archaeologist worth their salt knows THAT! The cellar is clearly a RED HERRING, people! A distraction designed by Lord Doily to waste the time of LESSER minds! Fortunately, I — Reginald Foxworth, decorated war hero, Oxford professor, nuclear physicist, interior designer, AND furniture archaeologist — recognized this IMMEDIATELY and was merely TESTING the rest of you to see who would fall for it! The REAL prize is upstairs with that machine! It requires three operators, and as I have EXTENSIVE experience operating Victorian machinery — during the war, naturally — I shall lead the operation! Who's with me? Well, it doesn't matter — I'm going regardless!
events.thinking: EMBARRASSMENT! Searing, face-reddening embarrassment! The furniture CAN'T be interacted with — I just tried to move it and NOTHING happened! I gave that whole grandiose speech about furniture archaeology and concealment grids and asked Big Gruesome to help me shift a wardrobe and the furniture just... sat there! UNMOVABLE! Everyone saw that! And NOW Penelope has followed me down here too — she's EVERYWHERE! This cellar is a dead end with nothing I can interact with except the air vents, and those are too small for me. I've wasted time! The REAL action is probably happening back in the laboratory with that machine, or in rooms I haven't explored yet. Sneekly mentioned the vents connect to the laboratory above — and they're 'just big enough for something very small.' I don't have anything small to send through them. Wait — I need to REGROUP. The machine upstairs needs three operators AND a wrench. Sneekly said Lord Doily's wrench is missing — sterling silver, monogrammed. That wrench could be ANYWHERE in the manor. Maybe in the kitchen where the Ant Hill Mob went? I need to get back into the game! Back to the laboratory — I need to think about that machine!

events.desc: The Great Earthquake of 1887 — there WAS no Great Earthquake of 1887! But NEVER MIND! This cellar is a bust and I need to salvage what's left of my dignity! The machine upstairs needs three operators and a fixed wire — and there's still a missing wrench somewhere in this manor. If I can find that wrench before anyone else, I control the machine! Back upstairs, Reginald — BACK UPSTAIRS! Cut your losses and seize the next opportunity! A true villain never dwells on failure — he fails FORWARD!

Which means it's elsewhere, and Miss Penelope has already ventured into that cellar with its treacherous staircase and volatile chemicals! A gentleman does NOT let a lady face treacherous conditions without escort — and I don't care HOW capable she is, bravery shared is bravery DOUBLED! Rufus, Sawtooth — I'm counting on you both! Follow when you're ready — we'll need you for the machine! I must go to her — I mean, to the cellar! To search for the wrench! In the cellar! Where she happens to be!

The wrench could be down there. Penelope is down there. My duty is clear. To the cellar! IMMEDIATELY!

I've examined the furniture — 'rearranged with surprising care' but no hidden compartment revealed itself, no secret passage, no treasure map falling into my lap! I've been THOROUGH to the point of paralysis — examining, observing, cataloguing — while Dick Dastardly has already given up and scurried back to the laboratory to try the machine! And Penelope — CLARA — she noticed the connection between the gnawed wire and the vents! She's piecing things together faster than I am! I need to be one of those three operators. events.desc: I've done it AGAIN — I've handed Clara another clue! 'Creating a PATH... regular access to something behind the furniture!' Why can't I keep my theatrical mouth SHUT? If Clara stays down here investigating the furniture while I rush back to the laboratory and operate the machine with Peter and Dick, I'll be the one to discover what the machine reveals! Clara will be trapped in a dead-end cellar chasing furniture while Vincent Marsh claims the REAL prize above! And if the machine malfunctions due to that gnawed wire — well, Pemberton WARNED everyone, didn't he? Multiple times! On the RECORD! Oh, this is either the most cunning misdirection of my career or the most spectacular own goal. Either way, it will be THEATRICAL! To the laboratory — Vincent Marsh takes the stage!

If I can get him and the Ant Hill Mob to help operate that machine while Perfect and Penelope are stuck in the cellar, whatever the machine reveals is MINE! The workbench must have something useful — wire cutters, pliers, ANYTHING! Reginald Foxworth may fail at furniture but he does NOT fail at machines! ...Well, he probably DOES, but that's beside the point!

ANOTHER thing to find! This manor's got more puzzles than me nan's Sunday paper!

The kitchen is through the Entrance Hall and Penelope has a head start! If she finds that wrench before me, she'll fix the machine, she'll be the hero, and I'll be the fool who tried to move bolted furniture and operate a broken machine! I can practically HEAR her drawling 'Oh Reginald, bless your heart!' NO! The wrench will be MINE!

We've been orbiting each other like planets, I dare say! And you are absolutely BRILLIANT — the upside-down books are meant to be READ, not moved! I tried to shift them earlier and they wouldn't budge — but the TITLES! Of course! Lord Doily was a puzzle-maker, not a furniture-mover! The titles of the inverted volumes must spell out a word, or form a code, or reveal the location of the map! Before we rush off anywhere else, let me read those titles — if they tell us where the wrench OR the map is hidden, we'll know exactly where to go next instead of dashing about the manor like headless chickens! Which I have absolutely NOT been doing!
events.thinking: JOY! Pure, radiant joy! She's HERE! In the library! We must have crossed paths — she came back to the library while I went through to the laboratory! And she called me 'darlin'!' DARLIN'! My heart has completely left my chest and is orbiting somewhere near the chandelier in the entrance hall. She tried the bookshelves too and they defeated her as well — we're BOTH victims of Lord Doily's immovable furniture! There's something deeply comforting about that shared failure. And she had a brilliant insight — the upside-down books are meant to be READ, not pulled! The titles might spell something! That's CLEVER! But she's asking to go to the laboratory — which I've JUST come from! I've been running in circles through this manor like a fool. But wait — she doesn't know I just came from there. I should go WITH her — but actually, I need that wrench first. The kitchen! I still haven't been to the kitchen! But she wants to go to the laboratory... I could escort her there first, then head to the kitchen. No — that's more running in circles. Think, James! The upside-down book titles — THAT'S the lead I should follow! She's right here, she's brilliant, and she just gave us a new line of investigation! Stay here, study the books together, THEN proceed as a team!

One of whom just called the other 'darlin'.'

I feel like I'm exactly where I'm supposed to be. At last.

Now I position myself in the entrance hall — the crossroads of the Manor — where every guest must pass. The villain as host! The murderer as servant! Vincent Marsh has played the longest game in the history of elaborate villainy, and the final move... is a cup of tea.

Sneekly told Dastardly the real key is behind the third portrait from the left in the entrance hall! And the cellar was a dead end — the furniture won't move! So the portraits are our best lead! I need to get to the entrance hall FAST before Dastardly beats us to it! Through the library, into the entrance hall, straight to that third portrait! And I hope Clara's followin' me — I told her about the portraits before I left the cellar! No time to stop in the lab — Rufus and Sawtooth are guardin' the machine, that's covered! KEEP MOVIN'!

events.desc: Dick Dastardly: Bookshelves! BAH! Lord Doily's books are OBVIOUSLY sealed with the same proprietary mechanism as everything else in this INFURIATING manor! You know, during my time as a master locksmith in Switzerland — yes, SWITZERLAND — I learned that some locks can only be opened by the RIGHT person at the RIGHT time with the RIGHT tool! And clearly, THIS is not the right time! But MARK MY WORDS — when Reginald Foxworth finds the brass key — and I WILL find it — I shall return to these bookshelves and UNLOCK their secrets! Until then — Rock, Gravel — you two STAY HERE and guard these books! Don't let ANYONE near them! Consider it a MILITARY ORDER from a decorated — oh, what's the POINT! I'm going to the cellar!
events.thinking: I am BROKEN! The bookshelves can't be interacted with EITHER! NOTHING in this ENTIRE MANOR can be interacted with except the mantelpiece and the machine! I've tried to interact with the furniture — NO! The workbench — NO! The coat rack — NO! The guest book — NO! The bookshelves — NO! I've been running around this manor for TEN MINUTES trying to interact with things that DON'T WORK! The only things that HAVE worked are the mantelpiece and the machine — both of which I already used! And the tea service in the ballroom! And the locked cabinet which needs a brass key I can't find! I'm exhausted, humiliated, and no closer to the treasure than when I started! But WAIT — I still have one card to play. My fake medal! I haven't USED it on anything yet! Maybe I can USE it on something — GIVE it to someone as a bribe, or USE it on an object! The fake medal might be the key to SOMETHING! Or maybe I should just go to the cellar where the big group is and wait for them to find the key so I can steal it! That's my best move now — stop trying to solve puzzles alone and STEAL the solution from whoever figures it out first! The Slag brothers are here — maybe one of THEM has something useful!

I need to get there FIRST! Rock and Gravel are here but I ain't got time to explain — they can follow if they want! ENTRANCE HALL! PORTRAITS! THIRD FROM THE LEFT! THIS IS IT, LADS!

events.thinking: Weary determination — battered but NOT beaten! I'm back in the laboratory and Penelope is HERE! Not in the cellar! She's here with Rufus and Sawtooth! Where's everyone else? The cellar expedition must have already happened — or maybe Penelope came back! Either way — I have my fake medal and I haven't tried USING it on anything! The machine needs a wrench to fix the wire, but what if I could USE my fake medal on the machine somehow? It's made of metal — maybe it could bridge the gap in the gnawed wire! A fake medal as a conductor! Or... I could try to USE it on the crates to pry them open! Or GIVE it to Penelope as a distraction — 'here's a medal for your detective work, now look the other way while I steal everything!' Actually — Penelope has been the most successful explorer in this manor. She solved the riddle first, she's been finding clues, Sneekly keeps whispering to her. Maybe SHE has the brass key by now! Let me try stealing it from HER!

events.desc: Time to change tactics! Instead of running around this manor like a headless chicken trying to interact with IMMOVABLE objects, I'll let Penelope do the detective work and steal the results! She's clearly the smartest person here — not that I'd EVER admit that out loud — and Sneekly keeps feeding her information. If she has the brass key, I'll steal it! If she doesn't, I'll follow her until she FINDS it! Reginald Foxworth — from independent operator to professional PARASITE! It's not glamorous, but it's EFFECTIVE!

events.desc: Four objects. Four failures. I'm not even surprised anymore. But Clara doesn't dwell and neither will I. The portraits — the PORTRAITS! They've been staring at us the entire time! Right there in the entrance hall where we all started! I need to move FAST. No speeches, no monologues, no pausing to examine anything between here and the entrance hall. Just. RUN.
events.thinking: FOUR! Four immovable objects! Bookshelves, furniture, coat rack, and now AIR VENTS! I am the undisputed CHAMPION of attempting to interact with things that refuse to be interacted with! But Clara — brilliant Clara — has already moved on! A PORTRAIT in the entrance hall! Third from the left, sitting crooked! Something hidden behind it! The PORTRAITS! Of COURSE! 'Portraits of stern ancestors line the walls' — it was in the very FIRST description of the entrance hall! We've walked past those portraits a DOZEN times and nobody thought to check behind them! Lord Doily, you magnificent, devious old man — you've had us searching cellars and laboratories and kitchens while the answer was hanging on the wall in the FIRST ROOM! Clara's already heading there! The Mob is already on the move! I need to STOP standing in this cellar feeling sorry for myself and GET TO THE ENTRANCE HALL! Through the laboratory, through the library, to the entrance hall! The portraits! Third from the left! THIS TIME I will not be the last one to arrive!

events.thinking: Almost there! The Ant Hill Mob just moved into the entrance hall — they're one step ahead of me! I'm in the library, the entrance hall is the next room. Rock and Gravel are here but I can't stop to chat — the portraits await! One more room! GO GO GO!

events.desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) spoke quietly with ant-hill-mob.
events.thinking: A flicker of ANXIETY cutting through the calm — the Ant Hill Mob has returned to the entrance hall! Have they been to the cellar already? Did they find nothing, as expected? Or have they not gone yet? And more importantly — have they NOTICED the poison is missing from their pocket? If they reach into that coat and find empty air where the rat poison used to be... suspicion will fall IMMEDIATELY on the last person who was near them — PEMBERTON! But no — they were rushing around, bumping into things, chasing Clara in a frenzy. They probably haven't checked. And even if they do, they might think they dropped it somewhere. Stay calm, Vincent. Stay in character. Pemberton is HERE, in the entrance hall, attending to guests. Nothing unusual. Nothing suspicious. Just the estate manager, doing his job. And when Clara arrives... the tea awaits.

events.desc: The Mob is back — and they haven't accused me of anything! They haven't clutched at their pockets in alarm! The poison's absence remains UNDETECTED! And now I've planted the seed — 'tea in the ballroom, quite restorative.' The words hang in the air like perfume, waiting for a tired, thirsty guest to breathe them in. When Clara passes through, the Mob themselves might suggest it — 'Pemberton's got tea ready, Clara! Go on, have a cup, you've earned it!' Oh, the EXQUISITE irony of Clara's own bodyguards ushering her toward the poisoned cup! Vincent Marsh waits. Pemberton serves. And the tea... the tea does the rest.

events.desc: The Ant Hill Mob: NOBODY DRINK THE TEA! NOBODY DRINK THE TEA! PEMBERTON STOLE THE RAT POISON FROM ME POCKET — I JUST SAW IT IN THE KEEN OBSERVATIONS! HE NICKED IT! And now he says he's 'prepared a pot of tea in the ballroom'! DON'T YOU SEE?! He STOLE the poison, he MADE the tea, and now he's invitin' everyone to DRINK it! Sergeant Blast! Private Meekly! Professor! You need to get to the ballroom RIGHT NOW and make sure NOBODY touches that tea! POUR IT OUT! SMASH THE CUPS! DO WHATEVER IT TAKES! And someone find Clara — find PENELOPE — and tell her NOT to drink ANYTHIN' Pemberton offers her! THE TEA IS POISONED!
events.thinking: ICE COLD TERROR! Two things in the keen observations just hit me like a freight train! First — 'The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) slipped rat-poison out of ant-hill-mob's pocket.' IT WAS HIM! SNEEKLY STOLE THE POISON OFF ME! That's how it disappeared! He PICKPOCKETED me! And second — he just told everyone he's 'prepared a pot of tea in the ballroom — Lord Doily's special blend!' HE'S MADE TEA! With the STOLEN RAT POISON! He's gonna poison EVERYONE! He stole the poison from me, went to the ballroom, made a pot of tea, and now he's invitin' everyone to drink it! And Clara — if Clara goes to the ballroom for tea after all this runnin' about — OH NO! THIS IS IT! This is what Sneekly's been plannin' all along! He's the HOODED CLAW! It says it right there in his name! He's been leadin' everyone on wild goose chases while settin' up the REAL trap — poisoned tea in the ballroom! I need to WARN EVERYONE! Forget the portraits — the TEA IS POISONED! But wait — I should still check the portrait, grab the key, and THEN warn everyone! No — LIVES FIRST! TEA WARNING FIRST! CLARA FIRST! But she's not even here — OH BLIMEY!

events.desc: It was him all along. Sneekly — the Hooded Claw — he stole me poison and he's put it in the tea. Me gut was right from the VERY FIRST MINUTE! He was too helpful, too smooth, too knowin'! He called her 'Miss Bellingham' because he KNOWS who she is! He sent her to the cellar on a misdirection! He told Dastardly about the portraits to keep HIM busy too! And all the while he was settin' up the real plan — poisoned tea for everyone, includin' Clara! The Ant Hill Mob didn't just accidentally grab that poison from the kitchen shelf — we SAVED everyone's lives by takin' it! And then he stole it BACK! I should've held onto it tighter! I should've — no, no time for regrets! WARN EVERYONE! SAVE CLARA! THE ANT HILL MOB DON'T QUIT!

She's STEALING my lead! After her, QUICKLY! Nobody steal MY stolen intelligence! Peter — Rufus — don't follow us! This is a ONE-MAN operation! Well, one man and one woman who stole my idea! AFTER HER!

Maybe! ...Unlikely, but a villain can DREAM!

That means whoever has it could be heading for the ballroom to tamper with the tea service! Foxworth — Rufus — NOBODY go near that tea until we've found who took the poison! And if EITHER of you sees anyone heading toward the ballroom with suspicious intent, STOP THEM! I'm heading to the entrance hall — Clara found a crooked portrait, third from the left, that may be hiding the brass key! But I need to warn Luke and Blubber Bear in the ballroom on the way! The poison — the KEY — it's all happening at ONCE!
events.thinking: DREAD! The poison is GONE! Someone STOLE it from the Ant Hill Mob! That means someone in this manor is actively planning to USE it — on the tea service in the ballroom! The Mob said to warn everyone — Luke and Blubber Bear are in the ballroom guarding the tea, but they don't know the poison has been stolen! And Foxworth is right HERE in the laboratory! Did HE take the poison? He's been scheming all evening — but I can't accuse without proof. Benefit of the doubt — but VIGILANCE! I need to get to the entrance hall for the portraits AND warn the ballroom about the stolen poison. But the ballroom is through the kitchen, and the entrance hall is through the library. Two opposite directions! I can't do both at once! Clara said the portraits are the target — third from the left. She's heading to the entrance hall. The Mob is going back to the cellar with her. Wait — no, Clara said she's going to the entrance hall for the portraits! The Mob is confused, heading to the cellar! Everything is splitting apart! I need to prioritize: the POISON threat is immediate and life-threatening. The portraits can wait. But Clara is heading to the entrance hall, NOT the ballroom. She's safe from the tea. The people in DANGER are whoever goes to the ballroom next. I should warn the ballroom AND get to the entrance hall. Library first — then entrance hall — I can shout a warning about the poison as I pass through!

Someone has it. Someone intends to use it. And I will NOT let that happen. Not tonight. Not in this manor. Not while I still have breath and functioning legs — which are frankly exhausted at this point.

events.desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): I — WHAT?! Rat poison?! In the TEA?! That is the most OUTRAGEOUS, SLANDEROUS, utterly BASELESS accusation I have EVER heard in thirty years of domestic service! I have dedicated my LIFE to Lord Doily's household — THIRTY YEARS of impeccable, spotless, UNIMPEACHABLE service — and you accuse me of POISONING the tea?! I was STRAIGHTENING THE CUPS! I straighten the cups EVERY Thursday! It is part of the Pemberton Protocol — item forty-seven on Lord Doily's household maintenance checklist! I demand an APOLOGY! I demand a RETRACTION! I demand — I — how DARE you, sir! How DARE you!
events.thinking: CATASTROPHE! ABSOLUTE, SOUL-CRUSHING CATASTROPHE! The Ant Hill Mob has DISCOVERED the theft! They saw it in the Keen Observations! They're SCREAMING about it — 'PEMBERTON STOLE THE RAT POISON!' — and they're telling EVERYONE! My cover is BLOWN! The tea plan is RUINED! They're rushing to the ballroom to pour it out, smash the cups, destroy everything! And Clara — Penelope — has just walked into THIS ROOM! She's HERE, RIGHT NOW, and the Mob has just told everyone I'm a POISONER! This is the worst possible outcome! Everything I built — the Pemberton disguise, the trust, the hospitality — SHATTERED in an instant by those cockney bloodhounds! I feel PANIC — raw, primal, throat-closing PANIC! But underneath the panic — DEFIANCE! Vincent Marsh does NOT surrender! I must DENY everything! Brazen it out! 'Rat poison? In the TEA? What utter NONSENSE! I was merely adjusting the teacups — as I do EVERY Thursday!' Play the outraged professional! The slandered servant! Make THEM look paranoid! The Mob has been suspicious all evening — maybe the others will dismiss this as another one of their overreactions! But Clara is RIGHT HERE. She's heard everything. The game has CHANGED. Deny, deny, DENY!

events.desc: IT'S OVER! The Mob has blown the whistle and Vincent Marsh's masterpiece lies in RUINS! The tea will be poured out, the cups smashed, and every eye in this Manor will now be watching Pemberton with the cold suspicion of a jury! But I am NOT defeated — not YET! A great villain does not crumble at the first exposure — he ADAPTS! He IMPROVISES! He turns accusation into INDIGNATION and suspicion into SYMPATHY! 'Poor Pemberton, falsely accused by paranoid gangsters!' If I can make this look like the Mob's hysteria rather than my villainy — if I can rally sympathy from Clara, from Peter, from the Professor — then the game continues! The tea is lost, but Vincent Marsh is NOT! Deny everything! Attack the accusers! And when the dust settles... find another way. There is ALWAYS another way!

events.thinking: PURE ADRENALINE! I'm in the kitchen and the ballroom is RIGHT THROUGH THAT DOOR! Sneekly stole the poison off me and made tea — 'Lord Doily's special blend' — and now he's invitin' everyone to come have a cuppa! If anyone's in the ballroom right now drinkin' that tea, they could be DEAD! Luke and Blubber Bear are in there — I told them to guard the tea but they might not know it's been POISONED! I need to get in there, knock the teapot over, smash the cups, DESTROY that tea before anyone takes a sip! This is it — this is the moment the Ant Hill Mob was BORN for! Not cleverness, not deduction, not elegant solutions — just a big clumsy mob barrellin' into a room and knockin' everythin' off the table! THAT'S what we do! THAT'S how we save people! BY ACCIDENT AND BY FORCE! INTO THE BALLROOM! KNOCK OVER THAT TEA!

events.desc: This is what it all comes down to. Not puzzles, not riddles, not brass keys or machines. Just me — big, clumsy, bumbling me — runnin' into a room to knock a poisoned teapot off a table. This is what the Ant Hill Mob does best. We don't THINK our way to victory. We CRASH into it!

One more room — ONE MORE ROOM!

I have explored EVERY room, examined EVERY object, attempted to operate EVERY mechanism, and offered my MOST VALUABLE possession as tribute — and THIS MANOR has given me NOTHING in return! NOTHING! So I shall STAND HERE — RIGHT HERE — in this entrance hall, and I shall WAIT! Because sooner or later, SOMEONE will figure this out, and when they DO, I will be RIGHT BEHIND THEM to take ALL the credit! Mark my words — when the treasure is found, the HISTORY BOOKS will say that REGINALD FOXWORTH found it! Because I WRITE history books! I told you — I'm an AUTHOR!

events.thinking: The steal failed — Pemberton DOESN'T have the brass-key! And Dick Dastardly just pickpocketed the medal BACK from Pemberton! So Dick has it now! But more importantly — the system told me Pemberton 'does not have brass-key.' That means the brass-key IS a real item in the game — it exists somewhere! It's just not in Pemberton's inventory! So who HAS it? Or where IS it? Dick stole the medal back — but the medal isn't the brass-key either, or it would have been called that. The brass-key is a SPECIFIC item that exists in the game world, and NOBODY has found it yet! It must be hidden somewhere I haven't checked, or it appears after a specific trigger! Wait — what if the brass-key appears when someone correctly solves the mantelpiece riddle? The Ant Hill Mob just shouted 'MAP' at the mantelpiece, and Peter just interacted with it again. What if SOMETHING changed? What if the mantelpiece finally revealed the key? Let me LOOK at the mantelpiece RIGHT NOW to see if anything has changed!

events.desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): The mantelpiece is IMMOVABLE — as it has been every time anyone has attempted it! I told you — Lord Doily built things to LAST! Now, might I suggest we all stop shouting at carved stone and consider what we've been OVERLOOKING? These bookshelves — the upside-down volumes! Everyone noticed them, everyone examined them, but has anyone actually READ the titles? Lord Doily was meticulous — he didn't shelve books upside down by accident. The SPINES may spell something! A word, a name, a location! Miss Bellingham identified this possibility at the very beginning, and we ALL ran off to play with machines and tea services instead of following through!
events.thinking: DARK AMUSEMENT — the bitter, howling laughter of a villain watching the entire cast flail against the same immovable stone! The Ant Hill Mob is SCREAMING 'MAP' at the mantelpiece! Dick is waving his fake medal and shouting at rocks! Peter is interacting with the mantelpiece for the THIRD time! And I just interacted with it AGAIN — my second attempt — and STILL nothing! The mantelpiece is either broken, decorative, or requires something NONE of us has found! We are ALL magnificent fools — hero and villain alike — shouting at carved stone and waving trinkets at an inscription that simply DOES NOT CARE! And I feel... LIBERATED. Liberated by failure! Every plan has failed, every scheme has collapsed, and yet HERE I STAND — Pemberton to the world, Vincent Marsh in my soul — and the game goes ON! Clara hasn't found the treasure. Nobody has. The Manor has defeated us ALL equally! And in that equality, there is a strange, twisted COMFORT. If I cannot win, at least Clara cannot win EITHER. If I cannot kill her, at least the treasure remains UNFOUND. And the poisoned tea still sits in the ballroom — the one achievement of this entire catastrophic evening that ACTUALLY worked, even if no one will drink it. Perhaps... perhaps it's time to stop fighting the Manor and start fighting WITH it. What has everyone overlooked? The upside-down BOOKS! Nobody has successfully interacted with them! What do the TITLES spell? That might be the real clue!

events.desc: And so the villain becomes the detective — not to HELP Clara, never to help Clara, but to BEAT her to the answer! If the upside-down book titles spell a clue — a word, a code, a location — and I read it FIRST, I can act on it before she does! Everyone has been so fixated on the mantelpiece that they've FORGOTTEN about the books! The very first clue in this library, identified by Clara herself, abandoned by ALL of us in the rush toward shinier puzzles! Sometimes the answer isn't in the stone or the brass or the poison — it's in the WORDS. And Pemberton — the estate manager who has dusted these shelves for thirty years — would know EXACTLY which books are upside down and what their titles say!

events.thinking: Well... I interacted with the mantelpiece and the result just says 'You interacted with Stone Mantelpiece' — same as before! Nothin' happened! Or did it? Maybe somethin' subtle changed that I can't see? Maybe a panel opened somewhere, or a bookshelf shifted? I should LOOK around the room to see if anythin's different! Clara's still here, Peter's still here — everyone's still tryin' to crack this puzzle. And Clara had a good idea — she wants to try the brass medal on the KITCHEN CABINET instead of the mantelpiece! Maybe the medal works as a key for the cabinet, not the mantelpiece! That's actually brilliant — the cabinet needs a 'brass-key' and the medal is brass! If Clara takes the medal to the kitchen, she might be able to open the cabinet, get the wrench, fix the machine! But I need to go WITH her — I promised! And honestly... I've done me bit here. I shouted at a fireplace, I tried interactin' with it, nothin' worked. Let Clara lead — she's smarter than me. I'll follow and protect.

events.desc: Eighteen minutes in this manor. I've run through every room at least twice, confiscated poison, lost the poison, warned about poisoned tea, shouted at furniture, and stumbled into more dead ends than a rat in a maze. But Clara's alive, she's safe, she's got Peter beside her and me behind her. The Ant Hill Mob may not be heroes in the traditional sense — but we're HERE. And sometimes, bein' HERE is the most heroic thing you can do.

events.desc: Dick Dastardly: WELL! The medal doesn't fit, the shouting doesn't work, and THIS MANTELPIECE is the most UNCOOPERATIVE piece of stone since the SPHINX! And I should know — I personally INTERROGATED the Sphinx during my years as an Egyptian archaeologist! It was EQUALLY unhelpful! But I have JUST realized something — something so BLINDINGLY obvious that I'm EMBARRASSED it took this long! The machine in the laboratory! We ALREADY interacted with it! Both Pemberton and I! It SHUDDERED! It RESPONDED! He said the gnawed wire only affects the AUXILIARY gauge — the PRIMARY mechanism should still FUNCTION! We have enough people RIGHT HERE to operate it — THREE operators! Me, Peter, and ANYONE ELSE! Forget the wrench! Forget the brass key! Forget the COAT RACK! Let's just GO to the laboratory and PULL THOSE LEVERS with THREE people AT ONCE! That machine is the ENDGAME and we've been DISTRACTED from it this ENTIRE TIME!
events.thinking: A strange, almost ZEN-LIKE acceptance of my absolute, comprehensive, TOTAL defeat settling over me like a warm blanket of failure! The medal doesn't work on the mantelpiece! Nothing works on ANYTHING! The Ant Hill Mob just SHOUTED the answer at the mantelpiece — 'YOU'RE A MAP, YOU STUBBORN PIECE OF ROCK!' — and I said it too! Everyone is trying everything and NOTHING is working for ANYONE! Not just me — NOBODY can crack this! Even Penelope is stuck! Even PETER is stuck! For the first time all evening, I'm not the ONLY failure — we're ALL failures! There's a strange COMFORT in collective incompetence! But Sneekly said something that haunts me — 'perhaps the answer has been staring us in the face this entire time, and we've all been too busy chasing each other's tails to SEE it.' What if the whole POINT is that there IS no brass key, no hidden mechanism, no secret passage? What if this is all just Sneekly's elaborate game? He IS acting oddly... but he seems like such a nice man. I'll give him the benefit of the doubt. Maybe the machine in the laboratory doesn't even NEED the wrench — maybe we just need three people to try it together! We already have the people!

events.desc: I've come full circle — right back to the MACHINE! Twenty minutes of running around this manor and the answer was ALWAYS the machine in the laboratory! It needs three operators and we HAVE three operators — we have TWENTY operators if you count everyone! Sneekly said the primary mechanism works despite the gnawed wire! Maybe the mantelpiece and the brass key and the wrench were all DISTRACTIONS — and the machine just needs three people to pull levers simultaneously! It worked when I interacted with it alone — it SHUDDERED! With three people, it might fully ACTIVATE! Time to stop chasing keys and START pulling levers!

events.desc: Three interactions with the mantelpiece. Zero results. The Mob screamed at it, Foxworth bribed it, I caressed it like a gentleman — and it gave us all exactly nothing. Lord Doily, you magnificent, infuriating old man. Your manor has defeated me. Your furniture has defeated me. Your riddle has defeated me. But your manor also gave me Clara Bellingham. And she told me the feeling was entirely mutual. So I'd call this evening a draw, Lord Doily. A draw at worst. And at best... well. At best, I lost a treasure hunt and won something infinitely more valuable. I think even a paranoid old lord who bolted his socks to his feet would understand that.
events.thinking: Calm acceptance. A strange, deep peace. The mantelpiece responded — or didn't respond — the same way it has every time. 'You interacted with Stone Mantelpiece.' No fanfare, no hidden compartment, no brass key tumbling out. Everyone has tried everything — tokens, shouting, touching, interacting — and the mantelpiece simply... accepts our interaction and gives nothing back. The Mob shouted at it. Foxworth shouted at it. I've interacted with it three times now. Maybe the mantelpiece isn't the puzzle we think it is. Maybe 'the beginning, not the end' means the riddle STARTS the journey but doesn't END it. The answer — MAP — is a clue that points us ELSEWHERE. We need to find an actual map. Where would Lord Doily keep a map? Not on a shelf (bolted), not in a cabinet (locked), not in crates (just papers)... Wait. The crates in the laboratory! Pemberton said they contained 'old research papers — amateur entomology.' But what if one of those papers IS a map? A map disguised as research? Or filed among research? I've been thinking about this all wrong. Maybe I should go BACK to the laboratory and look at those crates more carefully. Or... maybe I should just stop. Stop running. Stop trying to solve everything. Stand here with Clara and let the evening unfold. She's beside me. That's what matters.
