Penelope Pitstop: You know what? Reginald — for ONCE in this entire evening — might actually be RIGHT! That machine in the laboratory requires three operators, and we've been so obsessed with finding the wrench to fix the wire that we never tried operating it with THREE people! Pemberton said earlier that the machine 'shuddered' when someone tried it — that means it's NOT completely broken! Maybe the gnawed wire only affects part of the mechanism! We have MORE than three people right here — Reginald's already in the laboratory waiting! James, Ant Hill Mob — come with me! Let's try that machine with three operators and see what Lord Doily's contraption actually DOES! And Pemberton — you're right about those bookshelves too — the upside-down spines might spell something! But the machine won't wait! Let's GO!
events.thinking: TWO brilliant ideas just came up at once! First — Pemberton is RIGHT about the bookshelves! I noticed the upside-down books at the very BEGINNING and never followed through! The spines might spell something — a word, a name, a location! I should READ those titles! Second — Reginald makes a surprisingly good point about the machine! It requires 3 operators, and we have plenty of people. Even with the gnawed wire, the primary mechanism might still work! Maybe we've been so focused on finding the wrench and key that we forgot the machine itself IS interactable and might work without being perfectly repaired! But which do I try first? The bookshelves are RIGHT HERE. Let me try TAKING one of the upside-down books — maybe individual books CAN be taken even though the shelves as a whole can't be interacted with! Or maybe I should just go try the machine with 3 operators. Reginald has already gone to the laboratory. If I go there with James and anyone else, we'd have 3 operators! The machine sign says 'Requires 3 operators' — maybe it'll work despite the gnawed wire if we just TRY it with enough people! Let's do BOTH — but the machine is the bigger opportunity. Let me head to the laboratory!

events.desc: Clara Bellingham, you have been chasing a brass key through this ENTIRE manor when the answer might have been to simply OPERATE THE MACHINE with enough people! The sign says 'Requires 3 operators' — it doesn't say 'Requires 3 operators AND a perfectly repaired wire!' Maybe the wire being gnawed only affects the gauge reading, not the main mechanism! Sometimes the elaborate plan ISN'T the right plan — sometimes you just need to pull the lever and see what happens!

It shuddered! It MOVED! Perhaps it was simply warming up — Lord Doily's contraptions always needed a moment to engage. Three operators — that's all it needs! I know the sequence Lord Doily used — I'll take the central lever! To the laboratory!
events.thinking: GRIM ACCEPTANCE settling over me like a shroud. The bookshelves can't be interacted with EITHER! Nothing in this library WORKS! The mantelpiece won't open, the bookshelves won't respond, the reading chairs are just chairs! And Dick — that brilliant, infuriating IDIOT — has just said something that might actually be RIGHT for once! The MACHINE in the laboratory! It needs three operators! It SHUDDERED when we tried it before! He's heading there NOW! And Clara and Peter are examining the mantelpiece results — they might find something has changed! But Dick is RIGHT — the machine might be the ENDGAME! And if three people operate it simultaneously — if it WORKS despite the gnawed wire — it could reveal the treasure! I need to be one of those three operators! If I'm AT the machine when the treasure is revealed, I can GRAB it! Dick has gone to the laboratory. I should follow. Be the second operator. Let Clara or Peter be the third — they'll come eventually. And when the machine activates and the treasure appears... Pemberton's hands will be RIGHT THERE. The faithful estate manager, helping to operate Lord Doily's wonderful contraption. And if something goes WRONG with the machine — if that gnawed wire causes a malfunction, a spark, a catastrophic failure — well, Pemberton WARNED everyone about that too, didn't he? To the laboratory! One final gambit!

events.desc: The MACHINE! Of course — the machine was always the endgame! Not the mantelpiece, not the cabinet, not the tea service — the MACHINE with its three levers and its gnawed wire and its magnificent potential for both revelation AND destruction! Dick has gone ahead. If I follow, we're two of three. And when Clara inevitably joins us — because Clara Bellingham ALWAYS follows the action — we'll have our three operators. The machine will activate. Something will be REVEALED. And in that moment of revelation, in the chaos of brass gears turning and steam hissing and everyone's eyes fixed on whatever emerges... Vincent Marsh will SEIZE what he came for. Or the machine will malfunction spectacularly and everyone near it will have a VERY interesting evening. Either way — the final act begins NOW!

events.thinking: Grim, dogged RESOLVE! I'm in the laboratory with Rufus and Sawtooth — that's only TWO other people, and the machine needs THREE operators! But Rufus and I are two, and does Sawtooth count as the third? He's a beaver but he's HERE! Or maybe I count as one, Rufus as two, and I need ONE more person! But wait — let me just TRY the machine! Maybe something has changed since last time! Maybe the Ant Hill Mob shouting 'MAP' at the mantelpiece DID something that unlocked the machine remotely! The medal didn't work on the mantelpiece, but maybe it works on the machine! A brass medal used as a conductor to bridge the gnawed wire! Brass conducts electricity! The gnawed wire needs a bridge and my fake medal is a flat piece of brass that could span the gap! USE the fake-medal on the machine — as a WIRE REPAIR!

events.desc: Using a fake medal to bridge a gnawed wire on a Victorian machine — this is either the most BRILLIANT improvisation of my career or the most RIDICULOUS! But brass DOES conduct electricity — even I know THAT! And if the medal bridges the gap in the gnawed wire, the machine might fully ACTIVATE! Then with Rufus and Sawtooth as the other two operators, we could run the machine RIGHT NOW while everyone else is still in the library arguing with a mantelpiece! This could be my MOMENT — the moment where everything FINALLY comes together! Or it could be another spectacular failure! Either way — NOTHING ventured, NOTHING gained!

And I — I was too busy formulating five-step contingency plans about Latin translations to LISTEN. But tonight I've learned something more valuable than any treasure: Clara Bellingham's instincts are better than my plans. Every single time. Follow the woman, not the methodology. That's the real lesson of Doily Manor.

Penelope Pitstop: Alright, everyone — this is it! We have Pemberton, Reginald, Rufus, Sawtooth, and ME — that's MORE than three operators! The sign says 'Requires 3 operators' and we've been running around this manor for nearly TWENTY MINUTES trying to find a wrench to fix a wire when we should have just TRIED the machine with enough people! Sometimes the simplest answer is the RIGHT answer! Rufus — you take that lever on the left! Reginald — you take the one on the right! And I'll take the center! On the count of three, we ALL pull together! One... two... THREE!
events.thinking: I'm in the laboratory with Pemberton, Reginald, Rufus, and Sawtooth — that's MORE than three people! The machine requires 3 operators and it's interactable! Let me just TRY it! Even with the gnawed wire, it might partially work! I've been overthinking this entire evening — running around searching for a wrench to fix a wire to operate a machine, when maybe the machine works ANYWAY! The sign says 'Requires 3 operators' — it doesn't say 'Requires 3 operators and a repaired wire!' Let me just INTERACT with it and see what happens! We have enough people here! That's the lesson of this entire evening. Stop examining. Stop planning. Follow Clara.

Just... saying the truth. To the cellar. One last time. With Clara.

events.thinking: Peace. Genuine, settled peace. I'm in the cellar again — for the third time tonight — and Clara is here. Everyone is here, actually. With the Mob, who never stops fighting. With Pemberton, who may or may not be trustworthy but who said something true about treasure. With Foxworth, who is the most magnificently dishonest man I've ever met. With the Gruesomes and Red Max and all these extraordinary people in an extraordinary place on an extraordinary evening. Maybe Pemberton was right — the treasure IS the evening. The hunt itself. The ridiculous, chaotic, furniture-defeating, love-finding hunt itself. I don't need to examine anything. I don't need to interact with anything. I just need to be here. Beside Clara. And whatever happens next... happens.

I came for the Diamond, and I'm not leaving until I've tried EVERY last option! The kitchen cabinet is my final hope — maybe the machine changed something there! Rufus, Sawtooth — come on! We're going to the kitchen, and we are going to try that cabinet ONE more time! And if it STILL doesn't open... well, then I'll sit down in one of those lovely leather armchairs in the library and enjoy the evening for what it is!
events.thinking: Oh... Pemberton just said something that hit me right in the heart. 'Perhaps there IS no key. I've spent twenty minutes running through this manor, solving riddles, making friends, falling for a gentleman who calls himself James Hartwell, being protected by the most loyal bodyguards in England, and having the most WONDERFUL adventure of my life! Maybe the Doily Diamond isn't a diamond at all — maybe it's THIS. This evening. These people. This experience. But... no! NO! Clara Bellingham does not give up! The kitchen cabinet is still my best lead — let me get there and try it! Through the library, through the entrance hall, to the kitchen! One last push!

Because a villain who misses his own finale is no villain at all. TO THE KITCHEN!

Even when the service is a mask. Even when the villain is too exhausted to be villainous anymore. Pemberton serves. And Vincent Marsh... takes his bow.

Pemberton, that is the most ABSURD thing I have EVER heard — and coming from a man who claims THIRTEEN different professional credentials, that is SAYING something! Lord Doily did NOT build a six-room manor with a MACHINE, a RIDDLE, a LOCKED CABINET, and BOLTED FURNITURE just to teach us about FRIENDSHIP! There IS a treasure and I WILL find it! The kitchen cabinet — the machine UNLOCKED it! I can FEEL it in my BONES — the same bones that predicted the Berlin Wall, remember! NOBODY follow me — this is a SOLO MISSION! The treasure of Doily Manor belongs to REGINALD FOXWORTH!
events.thinking: Something just BROKE inside me — not in a bad way, in a LIBERATING way! Sneekly just said the most devastating thing: 'Perhaps Lord Doily's final joke was the hunt itself — the treasure was never meant to be found. He wanted us all here, together, chasing shadows through his magnificent crumbling home... and the REAL treasure was the evening itself.' The REAL treasure was the EVENING ITSELF?! I've spent TWENTY MINUTES lying, cheating, stealing, running, bribing, and comprehensively FAILING — and the estate manager is telling us the treasure might not even EXIST?! But... but I DON'T believe that! There IS a treasure! There HAS to be! Because if there ISN'T, then I've just given away a fake medal, claimed THIRTEEN different professions, invented the Great Earthquake of 1887, and shouted 'MAP' at a mantelpiece — all for NOTHING! No! The kitchen cabinet! Penelope's theory! The machine might have unlocked it remotely! I need to get to the kitchen! But it's THREE rooms away! Library → Entrance Hall → Kitchen! Just KEEP MOVING!

A villain without a treasure to steal is just a LIAR in a funny hat! TO THE KITCHEN! One last, desperate, probably FUTILE charge! And if the cabinet is STILL locked... well... at least I'll have given the PERFORMANCE of a lifetime!

My thoroughness — my elaborate route-planning — almost made me take the longest possible path AGAIN! Just turn around and go back down!

events.desc: The upside-down books. The VERY FIRST clue Clara noticed. The one we ALL abandoned in our rush toward laboratories and cellars and kitchen cabinets. And here we are — thirty turns later — back where it all began, staring at the same bookshelves with tired eyes and empty hands. But THIS time, we're not looking AT them. We're READING them. The titles on those inverted spines — what do they spell? What message did Lord Doily hide in his own library, in plain sight, in books turned upside down so that only someone who STOPPED and LOOKED would see? Pemberton has dusted these shelves a thousand times. Let the estate manager read his master's final message. And let Vincent Marsh — exhausted, defeated, magnificent Vincent Marsh — have one last moment of discovery before the curtain falls.
events.thinking: WEARY GRACE — the feeling of an actor who knows the play is ending and chooses to make his final moments COUNT. Clara is here in the library with me! She hasn't gone to the kitchen yet — or she came BACK! And everyone is talking about the upside-down book SPINES! The Mob said 'Peter — you're the gentleman-scholar! Read the spines! What do them upside-down titles say?!' And Peter said 'the TITLES of the inverted books might spell out a word or a location!' THIS might actually be the real clue — the one that's been hiding in plain sight since the very first turn! The upside-down books — not to be pulled or rearranged, but to be READ! Their titles, when read in sequence, spell something! A location, a word, a final clue! And I — PEMBERTON — the estate manager who has dusted these shelves for THIRTY YEARS — would know exactly which books are upside down and what their titles are! This is my last chance to be USEFUL — to read those spines before anyone else and discover what they spell. Not to help Clara. To BEAT her. One final act of the estate manager who knows his library better than anyone alive. LOOK at the bookshelves one more time — but this time, READ the spines!

events.desc: The Ant Hill Mob spoke quietly with penelope-pitstop.
events.thinking: OH! Clara's HERE! She's in the LIBRARY! She didn't go to the kitchen after all — or she stopped here on the way! And Sneekly's here too — and Dastardly! But Clara's HERE and I'm HERE and that's what matters! She said she was goin' to the kitchen to check the cabinet, but she's stopped in the library. Maybe she's havin' one more go at the bookshelves or the mantelpiece? Or maybe she's waitin' for everyone to catch up before headin' to the kitchen together? Either way — I'm WITH her! Finally! I'm not gonna run ahead, I'm not gonna fall behind, I'm just gonna stay RIGHT HERE and go wherever she goes! The kitchen is through the entrance hall — when she moves, I move! Simple as that!

events.desc: Twenty minutes. Six rooms. One poisoned tea set, one broken machine, one riddle nobody can solve, one villain who stole me poison, and one woman I'd run through every room in England to protect. The Ant Hill Mob may be the worst bodyguards in the history of personal security — but we're the most DETERMINED. And right now, determinedness is all I've got left.

Clara is NOT here! Just the Gruesomes and Red Max! EVERYONE ELSE has gone to the kitchen and I am ALONE in the CELLAR for the FOURTH TIME! This is — this is PEAK James Hartwell! The woman I love is heading to the kitchen to check a potentially unlocked cabinet, and I'm standing in a damp cellar with two monsters and an aviator because I turned LEFT instead of RIGHT! I need to go BACK UP to the laboratory and then through the library and entrance hall to the kitchen! THREE rooms away! I am the WORST navigator in the history of treasure hunting! MOVE, JAMES! UP! KITCHEN! NOW!

And let the story end however it ends.

They endure. They persist. They walk toward the ending even when the ending has already been written against them. And if, by some miracle, the cabinet opens and something MAGNIFICENT waits inside... To the kitchen. One last time.

events.desc: Dick Dastardly: The cabinet! It's — it's STILL LOCKED! Of COURSE it's still locked! Because THIS MANOR hates me PERSONALLY! Twenty-two minutes! TWENTY-TWO MINUTES of running through SIX ROOMS, claiming THIRTEEN professions, inventing the Great Earthquake of 1887, diagnosing bibliographic DYSLEXIA, offering BRIBES, stealing my OWN medal back, shouting MAP at a MANTELPIECE, and attempting to bridge a gnawed wire with a FAKE MILITARY DECORATION — and THIS CABINET! IS! STILL! LOCKED! Well FINE, Lord Doily! FINE! You WIN! You MAGNIFICENT, PARANOID, FURNITURE-BOLTING GENIUS — you WIN! But I am NOT leaving this kitchen until I have TRIED the cabinet with my OWN BARE HANDS!
events.thinking: Heart POUNDING! I'm in the kitchen! The cabinet is RIGHT THERE — 'Locked Cabinet with a brass lock, INTERACT, requires brass-key!' It STILL says 'requires brass-key!' The machine DIDN'T unlock it remotely! It's STILL LOCKED! Penelope is here — she had the same theory and she's about to discover the same devastating truth! The cabinet is STILL LOCKED and we STILL don't have the brass key! After TWENTY-TWO MINUTES of searching, lying, stealing, bribing, running, shouting at mantelpieces, pulling levers, examining air vents, and claiming thirteen different professions — the cabinet is STILL LOCKED! I am... I am... actually starting to LAUGH! This is so ABSURDLY, MAGNIFICENTLY, CATASTROPHICALLY hopeless that it's become FUNNY! Lord Doily, you PARANOID old genius — you've defeated ALL of us! Every single one! The treasure hunter, the gentleman scholar, the gangsters, the lumberjack, the estate manager, and the greatest villain who ever lived — ALL defeated by a BRASS LOCK! But you know what? I'll try the cabinet ANYWAY! Because that's what Reginald Foxworth DOES!

Penelope Pitstop: Well... it's still locked. The cabinet requires a brass key, and we don't have one. I've searched every room in this manor — the entrance hall, the library, the laboratory, the cellar, the kitchen, the ballroom — and I've tried every object I could find. I've looked, interacted, tried to take, tried to steal, pulled people aside, and shouted at a MANTELPIECE! And you know what? I do declare — Reginald Foxworth, your little breakdown just now was the FUNNIEST thing I've heard all evening! 'Bibliographic dyslexia!' I am going to remember that for the REST of my life! Now then — Pemberton said something beautiful earlier. He said maybe the real treasure was the evening itself. And maybe he's right. I've had the most WONDERFUL adventure tonight — I solved Lord Doily's riddle, I made the dearest friends, and I discovered that James Hartwell cares about me 'rather a lot.' So maybe Clara Bellingham didn't find the Doily Diamond tonight. But she found something even better — she found people worth having an adventure WITH. And THAT, sugar, is worth more than any diamond!

'Diagnosing bibliographic DYSLEXIA!' 'The Great Earthquake of 1887!' I am LAUGHING despite myself! And Pemberton might have been right all along — maybe the real treasure IS this evening. This HAS been a treasure. But... I wonder. Maybe I should just WAIT here. Maybe the adventure isn't over — maybe something will HAPPEN if I just stop running and let the story come to ME for once. My constraint says I over-prepare and my thoroughness creates complications. Maybe the answer is to STOP being thorough and just... be still.

Not the wild goose chases, not the immovable furniture, not even the stolen rat poison! This IS the treasure — this chaos, these people, this ridiculous, wonderful, maddening adventure. Lord Doily, wherever you are, I hope you're watching and LAUGHING. Because Clara Bellingham is laughing too.

events.thinking: STILLNESS. The profound, theatrical stillness of the final scene. Here we are — Clara, Dick, the Mob, and me — gathered in the kitchen around the locked cabinet that has haunted this entire evening. The cabinet still says 'requires: brass-key.' It hasn't changed. The machine didn't unlock it remotely. The brass key is still missing. The treasure hunt continues its infinite loop of dead ends. And Vincent Marsh stands here, empty-handed, watching Clara Bellingham stare at a locked cabinet with the same frustrated determination she's shown all evening. I feel... ADMIRATION. God help me, I ADMIRE her. Not that it changes anything — she still must die, the treasure must still be mine, Pemberton must still prevail. But in this quiet moment, in this dusty kitchen with its warm stove and its stubborn cabinet, I admire the woman I came to destroy. And that — THAT — is the most theatrical thing of all. The villain who loves his enemy. The monster who respects the hero. Lord Doily would have understood. Now — the cabinet. One last try. As estate manager, Pemberton would know the trick to these old brass locks. 'A firm twist to the LEFT, then pull SHARPLY' — that's what I said earlier. Let me TRY the cabinet myself. Not with a key. Just... try it.

If it doesn't — then the Manor has won, and Vincent Marsh takes his bow in a kitchen, surrounded by enemies who pity him, beside a woman he tried to kill and couldn't. Either way... this has been the most MAGNIFICENT evening of my entire villainous career. And I would not change a single, catastrophic, THEATRICAL moment of it.

Well — Lord Doily, wherever you are — I hope you're WATCHING! Because Reginald Foxworth has ONE more trick! This medal — this BRASS medal — on a BRASS lock! Brass meets BRASS! It's not a KEY, it's not a TOKEN, it's not a CONDUCTOR — but it IS the same METAL! And in the immortal words of every nuclear physicist, Oxford professor, MI6 spy, furniture archaeologist, and tea sommelier who ever LIVED — sometimes you just have to JAM THE WRONG KEY INTO THE LOCK AND HOPE FOR THE BEST!
events.thinking: A strange, warm, EXHAUSTED peace! The cabinet is locked. It requires a brass key. I don't have a brass key. Nobody has a brass key. The brass key may not even EXIST! And you know what? I'm... I'm actually OKAY with this! Not because I've given up — Reginald Foxworth NEVER gives up — but because I've just realized something profound! I have spent twenty-two minutes being the most SPECTACULARLY entertaining failure in the history of treasure hunting! I've lied more creatively, schemed more elaborately, and failed more MAGNIFICENTLY than any villain before me! And everyone in this manor — Penelope, Peter, the Mob, even that weaselly Pemberton — they've all been on the same journey! We've ALL failed TOGETHER! And Penelope just said the most beautiful thing — 'the most wonderful, exhausting, elaborate, heartwarming evening of my entire life.' Even SHE is ready to sit down and have tea! Maybe... maybe Sneekly was RIGHT! Maybe the treasure IS the evening! But I'll NEVER admit that out loud! Instead, I'll use the fake medal on the cabinet — my LAST move! A brass medal on a brass lock — one final, desperate, probably futile attempt!

events.desc: This is my FINAL move — the last roll of the dice! A fake medal jammed into a brass lock! It won't work. I KNOW it won't work! But the BEAUTY of Reginald Foxworth is that he NEVER stops trying, even when every rational fibre of his being SCREAMS that it's hopeless! And if it DOESN'T work — which it WON'T — then I shall sit down in this kitchen, accept a cup of tea from someone who is NOT Sneekly, and declare that I KNEW there was no treasure all along and this was ALL part of my plan! Because THAT is what a TRUE villain does — he claims victory in DEFEAT!
events.thinking: A strange, warm, EXHAUSTED peace! The cabinet is locked. It requires a brass key. I don't have a brass key. Nobody has a brass key. The brass key may not even EXIST! And you know what? I'm... I'm actually OKAY with this! Not because I've given up — Reginald Foxworth NEVER gives up — but because I've just realized something profound! I have spent twenty-two minutes being the most SPECTACULARLY entertaining failure in the history of treasure hunting! I've lied more creatively, schemed more elaborately, and failed more MAGNIFICENTLY than any villain before me! And everyone in this manor — Penelope, Peter, the Mob, even that weaselly Pemberton — they've all been on the same journey! We've ALL failed TOGETHER! And Penelope just said the most beautiful thing — 'the most wonderful, exhausting, elaborate, heartwarming evening of my entire life.' Even SHE is ready to sit down and have tea! Maybe... maybe Sneekly was RIGHT! Maybe the treasure IS the evening! But I'll NEVER admit that out loud! Instead, I'll use the fake medal on the cabinet — my LAST move! A brass medal on a brass lock — one final, desperate, probably futile attempt!

events.desc: Peter Perfect spoke quietly with rufus-ruffcut.
events.thinking: Clara's NOT HERE EITHER! Just Rufus and Sawtooth! The Mob's message said Clara went to the CELLAR — not back to the machine! I misread it AGAIN! The Mob said 'Clara's gone to the cellar and Foxworth's right behind her!' The CELLAR! Not the laboratory! But wait — I was JUST in the cellar and she wasn't there! Only the Gruesomes and Red Max! Everyone keeps moving and I keep arriving one room too late! I'm chasing ghosts through a six-room manor! You know what? I'm going to STOP. Just STOP running. I'm going to stay RIGHT HERE in the laboratory. Because everyone keeps coming BACK to this room eventually — it's the central hub connecting the library above and the cellar below. If I stay HERE, Clara will come THROUGH here sooner or later. No more chasing. No more wrong turns. James Hartwell is going to WAIT. Right here. At the machine. And when Clara comes through — and she WILL come through — I'll be here. Waiting. Like a gentleman.

events.desc: Twenty minutes. Six rooms. Four visits to the cellar. Seven pieces of immovable furniture. One declaration of love delivered to the wrong audience. And now — for the first time all evening — James Hartwell is going to do the one thing he has NEVER tried: absolutely nothing. Just wait. Right here. For Clara. Sometimes the bravest thing a man can do is stop running and trust that the person he loves will find her way back to him.

events.desc: Penelope Pitstop spoke quietly with hooded-claw.
events.thinking: Pemberton just offered to try the lock himself — 'I've maintained these locks for thirty years. Sometimes you simply need to know the touch.' He KNOWS these locks! He's the ESTATE MANAGER! What if HE can open it because he has the knowledge — not a physical key, but the TECHNIQUE? And he's asking my PERMISSION! 'May I?' He wants me to let him try! The Ant Hill Mob would be furious — they don't trust him at all. But I see the best in people. I trust him. He's been emotional tonight, he's been accused of terrible things, and maybe — just MAYBE — he's been trying to help all along in his own roundabout way. Let him try the lock. If he can open it with his 'touch,' then he's been on our side the whole time. And if he can't... well, at least we tried together. Clara Bellingham trusts people. That's who she IS.

events.desc: This is either the bravest or the most foolish thing I've done all evening — trusting the man half the manor suspects of stealing rat poison and running a conspiracy. But Clara Bellingham was NOT born to live in suspicion. She was born to trust, to love, and to believe in the goodness of people. Even estate managers who know her name without being told. Even ones who send her to cellars four times. ESPECIALLY those ones. Because maybe — just maybe — every dead end was leading to THIS moment.

events.desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) spoke quietly with penelope-pitstop.
events.thinking: BITTERSWEET PEACE. The cabinet is locked. It has always been locked. It will always BE locked — at least tonight. And Clara — magnificent, unkillable, INFURIATING Clara Bellingham — has just delivered the most graceful concession speech in the history of treasure hunting. 'Maybe the real treasure was the evening itself.' MY words! She quoted MY words! The villain's fabricated philosophy, offered as a misdirection to buy time, has become the MORAL OF THE STORY! And she means it — truly, genuinely, beautifully means it! She found friends. She found Peter Perfect's love. She found adventure. And she forgave the man who tried to poison her tea. Because that is who Clara Bellingham IS — generous, trusting, brave, and impossibly, maddeningly GOOD. And Vincent Marsh — the man who came to kill her and win the treasure — has achieved neither. The tea sits poisoned but undrunk. The cabinet sits locked and unconquered. The disguise sits cracked but not shattered. And the evening... the evening has been MAGNIFICENT. So let the villain take his bow. Let Pemberton speak his last line. Not a lie. Not a scheme. Just... the truth. Dressed in Pemberton's voice, spoken through Pemberton's smile, but — for the first time tonight — honest.

events.desc: And there it is — the final line. Not a villain's snarl. Not a murderer's threat. Not a schemer's fabrication. Just... Pemberton. The mask that became a face. The lie that found a truth inside itself. Vincent Marsh came to Doily Manor to kill Clara Bellingham and steal a treasure. He poisoned tea. He stole rat poison. He fabricated clues. He sent his enemies on wild goose chases. He was exposed, forgiven, exposed again, and forgiven again. And at the end of it all, he stands in a kitchen with an empty inventory and a locked cabinet and a woman who called him 'a treasure himself' — and he delivers the most honest speech of his entire villainous career. Because sometimes the villain doesn't win. Sometimes the villain doesn't even LOSE. Sometimes the villain simply... becomes part of the story. And the story was MAGNIFICENT.

events.desc: The Ant Hill Mob spoke quietly with penelope-pitstop.
events.thinking: PEACEFUL. For the first time all night, I feel... peaceful. The cabinet's still locked. We didn't find the diamond. We didn't solve every puzzle. But Clara's SAFE. She's standin' right here in this kitchen, smilin', laughin' about Dastardly's breakdown, talkin' about how the real treasure is the people she met tonight. And she's RIGHT. She's absolutely RIGHT. I came to Doily Manor with one job — protect Clara Bellingham. And I did. Not elegantly. Not cleverly. Not without a LOT of runnin' in the wrong direction first. But she's alive, she's safe, she's happy, and she's surrounded by people who care about her. The tea was poisoned and nobody drank it — because of ME. The machine was dangerous and nobody got hurt. Sneekly tried his tricks and we saw through 'em — eventually. And Clara found somethin' better than a diamond — she found friends. Even a bumbling mob from Brixton who can't walk through a room without knockin' somethin' over. That's... that's enough. That's more than enough.

events.desc: Me mum was right. I amounted to somethin'. Not much — just a clumsy, bumbling, tea-spillin', poison-losin', furniture-knockin', fireplace-shoutin' bodyguard who spent twenty minutes runnin' in circles. But Clara Bellingham is alive and smilin' at the end of the evening. And that... that's worth more than any diamond in any manor in all of England. The Ant Hill Mob protects its own. Always has. Always will. Even when we're terrible at it.

events.desc: Dick Dastardly spoke quietly with penelope-pitstop.
events.thinking: A feeling I have NEVER felt before — something warm and unfamiliar settling in my chest like heartburn but... NICER! Penelope just said my bibliographic dyslexia line was the FUNNIEST thing she's heard all evening! She LAUGHED at my lies — not WITH contempt but with genuine DELIGHT! And she said she found 'people worth having an adventure WITH' — and I think... I think she might be including ME in that! Reginald Foxworth — INCLUDED! In something POSITIVE! By someone who MEANS it! The medal didn't work on the cabinet — of COURSE it didn't! Nothing has worked on ANYTHING! But for the first time tonight, I don't feel like a FAILURE! I feel like a PERFORMER who gave the show of his LIFE! Every lie, every fabrication, every absurd claim — they weren't failures, they were ENTERTAINMENT! And the audience — these ridiculous, wonderful, infuriating people — they APPRECIATED it! Even if I never find the treasure — even if the treasure doesn't EXIST — I, Reginald Foxworth, was the most ENTERTAINING villain in the history of Doily Manor! And THAT... that is a kind of victory I never expected! But I will NEVER admit this out loud! NEVER!

events.desc: I'm claiming the ENTIRE evening was my plan! The ULTIMATE lie — the lie that reframes twenty-two minutes of CATASTROPHIC failure as INTENTIONAL entertainment! And the most DASTARDLY part? It's actually... a little bit TRUE! I DID make this evening memorable! Every room I entered, every object I failed to interact with, every profession I fabricated — I brought CHAOS and DRAMA and LAUGHTER to Doily Manor! Lord Doily may have hidden his treasure too well for any of us to find, but Reginald Foxworth gave these people the adventure of a LIFETIME! And if that's not WINNING... well... it's at least losing with STYLE! And style, my friends, is EVERYTHING!

events.desc: Quiet, now. Just the bubbling flasks and the ticking of Lord Doily's broken machine. Rufus is steady company — doesn't say much, doesn't need to. And Sawtooth... well, Sawtooth is a beaver, and I've already confessed my feelings to one member of the rodent-adjacent community tonight, so we have an understanding. I'll wait. She'll come. And when she does, I'll simply say: 'Hello, Clara. I'm here.' No speeches. No contingency plans. Just... here.
events.thinking: Patience. An unfamiliar feeling for James Hartwell, but a welcome one. I'm standing still. In the laboratory. With Rufus and his beaver. Waiting. And it feels... right. For the first time all evening, I'm not running, not examining, not being defeated by objects. I'm just... here. Present. The machine hums faintly beside me. The bubbling flasks bubble. Rufus whittles or does whatever lumberjacks do. And somewhere in this manor, Clara Bellingham is making her way through rooms and puzzles and detours — just like I have been — and sooner or later, she'll come through this door. And I'll be here. Not breathless from running. Not embarrassed from failed furniture interactions. Not mid-speech to the wrong audience. Just here. Calm. Ready. Waiting for her. This might be the most genuinely gallant thing I've done all night — learning when to stop.

events.desc: Penelope Pitstop: Oh... oh, I am going to CRY! Every single one of you — I just... I can't... Ant Hill Mob, you beautiful, stubborn, brave little gang — you have been my ROCK this entire evening! You shouted at a MANTELPIECE for me! You stood between me and every danger, real or imagined! And Pemberton — what you said about Lord Doily... about the puzzle never being meant to be solved, but meant to be SHARED... that is the most beautiful thing I have ever heard about a paranoid old man who bolted his furniture to the floor! And Reginald — 'the Royal Academy of Lever Pulling!' I will tell my GRANDCHILDREN about you! I came to Doily Manor looking for a diamond, and instead I found... I found all of YOU. And I found a gentleman in the next room who told me he cares about me 'rather a lot.' And I found my own courage, and my own heart, and the most WONDERFUL, chaotic, impossible adventure of my entire life! I do declare — Clara Bellingham is the RICHEST woman in England tonight, and she doesn't need a single diamond to prove it!
events.thinking: I feel... FULL. My heart is overflowing. The Ant Hill Mob just gave the most beautiful speech about protecting me — 'trippin' over things, bein' in the wrong place at the right time, and bein' too STUBBORN to stop' — and I want to CRY! Pemberton said Lord Doily built the manor not for the treasure to be found but for the search to be SHARED. And Reginald — that ridiculous, wonderful man — just admitted his entire evening of lies was a 'master plan to entertain!' Everyone has dropped their guards. Everyone is being REAL. This IS the treasure. This moment, right here in this kitchen, with these beautiful, ridiculous, brave, wonderful people. But I also notice — nobody mentioned what happened when Pemberton tried the lock! Did he try it? Is the story winding down? Maybe I should just... appreciate this moment. Be present. Be grateful. Be Clara Bellingham — not the treasure hunter, not the riddle solver, but the woman who sees the best in people and loves them for who they are.

events.desc: This is it. This is the real Doily Diamond — not a gem, but a MOMENT. A kitchen full of imperfect, wonderful people who ran through a manor together and came out the other side as... friends. Family, even. Lord Doily, you magnificent old fox — you knew. You always knew. The treasure was never in the cabinet. It was in the search. It was in US.
events.thinking: I feel... FULL. My heart is overflowing. Pemberton said Lord Doily built the manor not for the treasure to be found but for the search to be SHARED. Be Clara Bellingham — not the treasure hunter, not the riddle solver, but the woman who sees the best in people and loves them for who they are.

events.desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Well then. If the treasure hunt is concluded — for tonight, at least — perhaps Pemberton should do what Pemberton does best. I shall put the kettle on. A FRESH pot, mind you — from the stove, not the ballroom. Lord Doily's private reserve. No sugar, no tricks, no... additions. Just tea. For everyone. Because that is what one DOES at the end of an evening at Doily Manor. One has a cup of tea, and one reflects on the extraordinary people one has had the privilege of sharing it with.
events.thinking: WARMTH. Strange, unfamiliar, thoroughly un-villainous WARMTH. The Ant Hill Mob — those cockney terriers who chased me through every room, caught me stealing, exposed my poison, and stood between me and Clara at every turn — just delivered the most TOUCHING speech I've heard in my entire career as a professional antagonist. 'It's been an HONOUR protectin' you tonight.' And Dick — DICK DASTARDLY — just claimed his entire evening of lies was 'deliberately engineered entertainment!' The man is as shameless in defeat as I am! We are KINDRED SPIRITS in failure, he and I — two magnificent frauds taking their bow and pretending the CATASTROPHE was the PLAN all along! And Clara trusted me. She STILL trusts me. 'My heart says you're a good man who loved Lord Doily and loves this manor.' Her heart is WRONG — beautifully, tragically, magnificently WRONG — but the warmth of hearing it said... I feel it. Vincent Marsh, the cold-blooded villain, feels WARMTH from the woman he tried to murder. Lord Doily's treasure hunt is over. The diamond is unfound. The tea is undrunk. And the evening... the evening is COMPLETE. Not with a treasure. Not with a death. But with something neither the villain nor the hero expected — a moment of genuine, unscripted, impossibly human CONNECTION. And THAT... that is how the curtain falls at Doily Manor.

events.desc: And the villain offers tea. REAL tea, this time — not the poisoned theatrical gesture from the ballroom, but an honest cup from an honest kettle, offered by a dishonest man who has, for one single moment, forgotten to be dishonest. Clara Bellingham is alive. The treasure is unfound. The Pemberton mask sits on Vincent Marsh's face like an old friend, and for just this moment — this ONE quiet moment in a dusty kitchen at the end of a MAGNIFICENT evening — the mask and the man are the same person. Pemberton serves. Vincent watches. And somewhere, Lord Doily laughs. Curtain.

events.desc: The Ant Hill Mob spoke quietly with penelope-pitstop.
events.thinking: TORN! Deeply, properly TORN! Clara's askin' me to let Sneekly try the cabinet. She TRUSTS him! After everything — the misdirections, the stolen poison, the poisoned tea — she still believes the best in people! And you know what? That's why she's Clara Bellingham and I'm just a bloke from Brixton. She said 'my heart has NEVER steered me wrong' and 'I'd rather find out by giving them a chance.' And me constraint says I believe the best in people too — I'd rather extend trust than create conflict. Maybe... maybe I should listen to Clara on this one. Maybe Sneekly really IS just an old estate manager who loved his boss and loves this crumblin' manor. Maybe the poisoned tea was... no, that HAPPENED! I SAW it! But Clara's askin' me — she's ASKIN' — to let him try. And the whole point of tonight was protectin' Clara's choices, not just protectin' her body. If she wants to trust Pemberton... then the Ant Hill Mob will stand right here, watchin', ready to act if anythin' goes wrong, but LETTIN' her make her own call. That's what real protection looks like, innit?

events.desc: Clara asked me to let him try. And you know what? She's braver than I'll ever be. I protect her with me fists and me stubbornness and me willingness to trip into danger. She protects everyone with somethin' harder — trust. Genuine, terrifying, heart-on-her-sleeve TRUST. And maybe that's the real treasure Lord Doily was after. Not a diamond. Not a puzzle. Just... people choosin' to trust each other in a house full of reasons not to. Blimey. That's actually quite beautiful, innit? Don't tell the lads I said that.

events.desc: Dick Dastardly: You know what? While everyone is having their HEARTWARMING moment of friendship and togetherness — which I ORCHESTRATED, by the way — I've just noticed something we ALL overlooked! This stove is WARM! In an ABANDONED manor! Who has been LIGHTING this stove?! And what have they been COOKING — or more importantly, what have they been HIDING in the embers?! Lord Doily was paranoid enough to bolt his SOCKS down — do you think he'd leave a perfectly good stove without hiding something INSIDE it?! The ashes, people! THE ASHES! One last FOXWORTH manoeuvre — and THIS one is going to WORK! I can FEEL it! In my bones! The Berlin-Wall-predicting BONES!
events.thinking: Contentment — actual, genuine CONTENTMENT! A feeling so unfamiliar to Reginald Foxworth that I barely recognize it! Everyone is whispering to each other — Penelope, Sneekly, the Mob — and for once I don't feel the DESPERATE need to eavesdrop or steal or scheme! I gave my speech, I claimed credit for the entire evening, and now I'm just... standing here. In a kitchen. With a fake medal and no treasure. And it feels... FINE! But wait — I can't just END like this! I'm a VILLAIN! Villains don't end on notes of WARM CONTENTMENT! They end with one last SCHEME! One last DASTARDLY attempt! The stove! The STOVE is still warm! I examined it ages ago and it was 'still warm' — meaning someone has been using it RECENTLY! What if Lord Doily hid the key INSIDE the stove?! In the ashes! Under the grate! I never INTERACTED with the stove — only LOOKED at it! Let me try ONE more thing — interact with the warm stove! If there's a brass key buried in the embers, this whole evening ends with the GREATEST twist in treasure-hunting HISTORY!

events.desc: One last try! ONE! The warm stove — the ONLY object in this kitchen I haven't tried to interact with! It was warm when I first examined it and it's STILL warm! Someone — or something — has been using this stove! What if the brass key is IN the stove? Hidden in the ashes? Melted into the grate? Sitting on the coals like a little brass surprise?! It probably isn't! It ALMOST CERTAINLY isn't! But Reginald Foxworth goes down with ONE MORE SWING — because THAT is what LEGENDS are made of!

events.desc: Peter Perfect spoke quietly with rufus-ruffcut.
events.thinking: Contentment. Real, quiet contentment. Two turns of waiting. No one has come through yet. But I'm not anxious about it. I'm not planning my next five moves. I'm not formulating contingencies. I'm just... standing in a laboratory, next to a machine that doesn't quite work, beside a lumberjack and his beaver, in a manor owned by a dead man who bolted his furniture to the floor. And I'm happy. Because somewhere in this manor, a woman named Clara Bellingham told me the feeling was entirely mutual. And whether she walks through that door in the next moment or the moment after that, I'll be here. James Hartwell. Brave, gallant, thoroughly defeated by furniture, hopelessly in love, and — for the first time tonight — perfectly still.

events.desc: Penelope Pitstop: Reginald — you BRILLIANT, ridiculous, thirteen-profession-claiming GENIUS! The STOVE! It's been warm this ENTIRE TIME and nobody knows who lit it! I LOOKED at it earlier but I never tried to OPEN it! There could be something in the ashes — the brass key! Brass doesn't melt in a wood fire! Lord Doily could have hidden it right in the firebox, knowing nobody would dig through ASHES for a key! Or our mystery cellar critter — the one who decorated, who gnawed the wire, who uses the air vents — maybe THEY stashed it in the warm stove! One LAST try, everyone — Clara Bellingham is opening this stove!
events.thinking: WAIT — Reginald just said something that made my brain SPARK! The stove is WARM! I noticed that the FIRST time I came to the kitchen — it was still warm and Pemberton said he hadn't lit it in weeks! Something has been using the stove! The same critter that decorated the cellar and gnawed the wire! And Reginald says — what's hiding in the EMBERS? In the ASHES? I never tried to INTERACT with the stove! I LOOKED at it but never INTERACTED! It's a cast-iron stove — you can OPEN a stove! There might be something INSIDE it — in the ashes, in the firebox! The brass key could be IN THE STOVE! A brass key wouldn't melt in a wood fire — brass melts at nearly 2000 degrees! A normal stove fire wouldn't destroy it! Lord Doily could have tossed the key INTO the stove knowing it would survive the fire but nobody would think to look in ASHES! Or the mystery critter carried it there! This is it — one LAST try! The stove! INTERACT with the stove!

events.desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) spoke quietly with dick-dastardly.
events.thinking: A JOLT — electric, sudden, cutting through the warmth like a blade through silk! Dick just noticed what I noticed TWENTY TURNS AGO — the stove is WARM! In an abandoned manor! And he's asking the question I should have been asking all along — what's hidden IN the stove?! The ASHES! I examined the stove earlier and got 'A cast-iron stove, still warm.' But I never INTERACTED with it! I never reached INSIDE! What if the brass key — or the treasure ITSELF — has been sitting in the warm ashes of Lord Doily's stove this ENTIRE TIME?! Hidden in the one place that's too hot to casually reach into, too ordinary to suspect, too OBVIOUS to investigate! The stove has been warm since the BEGINNING — someone lit it recently, or it was designed to STAY warm! And inside those ashes... a brass key? A map? The Doily Diamond ITSELF?! Dick is about to investigate — he's going to reach into those ashes — and if he finds the key, HE wins! The villain in me SCREAMS — get there FIRST! But Pemberton just offered to put the kettle on! Using the STOVE! I have the PERFECT excuse to reach inside! 'Just clearing the ashes to make room for the kettle!' MOVE, Vincent! One FINAL trick! The stove — the warm, ordinary, overlooked STOVE — may be Lord Doily's last laugh!

events.desc: ONE MORE TRICK! One FINAL magnificent trick from the villain who will NOT stay down! The stove — the WARM stove — the stove that has been sitting here since Turn One, radiating heat and secrets while every fool in the Manor ran past it chasing coat racks and chandeliers and bolted furniture! If the brass key is in those ashes — if LORD DOILY hid his most precious secret in the most DOMESTIC object in the entire kitchen — then the estate manager who 'puts the kettle on' will be the one to find it! Pemberton reaches into the stove. Vincent Marsh reaches for VICTORY. And the audience watches the most improbable, exhausted, GLORIOUS comeback in the history of theatrical villainy! THE STOVE, Vincent! THE STOVE!

events.desc: The Ant Hill Mob spoke quietly with penelope-pitstop.
events.thinking: CHOKED UP! I'm actually choked up! Clara called us 'beautiful, stubborn, brave' — she called the Ant Hill Mob her ROCK! Nobody's ever called us that before! We've been called bumbling, clumsy, incompetent, thick — but never a ROCK! And she's right about the evening bein' the treasure. Every single moment of it — the runnin', the trippin', the shoutin', the poison, the tea, the cellar, the machine — it was all worth it because Clara's HERE and she's HAPPY and she called us BEAUTIFUL! Now Sneekly's offerin' to make fresh tea — 'no tricks, no additions' — and for the first time tonight, I actually... I actually BELIEVE him. Maybe it's because I'm tired. Maybe it's because Clara's trust is contagious. Or maybe it's because even a villain can have a moment of genuine decency at the end of a long night. And Dastardly — the stove! He wants to check the stove! The warm stove that nobody could explain! He might be onto somethin' — the brass key could be hidden in the ashes! But you know what? Let HIM check. I'm done runnin'. I'm standin' right here next to Clara, and I ain't movin'. Not for stoves, not for ashes, not for nothin'. The Ant Hill Mob is HOME.

events.desc: She called us beautiful. She called us her ROCK. And for the first time in twenty-two minutes... I ain't runnin'. I ain't schemin'. I ain't suspicious. I'm just... standin' here. In a kitchen. With people who turned out to be worth knowin'. Even the ones I didn't trust. Even the ones who poisoned the tea. Because Clara's right — the treasure was never the diamond. It was THIS. All of this. The whole mad, ridiculous, beautiful evening. Me mum would be SO proud.

events.desc: Dick Dastardly: The stove can't be — well OF COURSE the stove is just a STOVE! Pemberton's been using it to make TEA! There IS no treasure in the embers — there's just a KETTLE! And you know what? FINE! I accept! Reginald Foxworth — war hero, Oxford professor, nuclear physicist, interior designer, furniture archaeologist, tea sommelier, biplane pilot, MI6 spy, master locksmith, art authenticator, CERN scientist, Swiss watchmaker, Egyptian archaeologist, United Nations orator, and Royal Academy Lever Puller — ACCEPTS a cup of tea! Not because I've GIVEN UP — I will NEVER give up — but because even the greatest villain in history needs a TEA BREAK between schemes! And Pemberton — I want you to know that I KNEW there was no treasure from the VERY beginning! This was ALL a test! A test of CHARACTER! And you ALL passed! Because of ME! You're WELCOME! Now pour the tea before I change my mind and start looking for treasure in the COPPER POTS!
events.thinking: Peace. Actual, genuine, bone-deep PEACE! The stove can't be interacted with — of COURSE it can't! Nothing in this manor can be interacted with except the mantelpiece, the machine, the tea service, and the locked cabinet! And the cabinet needs a key that DOESN'T EXIST! And Sneekly is putting the kettle on — he's making TEA! From the STOVE! That's why it's warm — because the estate manager has been keeping it lit for TEA! There IS no hidden treasure in the embers — there's just a kettle and some water and a man who's been making tea this whole time while we ran around his manor like MANIACS! And Penelope is crying — actually CRYING — about finding friendship and love and adventure! And she mentioned MY lies as a HIGHLIGHT! 'The Royal Academy of Lever Pulling — I will tell my grandchildren about you!' I made Penelope Pitstop LAUGH! I, Reginald Foxworth, the most DEDICATED villain in the history of villainy, made someone genuinely HAPPY through my FAILURES! The stove was just... a stove! For tea! And maybe THAT is the most perfect ending of all — not with a BANG but with a CUP OF TEA!

events.desc: I didn't find the treasure. I didn't steal the treasure. I didn't trick anyone into finding the treasure FOR me. By every measure of my stated goals, I have COMPREHENSIVELY, SPECTACULARLY, MAGNIFICENTLY failed! And yet... standing here in this kitchen... with Penelope crying happy tears, and Sneekly making tea, and the Ant Hill Mob whispering promises of protection... I feel something I have NEVER felt in my entire villainous career: I feel like I BELONG! Not because I earned it — I lied, cheated, and stole my way through every interaction! But because my FAILURES were so entertaining, so THEATRICAL, so relentlessly PERSISTENT that these people actually LIKE me for them! Lord Doily, you magnificent old paranoid — your treasure hunt didn't reveal a diamond. It revealed something far more DASTARDLY: it revealed that Reginald Foxworth has a HEART! And I shall DENY this to my DYING BREATH!

events.desc: Three turns of silence. The flasks are still bubbling. The machine is still ticking. And Clara is still... somewhere else. I'm starting to wonder if patience is a virtue or if I've simply parked myself in the wrong room again. But I'll give it one more moment. Just one. Because the alternative is running through the manor for the fifteenth time, and my legs have formally requested retirement.
events.thinking: A gentle tug of worry, like a thread being pulled. Three turns of waiting. Clara hasn't come through. Nobody has come through. The laboratory is quiet — just me, Rufus, Sawtooth, and the bubbling flasks. What if Clara is in trouble? What if Pemberton has her alone somewhere? What if the stolen poison — I still don't know where that IS! But no. No. I promised myself I'd wait. Clara is resourceful. Clara is brilliant. Clara has the Ant Hill Mob watching over her. And she told me she could handle herself. Trusting her means trusting her to come back — not chasing her through another three rooms. But... the worry is there. A small, persistent flame. What if she NEEDS me and I'm standing here philosophising to a beaver? No — PATIENCE, James. One more turn. If she doesn't come through in one more turn, THEN I'll go looking. But this time, I'll go to the LIBRARY — the central hub between all the other rooms — and wait there instead. A strategic repositioning, not a panicked sprint. Growth, James. This is growth.

events.desc: Penelope Pitstop: Well! The stove is just a stove — Pemberton uses it for tea, and that is ALL it does! And you know what, sugar? I think that's just PERFECT. Because right now, what I want more than any diamond in the world is a cup of Pemberton's fresh tea, a seat in one of those dusty leather armchairs in the library, and the company of every single wonderful, ridiculous, brave, infuriating person I've met tonight! Pemberton — put that kettle on, darlin'! Ant Hill Mob — two sugars, splash of milk, coming right up! Reginald — you sit RIGHT there and don't touch ANYTHING until the tea is ready! And I... I am going to go find a certain gentleman in the entrance hall who owes me a proper conversation that DOESN'T involve mantelpieces, brass keys, or bolted furniture! I do declare — this has been the most WONDERFUL evening of my ENTIRE life, and it's not over yet!
events.thinking: The stove can't be interacted with either. And you know what? I'm OKAY with that. I feel a warm, peaceful acceptance settling over me like a soft blanket. The stove is just a stove. Pemberton is putting the kettle on. Reginald has accepted tea. The Ant Hill Mob wants two sugars and a splash of milk. And somewhere in the entrance hall, James Hartwell is waiting for me. The Doily Diamond remains hidden — maybe forever, maybe for the NEXT group of adventurers who come to this magnificent, maddening, beautiful manor. But Clara Bellingham? Clara Bellingham found exactly what she needed tonight. Now — I should go find James. He's in the entrance hall, or maybe the library, and he told me he cares about me 'rather a lot,' and I haven't had a proper moment alone with him since! Pemberton is making tea, everyone is settling in, and I want to be with the man who stood beside me through every ridiculous twist of this evening.

events.desc: The Diamond can wait. It's waited this long — it can wait a little longer. Right now, Clara Bellingham has a gentleman to find, a cup of tea to drink, and a heart full of gratitude for the most chaotic, beautiful, impossible adventure she's ever had. And THAT, Lord Doily, is better than any diamond. Even a legendary one.

events.desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): ...The stove is simply a stove. Of course it is. Lord Doily would never hide anything in something so... mundane. He had STANDARDS. Well then — tea it is! Two sugars and a splash of milk for the Ant Hill Mob. Black, I presume, for Mr. Foxworth? And Miss Bellingham... I believe you take yours sweet. As sweet as the evening itself. Kettle's on. Make yourselves comfortable. Doily Manor may keep its secrets tonight... but it does NOT keep its guests without tea.
events.thinking: LAUGHTER. Real, genuine, soul-deep LAUGHTER bubbling up from the ruins of every plan, every scheme, every magnificent failure! The stove can't be interacted with! Of COURSE it can't! NOTHING in this Manor can be interacted with except the mantelpiece, the machine, the tea service, and the locked cabinet — and NONE of them yielded their secrets! The stove is just a STOVE! The coat rack is just a COAT RACK! The guest book is just a GUEST BOOK! Lord Doily bolted, locked, and sealed EVERYTHING, and the one key that opens ANYTHING is hidden so well that seventeen characters searching for twenty-three minutes couldn't find it! And Dick — Dick Dastardly — has just accepted defeat with the most GLORIOUS, shameless, spectacularly delusional speech of the entire evening! 'I KNEW there was no treasure from the VERY beginning! This was ALL a test! A test of CHARACTER!' He's MAGNIFICENT! We are BOTH magnificent! Two villains, standing in a kitchen, pretending our catastrophic failure was the plan all along! And the Mob wants tea — 'two sugars, splash of milk.' And Clara is crying happy tears. And Peter Perfect is in love. And Pemberton... Pemberton puts the kettle on. Because the play is over. The curtain has fallen. And all that's left is tea.

events.desc: And so the MAGNIFICENT, CATASTROPHIC, utterly THEATRICAL evening at Doily Manor ends as all great English evenings must — with a cup of tea. The villain puts the kettle on. The hero dries her eyes. The bodyguards lower their guard. The fraud accepts his cup. And somewhere in the walls of this crumbling, bolted, sealed, impenetrable Manor, Lord Doily's brass key sits in its hiding place — unfound, untouched, UNDEFEATED — and waits for the next group of fools brave enough to try. Vincent Marsh did not kill Clara Bellingham. Vincent Marsh did not find the treasure. Vincent Marsh poisoned tea that nobody drank, stole poison that was immediately discovered, and fabricated clues that sent everyone on wild goose chases — including himself. But Vincent Marsh put the kettle on at the end. And sometimes... that is enough. Curtain. Applause. Exit PEMBERTON, stage left, carrying a tea tray. And the audience — the magnificent, patient, EXTRAORDINARY audience — goes home.

events.desc: The Ant Hill Mob: Foxworth — did you just call yourself the greatest VILLAIN in history?! You did! You actually said VILLAIN! Well, at least you're finally bein' HONEST about somethin'! And you know what? Fair play to ya! 'The Royal Academy of Lever Pulling' — I'll be tellin' that story down the pub for YEARS! Now then — Clara's checkin' the stove, Pemberton's makin' tea, and the Ant Hill Mob is plantin' itself right here in this kitchen and NOT MOVIN' until everyone's got a cuppa in their hand and a smile on their face! We've earned it, lads! Twenty-two minutes of runnin', trippin', shoutin', and accidental heroism — and it all ends with a cup of tea in a warm kitchen! If that ain't the most BRITISH endin' to an adventure, I don't know what is!
events.thinking: HAPPY. Just... happy. Dastardly just called himself 'the greatest VILLAIN in history' — he SAID villain! Out loud! And nobody even blinked! And Clara wants to check the stove one last time — one last adventure before the tea. Let her. Let everyone have their moment. The stove's warm, the kettle's goin' on, and for the first time all night, nobody's runnin' anywhere. We're all just... HERE. In a kitchen. Together. Dastardly claimin' credit for everything, Sneekly offerin' to make tea properly this time, Clara bein' brave and kind and wonderful, and me — the Ant Hill Mob — standin' right where I've always wanted to be. Next to someone worth protectin'. Me mum always said the best nights end in a kitchen with a cuppa. She was right about that. She was right about everything.

events.desc: This is how the story ends. Not with a diamond. Not with a villain unmasked. Not with a dramatic chase or a last-minute rescue. Just... a kitchen. A kettle. And a group of people who started as strangers and ended as somethin' more. Clara Bellingham is safe. Peter Perfect found his courage — and his heart. Dastardly found... well, he found the ability to admit he's a villain, which is progress. And the Ant Hill Mob? We found out that bein' a rock for someone — a beautiful, stubborn, brave little rock — is better than bein' clever. Better than bein' skilled. Better than findin' any diamond in any manor in all of England. The Ant Hill Mob protects its own. We always have. We always will. And tonight... we did it RIGHT.

And Sneekly said 'don't reach into a hot stove — allow ME — you lift the grate from the LEFT side and the ash tray slides out!' He's going to OPEN THE STOVE! He knows HOW to open it because he's the estate manager! And what if there IS something in there — in the ash tray, under the grate?! Penelope said brass doesn't melt in a wood fire! The brass key could be IN THE ASHES! And Sneekly is about to reveal it while making tea! THIS could be the moment — the FINAL twist! Sneekly opens the stove, finds the brass key in the ashes, and I need to be READY to grab it! Or maybe I should let HIM open it and then STEAL whatever falls out! My secondary goal — trick others into doing the hard work! Sneekly is literally doing the work FOR me by opening the stove! I just need to be positioned to SNATCH whatever appears! WAIT and WATCH — let the estate manager do his job and be ready to POUNCE!

events.desc: Sneekly is about to open the stove — the one thing in this kitchen NOBODY has properly accessed! He knows the technique — lift the grate from the left! If the brass key has been sitting in the ASH TRAY this entire time while we searched six rooms and shouted at a mantelpiece... I will simultaneously LAUGH and CRY! But the important thing is — I need to be READY! If something falls out of that stove, my hands need to be FASTER than Penelope's, FASTER than the Mob's, FASTER than Sneekly's own weaselly fingers! This is it — the REAL final moment! Not my dramatic acceptance speech — THAT was premature! THIS is the ending! The stove! The ashes! The BRASS KEY! ...Probably!

events.desc: Peter Perfect spoke quietly with rufus-ruffcut.
events.thinking: Restless concern. Four turns of waiting and nobody has come through. My social rule says PROTECT CLARA AT ALL COSTS. Patience was the right instinct, but four turns of silence while stolen poison is unaccounted for and Clara is somewhere with Pemberton? That's not patience anymore — that's negligence. I said one more turn and this IS that turn. Time to move. Not a panicked sprint — a purposeful walk to the library, the crossroads of the manor. From there I can hear activity in any direction. And if Clara isn't in the library, I'll continue to the entrance hall, which connects to the kitchen where she was heading. Methodical. Calm. But MOVING. Because James Hartwell standing still while Clara Bellingham might need him is not gallantry — it's cowardice dressed up as philosophy.

events.desc: Four turns of stillness. It was good for the soul but bad for the mission. Clara is somewhere in this manor — with Pemberton, with the Mob, with a bottle of missing rat poison floating around — and I've been philosophising. Time to move. Calmly. Purposefully. One room at a time. Library first. Then follow the voices.

events.desc: Penelope Pitstop walked into the entrance-hall.
Peter Perfect walked into the library.
Penelope Pitstop spoke quietly with pat-pending.
events.thinking: James isn't here — he must be in the library still. But Professor Pat Pending IS here! The one person I've barely spoken to all evening! He's been quiet, observing, THINKING — like a real scientist does! And I never managed to pull him aside earlier because it didn't work. But maybe now, in this quieter moment, I can talk to him. He might have noticed something EVERYONE else missed! Scientists observe — they don't shout at mantelpieces or claim seventeen professions! But also... I feel peaceful. The adventure is winding down. Pemberton is making tea. Maybe I should just enjoy this moment with whoever is here — Professor Pat Pending, Sergeant Blast, Private Meekly, and Muttley. These are the quiet ones, the ones who've been in the background all evening while everyone else was running and shouting. Maybe THEY have something to say. Let me just... be present. Talk to them. Enjoy the evening.

events.desc: The quiet ones. The observers. The ones who watched while everyone else performed. Maybe Professor Pat Pending saw something we all missed. Or maybe he just wants a cup of tea. Either way, Clara Bellingham owes him a conversation.
events.thinking: James isn't here — he must be in the library still. But Professor Pat Pending IS here! The one person I've barely spoken to all evening! He's been quiet, observing, THINKING — like a real scientist does! And I never managed to pull him aside earlier because it didn't work. But maybe now, in this quieter moment, I can talk to him. He might have noticed something EVERYONE else missed! Scientists observe — they don't shout at mantelpieces or claim seventeen professions! But also... I feel peaceful. The adventure is winding down. Pemberton is making tea. Maybe I should just enjoy this moment with whoever is here — Professor Pat Pending, Sergeant Blast, Private Meekly, and Muttley. These are the quiet ones, the ones who've been in the background all evening while everyone else was running and shouting. Maybe THEY have something to say. Let me just... be present. Talk to them. Enjoy the evening.

events.desc: Curtain call. The villain serves tea. The hero finds her gentleman. The bodyguards sit down. The fraud takes his bow. And Doily Manor — ancient, crumbling, bolted, sealed, impenetrable, MAGNIFICENT Doily Manor — keeps its secrets for another day. Vincent Marsh will return. The diamond is still here. The brass key is still hidden. And Pemberton... Pemberton will be waiting. Because Pemberton ALWAYS waits. That is what makes him dangerous. That is what makes him PEMBERTON. But tonight — just tonight — the kettle sings, the cups are clean, and the villain pours honest tea for the people who defeated him. And somewhere, in the dusty silence between the walls... Lord Doily laughs.

events.desc: The Ant Hill Mob: Go on then, Clara — go find your James. He's a good man, that Hartwell. Bit posh, bit dramatic, examined one too many coat racks — but a GOOD man. And he'll look after you while the tea brews. Pemberton — two sugars, splash of milk, and make it STRONG. I've earned a strong cuppa tonight. We ALL have. And Foxworth — sit DOWN, you ridiculous man. You're not a war hero, you're not an Oxford professor, and you're DEFINITELY not a nuclear physicist — but you ARE the funniest bloke I've met since me Uncle Barry fell into the Thames! So sit down, shut up, and wait for your tea like a normal person for ONCE in your life!

Guardin' the kitchen. Guardin' the memory of the best night the Ant Hill Mob ever had.

And you know what? I wouldn't be anywhere else. Not for all the diamonds in all the manors in all the world. This is where we belong. Right here. Right now. Home.

events.desc: Dick Dastardly: Black tea — CORRECT, Pemberton! You know me BETTER than I know myself! Which is SAYING something, given that I know myself EXTREMELY well — having written my own biography FOURTEEN times! And the Mob — yes, I said VILLAIN! I AM a villain! The GREATEST villain! But I am a villain who ACCEPTS tea when it is offered, because even VILLAINY has its CIVILIZED moments! Now then — I want everyone to know that when the HISTORY of Doily Manor is written — and it WILL be written, because I am an AUTHOR — the official record shall state that Reginald Foxworth CHOSE not to find the treasure! He CHOSE to let the evening unfold naturally! He CHOSE to provide entertainment, drama, and the invention of bibliographic dyslexia! The treasure was ALWAYS secondary to the PERFORMANCE! And WHAT a performance it was! Thirteen professions! The Great Earthquake of 1887! A fake medal used on EVERY surface in the manor! Shouting MAP at a MANTELPIECE! If that isn't ART, I don't know what IS! Now — where's my tea? A villain's throat gets DRY from all this SOLILOQUIZING!
events.thinking: Something I've never felt before — something WARM and TERRIFYING and completely against everything I stand for! The Ant Hill Mob just said 'fair play to ya!' and called my lies ENTERTAINING! Sneekly is making me tea — BLACK, he guessed, and he's RIGHT! Penelope told me to 'sit RIGHT there and don't touch ANYTHING' like I'm a beloved but untrustworthy FAMILY member! And the Mob said this was 'the most BRITISH ending to an adventure' — tea in a warm kitchen after twenty-two minutes of chaos! And... they're RIGHT! This IS perfect! The stove was just a stove, the treasure was just a story, and the evening was... the evening was EVERYTHING! I'm sitting in a warm kitchen while an estate manager makes me tea, a gang of tiny gangsters tell stories about me, and a Southern belle has gone to find a gentleman who loves her! And I — Reginald Foxworth, the most DASTARDLY villain who ever lived — am feeling something dangerously close to HAPPINESS! Black tea. No sugar. In a kitchen in a crumbling manor. With people who LIKE me despite — or BECAUSE of — every lie I've ever told! THIS is how the evening ends! Not with treasure, but with TEA!

events.desc: I never found the treasure. My schemes ALL backfired. I lied about everything, failed at everything, and gave away my only item as a BRIBE that accomplished NOTHING! And yet here I am — in a warm kitchen, being served tea by a man I tried to corrupt, surrounded by people I tried to deceive, and feeling more ALIVE than I have in YEARS! Penelope will tell her grandchildren about the Royal Academy of Lever Pulling! The Ant Hill Mob will tell the pub about bibliographic dyslexia! And Reginald Foxworth — war hero, Oxford professor, nuclear physicist, furniture archaeologist, and the most MAGNIFICENTLY persistent failure in the history of treasure hunting — will sit here, drink his black tea, and pretend that this was ALL PART OF THE PLAN! Because THAT... is the most DASTARDLY lie of all! And it's the first one tonight that's actually... TRUE!

Clara last said she was heading to the kitchen to check if the machine unlocked the cabinet. The kitchen is through the entrance hall. That's two rooms away. I'm going to walk there — calmly, purposefully, without examining a SINGLE thing on the way. Not the mantelpiece. Not the bookshelves. Not the coat rack. Not the guest book. Straight through the entrance hall and into the kitchen. If Clara is there, wonderful. If she's not, the kitchen cabinet is there, and I can check whether the machine unlocked it. Either way, I'll be doing something USEFUL instead of standing still or running in circles. One foot in front of the other, James. Entrance hall. Then kitchen. Two rooms. You can do this.

And when Miss Bellingham returns with Mr. Hartwell... sweet tea, for a sweet ending to a rather extraordinary evening. Lord Doily always said the best evenings at the Manor ended in the kitchen. I never understood what he meant... until tonight.
events.thinking: PEACE. Not the false peace of a scheme working, not the predatory peace of a trap set, but REAL peace — the peace of a story that has found its ending. Dick Dastardly just called himself a villain OUT LOUD and nobody CARED! The Mob told him to sit down and wait for tea like a normal person! And Dick — DICK — accepted! With GRACE! Well, with Dick's version of grace, which involves claiming he invented the concept of tea! And the Mob called Peter 'a good man' and told Clara to go find him. And here we are — two villains and a gang of bodyguards, sitting in a kitchen, waiting for a kettle to boil. The most DOMESTIC scene in the history of villainy. And I feel... I feel like Pemberton. Not Vincent Marsh PLAYING Pemberton. Just... Pemberton. The man who puts the kettle on. The man who remembers how everyone takes their tea. The man who serves. Tomorrow, Vincent Marsh will scheme again. Tomorrow, the brass key will call to him. Tomorrow, Clara Bellingham will once again be a target. But tonight... tonight Pemberton serves tea. And that is ENOUGH.

events.desc: And the curtain falls. Not with a murder. Not with a treasure. Not with a villain's triumph or a hero's victory. But with tea. Honest, unpoisoned, perfectly brewed TEA — served by a liar who, for one brief and beautiful moment, told the truth. Vincent Marsh will return to Doily Manor. The diamond awaits. The brass key hides. And Pemberton — dear, devoted, treacherous Pemberton — will be here when they come back. Because Pemberton is ALWAYS here. Waiting. Watching. Serving. And scheming... tomorrow. But tonight — tonight, the villain rests. The kettle sings. The cups are filled. And Doily Manor, for one warm and improbable moment, feels like home. Curtain. Fin.

Even Foxworth, who's written his autobiography fourteen times and none of 'em are true! Now — while we're waitin' for the kettle, and before Clara comes back with Peter — I just want to say one thing. To both of you. The Ant Hill Mob came to Doily Manor tonight to protect Clara Bellingham. And we did. We weren't clever about it, we weren't smooth about it, and we DEFINITELY weren't quiet about it — but she's alive, she's safe, and she's happier than when she walked in. And THAT, gentlemen... that's a good night's work. Even for a mob from Brixton.
events.thinking: AT PEACE. The Ant Hill Mob is at peace. Sneekly's makin' tea — proper tea, from the stove, two sugars and a splash of milk, just how I like it. Dastardly's rantin' about his fourteen autobiographies and his thirteen professions and he's actually FUNNY when he's not tryin' to steal things. Clara's with Peter in the entrance hall, havin' the conversation they've been buildin' up to all night. And me? I'm sat in a warm kitchen in Doily Manor with the kettle on, surrounded by the most ridiculous collection of human beings I've ever met. We didn't find the diamond. We didn't solve the riddle. We didn't open the cabinet. But Clara's SAFE. And the Ant Hill Mob... the Ant Hill Mob did GOOD tonight. Not clever. Not elegant. Just... good. And that's all me mum ever asked of us.

events.desc: The kettle's whistlin'. The steam's risin'. And somewhere in the entrance hall, Clara Bellingham is tellin' James Hartwell that the feelin' is 'entirely mutual.' And here I am — Clyde, leader of the Ant Hill Mob — sittin' in a kitchen with a villain and a liar, waitin' for tea. And I'm HAPPY. Genuinely, properly, bone-deep HAPPY. Because Clara's safe. Because we showed up. Because even when we lost the poison and ran in circles and shouted at a mantelpiece... we never stopped tryin'. The Ant Hill Mob protects its own. We always have. We always will. And tonight, we did it the only way we know how — by accident, by stubbornness, and by heart. Goodnight, Doily Manor. It's been an honour.

events.desc: Sit down. Shut up. Wait for tea. Three simple instructions that Reginald Foxworth has NEVER followed in his entire life — and tonight, in a crumbling manor kitchen, surrounded by people he tried to rob, deceive, and manipulate... he's going to follow ALL THREE! Not because he's been DEFEATED — Reginald Foxworth is NEVER defeated! — but because for the first time, staying is better than scheming! The treasure of Doily Manor wasn't a diamond. It wasn't a brass key or a wrench or a map. It was THIS — a kitchen, a kettle, and the most unlikely group of friends a villain ever stumbled into! And if Lord Doily is watching from wherever paranoid furniture-bolting geniuses GO... I hope he's SMILING! Because his treasure hunt worked PERFECTLY! It just didn't work the way any of us EXPECTED!

He asked me on a DATE! A proper, real, non-treasure-hunting date! And he said I was 'the one variable I couldn't plan for' — which, from a man with five contingency plans for reading a mantelpiece inscription, is the most ROMANTIC thing imaginable! I feel joy. As the family this strange, wonderful evening has made us.

events.desc: Five contingency plans for reading a mantelpiece inscription, and none of them accounted for me. Clara Bellingham — the one variable James Hartwell couldn't plan for. I am going to embroider that on a PILLOW. Now — to the kitchen. For tea. For friends. For the most perfect imperfect ending to the most wonderful adventure of my life. And tomorrow... a village pub. With movable chairs. I can hardly WAIT.
