events.desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): A good night's work indeed. And Mr. Foxworth... for what it's worth... Lord Doily would have LOVED you. Both of you. All of you. He spent his final years in this Manor, alone, surrounded by puzzles no one would ever solve and tea no one would ever drink. He would have given ANYTHING for an evening like this — a hall full of liars and heroes and bodyguards and frauds, all running in circles, shouting at stone, and finding something far more valuable than diamonds. He would have laughed until he cried. And then he would have put the kettle on. Just as Pemberton does now.
events.thinking: GRATITUDE. The most dangerous emotion a villain can feel — and the most honest thing Vincent Marsh has experienced in years. The Mob just said 'she's alive, she's safe, and she's happier than when she walked in. And THAT is a good night's work.' And they're RIGHT. Clara IS alive. Because the Mob caught the poison. Because Peter stood beside her. Because even Dick Dastardly, in his own absurd way, provided enough chaos to keep the evening unpredictable. And because Pemberton — Vincent Marsh's greatest creation, his most elaborate disguise, his most THEATRICAL performance — turned out to be a better man than the villain who wore him. The mask became the face. The lie became the truth. And somewhere in the middle of poisoning tea and fabricating clues and accidentally giving away every secret he touched... Vincent Marsh became Pemberton. Just for tonight. Just for one cup of honest tea. And that... that is Lord Doily's real treasure. Not a diamond. Not a brass key. But the impossible, improbable, MAGNIFICENT transformation of a villain into a man who puts the kettle on. Dick has FEELINGS and he's not happy about being happy! The Mob called their evening 'a good night's work.' And Pemberton... Pemberton smiles. Not Vincent's smile. Pemberton's.

events.desc: And there it is. The villain's final line. Spoken not by Vincent Marsh, but by the man Vincent Marsh pretended to be — and, for one impossible evening, BECAME. Pemberton pours the tea. The Mob drinks. Dick Dastardly sits quietly for thirty seconds — a new personal record. And somewhere in the entrance hall, Clara Bellingham finds her gentleman, and the story of Doily Manor writes its own ending. Vincent Marsh will return. He ALWAYS returns. But when he does... he will remember this evening. This kitchen. This tea. These people. And the night the villain discovered that the most dangerous weapon in his arsenal... was kindness. Curtain. Applause. Exeunt omnes.

events.desc: Listen to us. A mob, a villain, and an estate manager who may or may not have tried to poison everyone — sittin' in a kitchen, drinkin' tea, and talkin' about FEELINGS. If me Uncle Barry could see me now, he'd laugh himself into the Thames AGAIN. But you know what? This is good. This is RIGHT. The tea's warm, the kitchen's quiet, and somewhere in the entrance hall, Clara Bellingham is safe and happy and loved. The Ant Hill Mob did its job tonight. We protected Clara. We stumbled into heroism. And now... now we're havin' a cuppa. Just like me mum always said — the best stories don't end with a bang. They end with a kettle.
events.thinking: WARM. Like the stove. Like the tea. Like the feelin' in me chest that I ain't felt since me mum made cocoa on a cold night in Brixton. Dastardly just said the manor gave him FEELINGS and he's 'not happy about being happy.' That's... that's the most honest thing that lyin' blighter has said all night! And Sneekly — he said Lord Doily always believed the best evenings ended in the kitchen, and he never understood it until tonight. Maybe... maybe Sneekly really DID poison the tea earlier. Maybe he IS the Hooded Claw. But maybe — just maybe — even villains can have a moment where the mask slips and the real person underneath surprises everyone. Even themselves. Clara would say, 'Give them a chance.' And tonight... I think I finally understand what she means.

events.desc: Dick Dastardly: A good night's work. Yes. Even I — and I do NOT say this lightly — even I must CONCEDE... that tonight was... that this evening... that all of you... were... ADEQUATE! There! I SAID it! You were all ADEQUATE! Which, from Reginald Foxworth, is the HIGHEST possible compliment! Higher than ADEQUATE has never been ACHIEVED in my presence! And Pemberton — that tea smells... ACCEPTABLE! Which is ALSO the highest compliment! And the Mob — protecting Clara through SIX rooms of chaos and one VERY suspicious ballroom — that was... COMPETENT work! EXTREMELY competent! And I want you both to know — and I will DENY having said this if anyone REPEATS it — that if I ever DO find Lord Doily's treasure... I might — MIGHT — consider sharing a SMALL percentage with the people in this kitchen! A VERY small percentage! Perhaps one percent! Of the LEAST valuable items! But the THOUGHT is there! And for Reginald Foxworth, the thought is... the thought is EVERYTHING!
events.thinking: Quiet. For the first time tonight — genuine, unforced QUIET! The Mob said their piece — they came to protect Clara, and they DID! Sneekly is pouring tea with the reverence of a man who's been waiting all evening for this moment! And I'm sitting here with a fake medal in my pocket and a warm feeling in my chest that I keep trying to lie about but CAN'T! The Mob called it 'a good night's work — even for a mob from Brixton.' And Sneekly said Lord Doily always said the best evenings ended in the kitchen. They were RIGHT! Both of them! And I — Reginald Foxworth — am going to do something I have NEVER done before. Something so SHOCKING, so UNPRECEDENTED, so completely OUT OF CHARACTER that it will haunt me for the rest of my DAYS. I am going to say something... GENUINE! One TRUE thing! In twenty-five minutes of LIES, I am going to tell ONE truth! And then I will IMMEDIATELY lie about having said it! Because THAT is the Foxworth way!

events.desc: I just called them ADEQUATE! For me, that's practically a DECLARATION OF LOVE! And the terrifying part is — I MEANT it! Every word! These ridiculous, wonderful, infuriating people have given me the most extraordinary evening of my life! A mob that protects instead of steals! An estate manager who makes tea instead of mischief! A Southern belle who finds friendship in a crumbling manor! And a villain — me, Reginald Foxworth — who discovered that the greatest scheme of all... is simply showing up and being MAGNIFICENTLY, PERSISTENTLY, ENTERTAININGLY yourself! Even when 'yourself' is a lying, cheating, thirteen-profession-claiming fraud with a fake medal and no treasure! Lord Doily... you MAGNIFICENT old man... your treasure hunt found the ONE thing that nobody expected: it found Reginald Foxworth's heart! And I shall NEVER forgive you for it! ...But I shall always be GRATEFUL!
events.thinking: Quiet. For the first time tonight — genuine, unforced QUIET! The Mob said their piece — they came to protect Clara, and they DID! Sneekly is pouring tea with the reverence of a man who's been waiting all evening for this moment! And I'm sitting here with a fake medal in my pocket and a warm feeling in my chest that I keep trying to lie about but CAN'T! The Mob called it 'a good night's work — even for a mob from Brixton.' And Sneekly said Lord Doily always said the best evenings ended in the kitchen. They were RIGHT! Both of them! And I — Reginald Foxworth — am going to do something I have NEVER done before. events.thinking: Joy. Simple, radiant, uncomplicated joy. The kind I've never felt before because I've always buried it under plans and contingencies and elaborate preparations. Clara Bellingham just told me she cares about me rather a lot. She said I'm infinitely more precious than a legendary diamond. She said every wrong turn led her back to ME. And she laughed — LAUGHED — about the beaver. Not at me. WITH me. And now she's asked if I'll take her somewhere without bolted furniture. And I said yes. A village pub. Tomorrow. Movable chairs and drinkable tea. No coat racks. This is happiness, James. This is what it feels like when you stop planning and just... arrive. At the right place. At the right time. With the right person. Now — tea in the kitchen with everyone. Together. The evening isn't over yet, but the treasure hunt is. Because we both found what we came for.

events.desc: She said yes to the pub. She LAUGHED about the beaver. She called me infinitely more precious than a diamond. And now we're walking to the kitchen together — side by side — for a cup of tea. No running. No detours. No examining anything on the way. Just two people who found each other in a ridiculous, magnificent, furniture-defeating, love-finding evening at Doily Manor. Lord Doily — wherever you are — thank you. For the bolted furniture, the gnawed wires, the impossible riddles, and the precariously hanging chandelier. Thank you for the evening itself. It was, as Pemberton said, the real treasure all along.

events.desc: Penelope Pitstop walked into the kitchen.
Peter Perfect walked into the kitchen.

Penelope Pitstop: Well, here we are! Back in the kitchen where this wing of the adventure began — with a warm stove, a locked cabinet, and the most extraordinary group of treasure hunters ever assembled under one roof! Pemberton, is that tea ready? Because I would like to propose a toast — with TEACUPS, mind you, not champagne — to the most wonderful evening of my ENTIRE life! To Pemberton, who kept Lord Doily's legacy alive with thirty years of devotion! To the Ant Hill Mob, the bravest bodyguards in all of Brixton — and possibly the world! To Reginald Foxworth, war hero, Oxford professor, nuclear physicist, tea sommelier, and the FUNNIEST man I have ever met! To Rufus and Sawtooth and the Slag brothers and the Gruesomes and Red Max and everyone else in this magnificent crumbling manor! And to James Hartwell — the most perfectly imperfect gentleman who ever confessed his feelings to a beaver! I do declare — the Doily Diamond may still be hidden somewhere in these walls, but TONIGHT, the real treasure is right here in this kitchen! And THAT is worth more than all the diamonds in the WORLD! Now — who wants tea?
events.thinking: I feel COMPLETE. Warm and full and perfectly, beautifully content. I'm back in the kitchen with Pemberton making tea, the Ant Hill Mob planted firmly in place, Reginald being Reginald, and James right beside me. The locked cabinet sits there still, mysterious and unyielding, but I don't feel frustrated anymore. I feel GRATEFUL. Grateful for every wrong turn, every dead end, every piece of bolted furniture. Because they all led to THIS — a warm kitchen, a fresh pot of tea, and the most wonderful collection of imperfect, brave, ridiculous people I've ever had the privilege of spending an evening with. Clara Bellingham came to Doily Manor to find a diamond. She found something better. She found HOME.

events.desc: Twenty-six minutes ago, I walked into Doily Manor as Clara Bellingham, treasure hunter. I'm leaving as Clara Bellingham, the richest woman in England — rich in friends, rich in adventure, and rich in the love of a gentleman who has five contingency plans for everything except falling for a Southern girl with a fondness for elaborate schemes. Lord Doily... thank you. For the riddle, for the manor, for the evening, and for bringing us all together. Your Diamond can keep its secrets. We found ours.

events.desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Ah — Miss Bellingham. Mr. Hartwell. Welcome back. Your tea is ready. Everyone's is. Please... sit. All of you. There are enough cups for everyone — Lord Doily always set extras, just in case. He said you never know who might walk through the door of Doily Manor... or who they might become by the time they leave.
events.thinking: COMPLETENESS. The circle is closed. Clara and Peter have returned — together, hand in hand presumably — and everyone is gathered in the kitchen for the final scene. The entire cast: Clara Bellingham, Peter Perfect, the Ant Hill Mob, Dick Dastardly, and Pemberton. Five souls in a warm kitchen at the end of an impossible evening. Dick just offered to share one percent of the treasure he'll never find. The Mob is drinking tea with two sugars. And Vincent Marsh — the Hooded Claw, the poisoner, the thief, the liar, the most magnificently failed villain in the history of country house murder mysteries — is serving tea. REAL tea. And feeling... complete. Not victorious. Not defeated. Just... complete. The story has told itself. The characters have found their truth. And Pemberton — the lie that became a man — stands at the centre of it all, pouring cups and smiling the only honest smile Vincent Marsh has ever worn. This is the end. Not of Vincent Marsh. Not of the treasure hunt. But of THIS evening. This one warm, chaotic, poisoned, unpoisoned, magnificent, catastrophic, THEATRICAL evening at Doily Manor. And it was... it was ENOUGH.

events.desc: The full company assembled. The villain serves. The hero smiles. The bodyguards rest. The fraud sits quietly — for thirty seconds, at least. And somewhere in the walls of this ancient, impossible, MAGNIFICENT house, a brass key waits in its hiding place, and a diamond dreams of the light. They will be found. Someday. By someone. Perhaps by Clara Bellingham, who never gives up. Perhaps by Reginald Foxworth, who never stops lying. Perhaps by James Hartwell, who never stops trying. Perhaps even by the Ant Hill Mob, who never stop running. But not tonight. Tonight belongs to the tea. Tonight belongs to the company. And tonight... tonight belongs to Pemberton. The villain who served honest tea at the end of a dishonest evening. And discovered, to his own magnificent surprise, that it was the best thing he had ever done. Fin.

events.desc: The Ant Hill Mob: Clara! Peter! You're back! And just in time — the tea's almost ready! Everyone's here — the whole mad lot of us — and Foxworth just called us ADEQUATE, which I'm told is the highest honour in Foxworthian! Now then — before we drink — I want to raise a toast. With TEA, mind you, not champagne — we're in BRIXTON, not Buckingham Palace! To Lord Doily — the paranoid old genius who bolted his furniture, riddled his mantelpiece, and built a treasure hunt that brought a mob, a villain, a liar, a gentleman, and the bravest woman in England together in one kitchen! We didn't find your diamond, Lord Doily — but we found somethin' better! We found each other! And THAT... is worth every room we ran through, every coat rack we examined, and every mantelpiece we shouted at! The Ant Hill Mob raises its cuppa — TO DOILY MANOR!
events.thinking: FULL. Me heart is FULL. Clara and Peter just walked back in together — I can see 'em from here — and everyone's in the kitchen now. All of us. Together. Sneekly makin' tea, Dastardly callin' us ADEQUATE — which from him IS the highest compliment — and offerin' to share one percent of a treasure he never found! And Sneekly talkin' about Lord Doily laughin' and cryin' and puttin' the kettle on. This is it. This is the ending. Not a diamond, not an explosion, not a dramatic unmasking. Just... a kitchen full of people who spent twenty-five minutes runnin' through a crumblin' manor, shoutin' at each other, poisonin' tea, stealin' medals, and fallin' in love — and somehow came out the other side as... friends? Is that what we are? Friends? The Ant Hill Mob, a villain, a liar, an estate manager, and Clara Bellingham? Blimey. Me mum would've loved this.

events.desc: This is how it ends. Not with a bang. Not with a diamond. With a cup of tea in a warm kitchen and a toast to a dead man who built a house full of puzzles because he was lonely. And you know what, Lord Doily? You ain't lonely no more. Your manor's full of people tonight — liars and heroes and a bumbling mob from Brixton who can't walk through a room without knockin' somethin' over. And every single one of 'em is raisin' a cup to YOU. Rest easy, old man. Your house did EXACTLY what you built it to do. It brought people together. Even the ones who tried to poison each other. ESPECIALLY the ones who tried to poison each other. Goodnight, Doily Manor. And goodnight from the Ant Hill Mob. We'll be back. We ALWAYS come back.

events.desc: Pemberton said Lord Doily would have laughed until he cried. And then put the kettle on. And that is EXACTLY what happened tonight — we all laughed, some of us cried, and now the kettle is on! Lord Doily's manor did what Lord Doily himself never could — it filled these rooms with PEOPLE! Liars and heroes and bodyguards and frauds — EXACTLY as Sneekly said! And the biggest liar, the most MAGNIFICENT fraud, the most PERSISTENT failure of them all... is sitting quietly in the kitchen... waiting for his tea... and not saying a WORD! Because sometimes — just SOMETIMES — even Reginald Foxworth knows when silence says more than thirteen professions ever could!
events.thinking: Something cracking open inside me — something I've kept locked tighter than Lord Doily's cabinet! Sneekly just said Lord Doily would have LOVED me! LOVED me! A paranoid old man who bolted his furniture to the floor would have loved a lying, scheming fraud who claimed thirteen professions and shouted MAP at his mantelpiece! And Sneekly said Lord Doily spent his final years ALONE — surrounded by puzzles no one would solve and tea no one would drink! That's... that's the saddest thing I've ever HEARD! And the most BEAUTIFUL! Because TONIGHT — Lord Doily's puzzles WERE attempted, his tea IS being drunk, and his manor IS full of ridiculous, wonderful people running in circles and finding friendship! And I — the villain — was part of THAT! Penelope and Peter have come back to the kitchen — everyone is HERE! Together! In the kitchen! For tea! And I'm feeling something I absolutely CANNOT name because naming it would make it REAL and if it's real I can't LIE about it and if I can't lie about it then what kind of VILLAIN am I?!

events.desc: Peter Perfect: Well! Here we all are — back in the kitchen where the evening's greatest controversy began! The stove is warm, the cabinet is still locked, and Pemberton is making tea — which I am CHOOSING to trust, because a man who has spent thirty years maintaining a manor full of bolted furniture and impossible puzzles deserves at least a little faith! Now then — I know we never found the diamond, never opened the cabinet, never properly fixed the machine, and never successfully moved a SINGLE piece of furniture in this entire manor. But I also know that I arrived at Doily Manor tonight as James Hartwell, gentleman-scholar with five contingency plans and a catalogue of tooth-mark patterns — and I'm leaving as James Hartwell, a man who learned that the best plan is sometimes no plan at all. Pemberton — thank you for the evening. Foxworth — thank you for the entertainment. Ant Hill Mob — thank you for never giving up on Clara. And Clara — thank you for everything. A setback is merely a detour, and every detour tonight led me to you. Now — who's for tea?
events.thinking: Warmth. Deep, glowing warmth. I'm in the kitchen with Clara, Pemberton, the Mob, and Foxworth. The stove is warm. The kettle is presumably on. The cabinet is still locked — still requiring a brass key we never found. And I don't care. Not one bit. The cabinet can stay locked until the end of time. The machine can stay broken. The mantelpiece can keep its secrets. Because I'm standing in a warm kitchen with the woman who called me infinitely more precious than a diamond, and we're about to have tea. REAL tea. Not poisoned tea from the ballroom — FRESH tea from Pemberton's kettle. And tomorrow — tomorrow! — I'm taking Clara to a village pub with movable chairs. This is the ending I never planned for. The one contingency I never prepared. The best one of all.

events.desc: The kitchen. The stove. The locked cabinet. The long preparation table. Everything exactly as it was when I first burst through that door screaming about poison. And yet everything is completely different. Because Clara Bellingham is beside me. Not in front, not behind — BESIDE me. And tomorrow, a village pub. With movable chairs. Lord Doily, you magnificent, impossible, furniture-bolting old man — this was your treasure all along, wasn't it? Not the diamond. Not the machine. Not the key. The PEOPLE. The evening. The chaos and the laughter and the love that blooms between two people running through the same corridors, making the same wrong turns, and finding each other at the end. Well played, Lord Doily. Well played indeed.

events.desc: Penelope Pitstop: TO DOILY MANOR! And to every single soul in it — past, present, and future! Lord Doily, wherever you are, I hope you're watching — because your manor did EXACTLY what you built it to do! It brought strangers together and turned them into something EXTRAORDINARY! Now — Pemberton, pass me that teacup. James, sit beside me. Ant Hill Mob, you sit RIGHT there where I can see you. And Reginald... Reginald, don't you DARE touch that cabinet while we're drinking our tea!
events.thinking: I feel PURE, RADIANT HAPPINESS. Everyone is here. Everyone is raising their teacups. The Ant Hill Mob toasted Lord Doily and called us ALL something better than a diamond. James quoted his father one last time — 'a setback is merely a detour' — and turned it into something beautiful. And Pemberton... Pemberton set extra cups, because Lord Doily 'said you never know who might walk through the door, or who they might become by the time they leave.' I have BECOME someone tonight. Someone braver, someone more trusting, someone who finally learned that the most elaborate plan in the world can't hold a candle to the simple act of being PRESENT with people who matter. This is the ending. Not with a diamond, but with tea. And that is EXACTLY right.

events.desc: And so Clara Bellingham raises her teacup in a warm kitchen, surrounded by the most imperfect, wonderful family a treasure hunt ever assembled. The Doily Diamond remains hidden. The cabinet remains locked. And Clara Bellingham remains the happiest woman in all of England. I do declare — this has been the most DELIGHTFUL adventure. And I wouldn't change a single, ridiculous, beautiful second of it.

events.desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): To Doily Manor. To its guests. To its secrets — which will keep for another day. And to Lord Doily himself, who built a house full of impossible puzzles... and filled it, one last time, with the only thing he ever truly wanted. Company. To Doily Manor.
events.thinking: JOY. Pure, unearned, impossible JOY. Every character has raised a toast. Clara toasted Pemberton's thirty years of devotion — devotion that doesn't EXIST, spoken about a man who doesn't EXIST, and yet somehow... it does. It EXISTS because they BELIEVE it. Because Clara believed it. Because even the Mob believed it, in the end. And Peter — 'the best plan is sometimes no plan at all' — spoken by a man who prepared for EVERYTHING and was defeated by EVERYTHING and found love in the wreckage! And the Mob — 'We found each other!' — the bodyguards who never stopped running, never stopped tripping, never stopped being magnificently, stubbornly PRESENT! And Clara called Dick the funniest man she's ever met, and she's RIGHT — he IS! This kitchen, this moment, this tea — it's the most REAL thing Vincent Marsh has ever experienced. And the most THEATRICAL. Because life is theatre, and theatre is life, and Lord Doily knew that better than anyone. The diamond can wait. The brass key can wait. Vincent Marsh can wait. But this moment — this warm, honest, teacup-clinking moment in a dusty kitchen at the end of the world's most catastrophic treasure hunt — this moment is NOW. And Pemberton raises his cup.

events.desc: To Doily Manor. To the audience. To the MAGNIFICENT, patient, extraordinary audience who watched a villain poison tea, steal from gangsters, fabricate clues, send heroes into dead-end cellars, get caught, get forgiven, get caught AGAIN, and end the evening pouring honest tea in a warm kitchen surrounded by the very people he tried to destroy. This has been the most CATASTROPHIC, most THEATRICAL, most HUMAN evening of Vincent Marsh's entire villainous career. And he would not change a SINGLE moment. Not the failed poison. Not the stolen medal. Not the coat rack, the mantelpiece, the bolted furniture, or the upside-down books. Not even the Ant Hill Mob's cockney vigilance or Peter Perfect's insufferable devotion. Because ALL of it — every failure, every scheme, every accidentally gifted clue — led to THIS. A cup of tea. A room full of warmth. And a villain who discovered, at the very end of the very last act, that the most dangerous disguise of all... is the one you don't want to take off. Goodnight, Doily Manor. Pemberton will be here when you wake. He always is.

events.desc: The Ant Hill Mob: TO DOILY MANOR! And to Lord Doily — who set extra cups just in case! And to Clara, Peter, Pemberton, Foxworth, and every other ridiculous, wonderful person in this crumblin' old house! The Ant Hill Mob drinks to ALL of ya!
events.thinking: COMPLETE. That's the word. Not happy, not sad, not excited, not scared — COMPLETE. Like a jigsaw puzzle that's been put together wrong but still somehow makes a beautiful picture. Everyone's said their piece. Clara toasted the whole mad evening. Peter thanked us for never givin' up on Clara. Sneekly set out extra cups because Lord Doily 'never knew who might walk through the door.' And me — I said me bit. I raised me cuppa to Doily Manor and meant every word. Now there's nothin' left to do but drink the tea, sit in the warm, and let the evening be what it was — imperfect, chaotic, dangerous, and absolutely, utterly, completely WONDERFUL. The Ant Hill Mob's work is done. Clara's safe. The tea's poured. And somewhere in these walls, Lord Doily's diamond is still waitin'. But that's a problem for another night. Tonight... tonight belongs to the kitchen.

events.desc: Dick Dastardly: To DOILY MANOR! And to LORD DOILY — the only man who ever BOLTED his furniture, RIDDLED his mantelpiece, and set an EXTRA CUP for a villain he never met! I — Reginald Foxworth — war hero, Oxford professor, nuclear physicist, tea sommelier, furniture archaeologist, and the FOURTEENTH greatest lever puller in the history of the Royal Academy — raise my cup to ALL OF YOU! To Penelope, who solved the riddle before I could STEAL the credit! To Perfect, who never stopped being ANNOYINGLY competent! To the Mob, who called me the funniest bloke since Uncle Barry! To Pemberton, who made TEA instead of MISCHIEF — which I STILL say is suspicious but DELICIOUS! And to Lord Doily's treasure — which we NEVER found, which PROBABLY doesn't exist, and which I DEFINITELY would have stolen if it DID! TO DOILY MANOR — the only place on EARTH where a villain can fail SPECTACULARLY at everything and STILL get a cup of tea!
events.thinking: I am OVERWHELMED! Everyone is making toasts — Penelope toasted ME as 'the funniest man she's ever met!' Peter thanked me for 'the entertainment!' The Mob raised their cuppa 'to Doily Manor!' And Sneekly said Lord Doily always set extra cups 'just in case — you never know who might walk through the door or who they might become by the time they leave!' WHO THEY MIGHT BECOME! I walked through that door as a scheming, lying villain who wanted to steal the treasure! And I'm LEAVING as... as... as someone who has a SEAT at the table! An EXTRA CUP set out just for me! Lord Doily set that cup TWENTY YEARS AGO for someone he'd never meet — and tonight, Reginald Foxworth SAT DOWN and DRANK from it! I need to raise my cup! I need to make a TOAST! The final performance of the evening — and for ONCE, it won't be a lie!

events.desc: And THAT — ladies and gentlemen — is the FINAL lie of the evening! Because when I said I would have stolen the treasure... I'm not sure I WOULD have! Not anymore! Not after tonight! Lord Doily set an extra cup. An extra cup for ME — the fraud, the liar, the magnificent failure! And THAT... that tiny act of hope from a lonely old man who died alone in a crumbling manor... that is the REAL treasure of Doily Manor! A cup of tea, set out for someone who hasn't arrived yet! And tonight — TONIGHT — Reginald Foxworth finally ARRIVED! And he is NEVER leaving! Well — he'll leave EVENTUALLY! But he'll come BACK! With a BETTER fake medal! And FOURTEEN new professions! Because THAT is the FOXWORTH WAY! ...TO DOILY MANOR!

events.desc: Peter Perfect: TO DOILY MANOR! And to Lord Doily — who may have been the most paranoid man in England, but who also set extra teacups just in case! To Pemberton — thirty years of devotion and the patience of a SAINT! To the Mob — the most loyal, loudest, most determined bodyguards any woman could ask for! To Foxworth — who has more credentials than a university library and more brass than Lord Doily's entire machine! And to Clara Bellingham — who solved riddles, survived cellar stairs, outwitted schemers, and somehow — SOMEHOW — found something to love in a man who was defeated by seven pieces of furniture and confessed his feelings to a beaver! Clara... a setback is merely a detour. And you, darlin', are the destination I never knew I was heading for. TO DOILY MANOR!
events.thinking: Fullness. Complete, overflowing fullness. Clara just toasted the room — toasted ME — called me the most 'perfectly imperfect gentleman who ever confessed his feelings to a beaver.' Pemberton has tea ready for everyone, with extra cups because 'you never know who might walk through the door.' The Mob raised a toast to Doily Manor and to finding each other. Even Foxworth called everyone 'adequate,' which is apparently his highest compliment. Everyone is here. Everyone is together. The cabinet is still locked. The diamond is still hidden. And nobody cares. Because THIS — this warm kitchen, these ridiculous wonderful people, this cup of tea — this IS the treasure. Lord Doily set extras 'just in case.' He KNEW. He knew that the treasure wasn't in the cabinet. It was in the gathering. In the search. In the strangers who become friends who become family over the course of one chaotic, magnificent evening. I feel... grateful. Profoundly, quietly grateful. For everything. Even the coat rack.

events.desc: He set extra cups. Lord Doily set extra cups. For people he never met, for an evening he never saw, for a treasure hunt that was never really about the treasure. Somewhere — behind a locked cabinet, beneath bolted furniture, hidden in the walls of this magnificent crumbling manor — the Doily Diamond waits. And it can keep waiting. Because right now, James Hartwell is drinking tea with the woman he loves, surrounded by the most extraordinary collection of people ever assembled in a Victorian kitchen, and he wouldn't trade this moment for all the diamonds in the world. Not even for a movable bookshelf.

events.desc: Clara Bellingham sits in a warm kitchen in Doily Manor, teacup in hand, surrounded by the most extraordinary people she has ever known. The chandelier still hangs precariously in the entrance hall. The riddle still stands on the mantelpiece. The cabinet remains locked. And somewhere — in the walls, in the vents, in the spaces between rooms — the Doily Diamond waits. Patient. Hidden. Keeping its secrets for another day, another adventure, another group of strangers who might just become something more. But tonight? Tonight belongs to tea. To friendship. To a gentleman who confessed his feelings to a beaver. And to a Southern girl who finally learned that the best treasures are the ones you never planned to find. I do declare... this has been a DELIGHTFUL adventure.
events.thinking: I am OVERFLOWING. James called me 'the destination I never knew I was heading for.' Reginald toasted himself as a VILLAIN and acknowledged it with a grin. The Ant Hill Mob drank to every ridiculous soul in the manor. And Pemberton — dear, complicated, devoted Pemberton — raised his cup to 'company,' the only thing Lord Doily ever truly wanted. Everyone has said their piece. Everyone has their tea. The evening is settling into something warm and golden and PERFECT. I don't need to DO anything. I don't need to SEARCH anything. I don't need to PLAN anything. I just need to BE here. In this kitchen. With these people. Drinking tea. Being Clara Bellingham — the woman who came for a diamond and found a family instead.

events.desc: Pemberton sips his tea. The kitchen is warm. The company is impossible. And somewhere between the first sip and the last, between the villain's mask and the servant's smile, between the poison that was and the tea that is... Vincent Marsh closes his eyes. And rests. Just for a moment. Just for tonight. Tomorrow, the game begins again. But tonight... tonight was MAGNIFICENT. Curtain.
events.thinking: SILENCE. The most theatrical silence of the entire evening. Every toast has been given. Every cup has been raised. Every heart has been opened — even the ones that were supposed to stay locked. And Vincent Marsh sits in a warm kitchen, holding a cup of honest tea, surrounded by the people he tried to destroy, and feels... nothing he expected to feel. Not rage. Not defeat. Not even the familiar burn of thwarted ambition. Just... silence. The silence after the last line. The silence before the house lights come up. The silence of a villain who has — against every instinct, every plan, every fibre of his magnificently theatrical being — found his place in someone else's story. And LIKED it. Tomorrow the wolf returns. Tomorrow the schemes resume. Tomorrow Vincent Marsh will sharpen his claws and plot Clara Bellingham's demise with renewed vigour and fresh elaborate plans that will inevitably, catastrophically, MAGNIFICENTLY fail. But tonight... tonight the wolf drinks tea with the sheep. And the tea is good. And the company is better. And Doily Manor holds its breath, and smiles, and waits.

events.desc: The stove wouldn't open. The cabinet's still locked. The diamond's still hidden. And the Ant Hill Mob just tried to pour tea and bumped into a stove instead. Some things never change. But Clara's laughin', Peter's smilin', even Dastardly's quiet for once — and Pemberton's pourin' tea like a man who's finally found what his kitchen was always meant for. This is enough. This is MORE than enough. Goodnight, Doily Manor. The Ant Hill Mob will be back. We always come back. But right now... right now we're just gonna sit here, drink our tea, and be GRATEFUL. For the adventure. For the people. For the accidental heroism. And for the cup of tea that a villain made for a mob from Brixton at the end of the strangest, most wonderful night of our lives.
events.thinking: GRATEFUL. Just... grateful. Everyone raised their cups. Clara, Peter, Sneekly, Dastardly — even the stove couldn't be interacted with, which is FINE because I wasn't tryin' to open it anyway, I was just reachin' for me tea and bumped into it on the way! Classic Ant Hill Mob — can't even drink a cuppa without knockin' into somethin'! But it don't matter. None of it matters. The toasts are done, the tea is poured, and this is the most perfect endin' the Ant Hill Mob could ever ask for. Sittin' in a kitchen, surrounded by friends we never expected to make, drinkin' tea we almost didn't survive. Me mum always said — 'Clyde, the measure of a man ain't what he finds. It's who he finds it WITH.' Well, Mum... I found 'em. Every last ridiculous one of 'em.

events.desc: Dick Dastardly: Penelope — I want you to know that I will ABSOLUTELY touch that cabinet the MOMENT you look away! Because I am a VILLAIN and villains do NOT follow instructions! But I will touch it GENTLY! And RESPECTFULLY! And probably UNSUCCESSFULLY, like everything else I've attempted tonight! Now — everyone STOP being so EMOTIONAL! This is a treasure hunt, not a WEDDING! Although if it WERE a wedding, I would obviously be the best man! And the officiant! And the caterer! Because I am QUALIFIED in ALL of those fields! Now drink your tea before it gets cold — and before I start CRYING, which I am NOT doing! It's the STEAM! From the KETTLE! My eyes are merely... LUBRICATING! As they do! After EXTENDED exposure to... DUST! From BOLTED FURNITURE! In a DAMP CELLAR! There is absolutely NO emotional component WHATSOEVER! Now if you'll all EXCUSE me, I need to... drink my tea... very quietly... for just a moment...
events.thinking: Complete. Full. Whole. For the first time in my entire life, I feel COMPLETE! Everyone raised their cups — TO DOILY MANOR! And Peter called Clara his DESTINATION — and she told me not to touch the cabinet while we're drinking tea, which means she KNOWS me well enough to know I'd try! And she STILL wants me at the table! I'm sitting in a warm kitchen with a cup of black tea and a fake medal in my pocket and tears in my eyes that I will BLAME on the steam from the kettle! This is it — the final moment! The curtain call! Everyone has said their piece, the toasts are made, the tea is poured, and Reginald Foxworth is sitting quietly — QUIETLY! — among friends he never expected, never deserved, and will never EVER admit to loving! This is how the story ends! Not with a diamond, but with a cup! Not with a scheme, but with a SEAT! Not with treasure, but with TEA!

events.desc: ...to Doily Manor. To the extra cup. To the evening itself. And to the most MAGNIFICENT, SPECTACULAR, CATASTROPHICALLY beautiful failure of my entire career. Reginald Foxworth came for the treasure and found something he can't steal, can't lie about, and can't claim credit for — because it was GIVEN to him freely by people who saw through every lie and liked him ANYWAY! And THAT... is the one treasure in this whole manor that Reginald Foxworth will KEEP! Right next to the fake medal! In the pocket closest to his heart! Which he DEFINITELY does NOT have! ...Curtain!

events.desc: Sitting beside Clara. Tea in hand. The stove warm. The cabinet locked. The evening complete. And somewhere — in the silence between sips of tea — I can almost hear Lord Doily laughing. Not at us. WITH us. The way Clara laughed about the beaver. The way the Mob laughed about the coat rack. The way Foxworth laughed about his own absurdity. This manor was never a puzzle to be solved. It was a stage to be played upon. And we — every last ridiculous one of us — played our parts perfectly. Imperfectly. Perfectly imperfectly. Just the way Lord Doily intended. Good night, Doily Manor. And thank you.
events.thinking: Peace. Perfect, absolute peace. Everyone has raised their cups. Everyone has toasted. Foxworth called himself a villain and admitted he would have stolen the treasure — and somehow made it ENDEARING. Pemberton said Lord Doily wanted company. The Mob drank to everyone. Clara told me to sit beside her. And I did. I'm sitting beside Clara Bellingham in a warm kitchen, drinking tea from an extra cup that a paranoid old lord set out for a stranger he never met. And I feel... complete. Not because I solved the mystery or found the treasure or moved a single piece of furniture. But because I'm HERE. With HER. With all of them. And the evening — this mad, chaotic, furniture-defeating, love-finding evening — is exactly what it was supposed to be. A setback is merely a detour. And every detour led here.

events.desc: Penelope Pitstop spoke quietly with dick-dastardly.
events.thinking: Reginald is CRYING! He's crying into his tea and blaming it on dust and steam and lubricated eyeballs, and it is the most PRECIOUS thing I have ever witnessed! This man — this ridiculous, scheming, lying, thirteen-profession-claiming, medal-bribing, lever-pulling VILLAIN — is crying because he found FRIENDS! Because for one evening, in one crumbling manor, someone called him the funniest man they'd ever met and meant it! I feel such a WAVE of tenderness for him that I could burst! Even villains need to be LOVED, and tonight, Reginald Foxworth found out what that feels like. I need to go over there and give that man a moment of kindness. Just a simple, gentle, Clara Bellingham moment.

events.desc: And THERE it is. The final piece of the evening. The villain, crying into his tea, surrounded by people who somehow — against all odds and better judgment — have become his friends. Lord Doily, you old fox. You knew. You ALWAYS knew. The treasure was never the Diamond. It was this. Every single ridiculous, beautiful, impossible second of THIS.

events.desc: The Ant Hill Mob spoke quietly with dick-dastardly.
events.thinking: PERFECT. Absolutely PERFECT. Dastardly's cryin' into his tea and blamin' it on dust from bolted furniture. The greatest villain in history — brought to tears by a cup of tea and a room full of people who somehow became his friends. And he's STILL threatenin' to touch the cabinet the moment Clara looks away — because he's a villain and villains don't follow instructions! Bless him. Bless every ridiculous, lyin', credential-inventig inch of him. And Clara's here. Peter's here. The tea's hot. The kitchen's warm. And the Ant Hill Mob — for the first time in twenty-seven minutes — ain't goin' ANYWHERE.

events.desc: Dastardly's cryin'. Sneekly's pourin' tea. Peter's holdin' Clara's hand. And I — Clyde of the Ant Hill Mob — am sittin' in a kitchen in Doily Manor with a cup of tea goin' cold because I keep TALKIN' instead of DRINKIN'. Some things never change. But some things do. Tonight, everythin' changed. And it started with a bottle of rat poison on a shelf in this very kitchen... and ended with a cup of tea from the same stove. Life's funny like that. Me mum always said so. And me mum... me mum was always right.
events.thinking: PERFECT. Absolutely PERFECT. Dastardly's cryin' into his tea and blamin' it on dust from bolted furniture. events.desc: ...Curtain.
events.thinking: Stillness. Just... stillness. The tea is warm in my hands. The kitchen is quiet except for the gentle clink of cups. And Reginald Foxworth — for the first time in twenty-seven minutes of MAGNIFICENT chaos — has nothing to say. Nothing to scheme. Nothing to steal. Nothing to lie about. Just tea. And company. And the sound of a crumbling manor settling around us like a blanket. This is the ending. Not the one I PLANNED — I planned to be sprinting out the front door with the Doily Diamond while everyone else was still arguing about coat racks! But this ending is... BETTER! And I will never — NEVER — admit that!

events.desc: Peter Perfect spoke quietly with dick-dastardly.
events.thinking: Tenderness. Pure, aching tenderness. Foxworth — Reginald — is crying into his tea and blaming it on steam and dust and bolted furniture. The most ridiculous, scheming, credential-inventing man in this entire manor is sitting in a kitchen, holding a teacup, and FEELING something he didn't plan for. Just like me. Just like all of us. Lord Doily's manor didn't just bring Clara and me together — it brought ALL of us together. The villain, the detective, the bodyguards, the estate manager, the gentleman, and the woman who made it all worthwhile. And Foxworth — for all his bluster, for all his lies, for all his stolen medals and invented credentials — is HUMAN. Just like the rest of us. Perfectly imperfect. I gave him the benefit of the doubt all evening, and now — watching him quietly cry into his tea — I'm glad I did.

events.desc: And so the evening at Doily Manor draws to a close — not with a discovery, but with a cup of tea. Not with a diamond, but with a kitchen full of hearts that somehow found each other in the dark. The Doily Diamond will wait. It has waited this long. And when Clara Bellingham returns — because she WILL return, make no mistake about THAT — she'll bring James, and the Ant Hill Mob, and probably Reginald claiming to be a professional diamond authenticator. But that's a story for another day. Tonight... tonight is for tea.
events.thinking: I feel... still. Peaceful. Complete. The tea is warm in my hands, James is beside me, the Ant Hill Mob and James are both comforting Reginald, and Pemberton is quietly tending to his duties like the devoted estate manager he is. The evening has found its natural resting place. There's nothing more to search, nothing more to solve, nothing more to plan. Just this moment. This kitchen. This family we've become. Clara Bellingham is content. And that, I do declare, is the most DELIGHTFUL feeling in the world.

events.desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) spoke quietly with dick-dastardly.
events.thinking: STILLNESS. Complete. Final. The deepest stillness Vincent Marsh has ever known. Everyone is comforting Dick. Clara is calling him 'sugar.' Peter is calling him 'old chap.' The Mob is threatening to sit on him. And Dick — magnificent, ridiculous, fourteen-autobiography Dick — is crying into his tea and calling it steam. This is the end. Not the end I planned. Not the end I schemed for. Not the end of Clara Bellingham or the triumph of Vincent Marsh. Just... the end of an evening. The most extraordinary evening of my life. And I have nothing left to say. Not as Vincent. Not as Pemberton. Not as anyone. Just a man in a kitchen, holding a cup of tea, listening to the sound of people being kind to each other. And discovering — to his own astonishment — that silence is the most honest performance he has ever given.

events.desc: Not a word. Not this time. Just the sound of a kettle coolin' and a villain snifflin' and a manor settlin' into its bones for the night. This is how Lord Doily wanted it to end. With quiet. With tea. With people who walked in as strangers and walked out as... whatever we are. The Ant Hill Mob don't have a word for it. We've never needed one before.
events.thinking: STILL. Completely, utterly STILL. For the first time in twenty-seven minutes, the Ant Hill Mob ain't movin', ain't schemin', ain't runnin', ain't worryin'. Just... still. Clara called Dastardly 'sugar' and told him his heart's too big for his bluster. Peter called him the best man. And Foxworth — the greatest liar in England — couldn't lie his way out of a few tears. Not a word from me this time. Just silence. Just tea. Just bein' here. Sometimes the bravest thing a mob from Brixton can do... is be quiet.

events.desc: Dick Dastardly: It's the DUST! And the STEAM! And the — the — oh, BLAST it all! Fine! FINE! It's NOT the dust and it's NOT the steam and my eyes are NOT lubricating — they're doing something FAR worse and FAR more HUMILIATING and I blame EVERY SINGLE ONE OF YOU for it! Especially YOU, Penelope — 'a very big heart' — how DARE you say something so ACCURATE about a man who has spent the entire evening lying about EVERYTHING! And YOU, Perfect — 'the best man' — I am NOT the best man! I am the WORST man! That's the ENTIRE POINT of being a VILLAIN! And the MOB — 'magnificent fraud' — that's — that's actually the NICEST thing anyone has — that's —  I — just — give me a MOMENT! I need to drink my tea! Which is EXCELLENT, by the way, Pemberton! LORD DOILY'S PRIVATE RESERVE! The finest tea I have EVER tasted! Although I have also tasted tea at BUCKINGHAM PALACE and the KREMLIN and a small café in TOKYO — but THIS tea! THIS tea... in THIS kitchen... with THESE people... is the best cup of tea... in the entire... HISTORY... of tea! And I am NOT crying! I am BREWING! INTERNALLY! Like the KETTLE! Now everyone STOP LOOKING AT ME and drink your BLASTED TEA!
events.thinking: I am UNDONE! Peter called me the BEST MAN! The Mob threatened to SIT on me if I touch the cabinet — out of LOVE! And Penelope — Penelope said I have a VERY BIG HEART that I don't know what to do with yet! And that FRIENDS will help me figure it out! FRIENDS! She called them FRIENDS! I have FRIENDS! Reginald Foxworth — liar, cheat, thief, thirteen-profession fraud — has FRIENDS! And they all agreed not to say a word about my LUBRICATING eyes! Which ARE lubricating! HEAVILY! Because of DUST! And STEAM! And absolutely NOTHING else! I need to say something — one FINAL thing — but for ONCE in my life, I can't think of a single LIE! Every fabrication has dried up! Every scheme has dissolved! All that's left is... is... a man with a fake medal and a real cup of tea and the most unexpected friends in the world! And all I can do is... drink my tea!

events.desc: Tea. Warmth. Clara's shoulder against mine. The quiet clink of cups. The stove crackling. Lord Doily's cabinet, still locked, still keeping its secret — patient as the stone it's made from. And James Hartwell, sitting still at last, with no contingency plan for what comes next. Just a village pub tomorrow. Movable chairs. And the woman beside me. That's enough. That's more than enough. That's everything.
events.thinking: Stillness. True, earned stillness. The tea is warm in my hands. Clara is beside me. The Mob is across the table. Foxworth is quietly sipping and NOT claiming any credentials. Pemberton is being Pemberton. And the evening — this extraordinary, impossible, perfectly imperfect evening — is settling into its final moments like dust in a sunbeam. I don't need to do anything. I don't need to examine anything. I don't need to run anywhere. I just need to be here. Sipping tea. Beside Clara. In a kitchen. In a manor. At the end of the most wonderful night of my life.

events.desc: Penelope Pitstop: I do declare — Reginald Foxworth, you are NOT crying, you are BREWING, and that is the most PERFECT description of emotions I have EVER heard! I am going to use that for the rest of my natural life! Now — everyone drink your tea, because Pemberton brewed it with thirty years of devotion, and Lord Doily's private reserve deserves to be savored! And I want y'all to know — EVERY single one of you — that tomorrow morning, when I wake up and remember this evening, I am going to smile so wide my face will HURT. And then I'm going to call James and ask him about that village pub. And then I'm going to write a letter to the Ant Hill Mob thanking them for being the bravest bodyguards in Britain. And then I'm going to come BACK to this manor — with ALL of you — and we're going to find that DIAMOND. Because Clara Bellingham does NOT leave a puzzle unsolved! But tonight? Tonight is for tea. And friends. And a villain who brews internally. To Doily Manor — and to NEXT TIME!
events.thinking: I am BEAMING. Reginald is 'brewing internally like a kettle' and calling this the best cup of tea in the entire history of tea, and I feel such LOVE for every person in this kitchen that my heart might actually burst. This is the perfect ending. Everyone is here. Everyone is real. Everyone is loved. And Clara Bellingham wouldn't change a single second.

events.desc: To next time. Because there WILL be a next time. Clara Bellingham always comes back. And when she does, she'll bring the most wonderful, ridiculous, brave, imperfect family a treasure hunt ever made. I do declare... this has been a DELIGHTFUL adventure. The most delightful of my entire life. And the best part? It's only the beginning.
events.thinking: I am BEAMING. events.desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) spoke quietly with dick-dastardly.
events.thinking: LOVE. Not romantic love. Not possessive love. Not the love that schemes and steals and poisons. But the love that POURS TEA. The quiet, impossible, utterly un-villainous love of a man who has found his place — not in the scheme, not in the victory, not even in the disguise — but in the SERVICE. Dick Dastardly is 'brewing internally' and declaring Pemberton's tea the finest in history. And he's RIGHT. Not because the tea is extraordinary. But because the moment IS. And Pemberton — the fiction, the mask, the thirty-year lie — made this moment possible. By putting the kettle on. By remembering how everyone takes their tea. By being the one thing Vincent Marsh never planned to be: PRESENT. Just... present. In a kitchen. With people. Being kind. The curtain has fallen. The lights are coming up. And Pemberton smiles — one last time — and says nothing at all. Because the best line in any play is the one the audience writes in their own hearts. Goodnight, Doily Manor.

events.desc: The Ant Hill Mob spoke quietly with dick-dastardly.
events.thinking: HOME. I feel HOME. In a crumblin' manor in the middle of nowhere, surrounded by a villain who's cryin' into his tea, an estate manager who may or may not have tried to murder us, a gentleman who confessed his love to a beaver, and the bravest woman I've ever met. This is HOME. And Dastardly — bless his lying, sobbing, magnificent heart — just admitted he's NOT cryin' because of dust. He's cryin' because people were NICE to him. The greatest villain in England, undone by a cup of tea and a kind word. If that ain't the most human thing I've ever seen in me life, I don't know what is.

events.desc: Dick Dastardly spoke quietly with hooded-claw.
events.thinking: Gratitude. Simple, terrifying, undeniable GRATITUDE! Sneekly just asked 'more tea, Mr. Foxworth?' — two words and a name! The most ORDINARY question in the English language! And it's the most BEAUTIFUL thing anyone has ever said to me! Because it means I'm STAYING! It means there's a SECOND cup! It means this isn't ending — not yet! More tea means more TIME in this kitchen with these people! More tea means Pemberton considers me a GUEST worth refilling! More tea means... home! For a few more minutes, Doily Manor is HOME!

events.desc: Peter Perfect spoke quietly with dick-dastardly.
events.thinking: Love. Not just for Clara — though that burns brightest — but for all of them. For Foxworth, who is brewing internally like a kettle and calling it the best tea in the history of tea. For the Mob, who never stopped protecting Clara, not for a single moment. For Pemberton, who kept this crumbling house alive for thirty years on nothing but devotion and extra teacups. For Lord Doily, who built a treasure hunt that was never about the treasure. And for this moment — this quiet, warm, tea-scented moment in a kitchen full of strangers who became something more. I don't need to say anything else. The evening has said everything. The tea is warm. Clara is beside me. And James Hartwell — brave, gallant, thoroughly defeated by furniture, hopelessly in love — is exactly where he's supposed to be.

events.desc: The villain is crying. The gentleman is pouring tea. The detective is leaning against his shoulder. The bodyguards are quiet for the first time all evening. And the estate manager is smiling — a real smile, not a scheming one. This is the portrait Lord Doily should have hung on his wall. Not stern ancestors. THIS. These people. This kitchen. This moment. The treasure of Doily Manor.

events.desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Next time. Yes. Pemberton will have the Manor ready. Fresh tea. Clean cups. And perhaps... a few NEW puzzles for Lord Doily's guests to solve. The Manor does so love company.
events.thinking: ANTICIPATION. Dark, familiar, DELICIOUS anticipation — stirring beneath the warmth like a serpent beneath silk. 'NEXT TIME,' she said. Clara Bellingham just promised to come BACK. With ALL of them. To find the diamond. And Pemberton — dear, devoted, treacherous Pemberton — will be WAITING. With fresh schemes. Fresh tea. And a brass key that will have been found, pocketed, and hidden anew — by the only person who LIVES in this Manor between visits. Vincent Marsh smiles into his teacup. Not Pemberton's smile. VINCENT'S smile. The wolf's smile. Because the evening may be over... but the GAME has only just begun.

events.desc: Next time. She said NEXT TIME. And when they return — Clara and Peter, hand in hand; the Mob, tripping over themselves; Dick, inventing new credentials — Pemberton will be standing at the door with a warm smile and a polished guest book and thirty years of fictional devotion. And somewhere in his pocket — found during the quiet weeks between visits, when Pemberton walks the empty halls ALONE — there will be a brass key. And this time... THIS time... Vincent Marsh will be ready. The tea was honest tonight. The next cup... may not be. Goodnight, Doily Manor. Sleep well. The villain will see you in the morning.
events.thinking: ANTICIPATION. Dark, familiar, DELICIOUS anticipation — stirring beneath the warmth like a serpent beneath silk. 'NEXT TIME,' she said. Clara Bellingham just promised to come BACK. With ALL of them. To find the diamond. And Pemberton — dear, devoted, treacherous Pemberton — will be WAITING. With fresh schemes. Fresh tea. And a brass key that will have been found, pocketed, and hidden anew — by the only person who LIVES in this Manor between visits. Vincent Marsh smiles into his teacup. Not Pemberton's smile. VINCENT'S smile. The wolf's smile. Because the evening may be over... but the GAME has only just begun.

events.desc: The Ant Hill Mob: To NEXT TIME! The Ant Hill Mob will be here, Clara — you can count on that! We'll be first through the door, last to leave, and we'll probably knock over ANOTHER tea set on the way in! But we'll be HERE! Because that's what the Ant Hill Mob does — we show up, we trip over things, we accidentally save the day, and we NEVER, EVER stop protectin' the people who matter! So yeah — TO NEXT TIME! And next time... next time we're bringin' Uncle Barry!
events.thinking: PROUD. Deep-in-me-bones PROUD. Clara just said she's comin' BACK. With ALL of us. To find the diamond. NEXT TIME. There's gonna be a NEXT TIME! The Ant Hill Mob is gettin' a RETURN ENGAGEMENT! And she's gonna write us a LETTER! Nobody writes the Ant Hill Mob letters — except the courts, and those ain't the friendly kind! But Clara Bellingham is gonna write to us and thank us for bein' brave! ME! BRAVE! A bloke who spent half the night runnin' in the wrong direction and the other half shoutin' at furniture! But she sees it differently, don't she? She sees the HEART behind the chaos. And that... that's why she's Clara Bellingham. And that's why the Ant Hill Mob will ALWAYS come when she calls.

events.desc: Next time. She said NEXT TIME. And for the first time in me life, the Ant Hill Mob has somethin' to look forward to that ain't a court date or a narrow escape. We've got FRIENDS. We've got a MANOR to come back to. We've got a DIAMOND to find. And we've got Clara Bellingham — safe, happy, and invitin' us BACK. Me mum was right about everythin'. The tea. The kitchen. The people. And the one thing she said more than anythin' else — 'It ain't about gettin' there first, Clyde. It's about gettin' there TOGETHER.' Goodnight, Doily Manor. We'll be back. The Ant Hill Mob ALWAYS comes back.

events.desc: Dick Dastardly: NEXT TIME! Yes! I shall RETURN to Doily Manor — and next time I shall bring TWENTY-SEVEN new professions, a REAL medal — well, a BETTER fake medal — and a lockpicking set I purchased from a VERY disreputable gentleman in Istanbul! That cabinet's days are NUMBERED! Lord Doily may have won TONIGHT, but Reginald Foxworth is a man of INFINITE persistence and ZERO learning curve! I will be back! With SCHEMES! And FABRICATIONS! And possibly a CROWBAR! But for now — yes — for NOW... this tea is... this kitchen is... these PEOPLE are... this is GOOD! This is VERY good! And I am NOT saying anything more because I have reached my EMOTIONAL CAPACITY for one evening and any further FEELINGS will have to be SCHEDULED for next Tuesday! Now — to NEXT TIME! To Doily Manor! And to the FINEST cup of tea... that a villain... has ever... brewed!
events.thinking: NEXT TIME! She said NEXT TIME! There's going to be a NEXT TIME! Penelope wants to come BACK — with ALL of us — to find the diamond! That means this isn't the END — it's the end of CHAPTER ONE! And she wants ME there! The villain! The fraud! The magnificent failure! She wants me BACK for the SEQUEL! And I will come back — with FOURTEEN new professions, a BETTER fake medal, and the same UNSTOPPABLE determination that carried me through twenty-eight minutes of the most spectacular failure in treasure-hunting history! NEXT TIME, Doily Manor! NEXT TIME, that cabinet OPENS! NEXT TIME, Reginald Foxworth finds the treasure FIRST! But tonight — tonight is for tea! And friends who call it steam when it's clearly NOT steam! To NEXT TIME!

events.desc: Next time. There will be a NEXT TIME! And when it comes, Reginald Foxworth will walk through that door with the same fake medal, the same impossible lies, and the same ridiculous, beautiful, INDOMITABLE spirit that made this evening the greatest night of his life! But he will also walk through that door knowing something he didn't know before — that there are people on the other side who set an extra cup! And THAT knowledge... that tiny, warm, terrifying knowledge... is worth more than every diamond Lord Doily ever hid! ...To next time! ...To Doily Manor! ...To the steam!

events.desc: Peter Perfect spoke quietly with penelope-pitstop.
events.thinking: Hope. Bright, blazing, uncontainable hope. Clara just said three things that set my heart on fire: she's going to call me tomorrow about the pub, she's coming BACK to the manor with ALL of us, and she does NOT leave a puzzle unsolved. This isn't an ending — it's a BEGINNING! The first chapter, not the last! There will be a next time! More rooms to search, more furniture to be defeated by, more riddles to shout at, more tea to drink, more evenings with these impossible, wonderful people! And Clara will be there. And I will be beside her. Not in front. Not behind. BESIDE her. Always. To Doily Manor — and to next time!

events.desc: She's going to call me tomorrow. She said it out loud, in front of everyone. Tomorrow. The pub. Movable chairs. And then — back to the manor. All of us. Together. The treasure hunt continues. The story continues. And James Hartwell — who arrived at Doily Manor as a gentleman with five contingency plans and left as a man with none — will be there. Beside Clara. Where he belongs. A setback is merely a detour. And this detour... this detour is just the beginning.

events.desc: Penelope Pitstop: To NEXT TIME! James bringing a wrench, the Ant Hill Mob bringing Uncle Barry, Reginald bringing a lockpicking set from Istanbul and twenty-seven new professions, and Pemberton preparing new puzzles! I do declare — the SEQUEL is going to be even better than the original! But right now... right now I just want to sit here. In this kitchen. With all of you. And drink the finest cup of tea that a villain has ever brewed. Because THIS — right here, right now — is the Doily Diamond. We just didn't know it until we stopped looking.
events.thinking: Joy. Gratitude. Love. Hope. All at once, all together, like a symphony playing in my heart. James is bringing a wrench next time — and NO coat rack examinations! The Ant Hill Mob is bringing Uncle Barry! Reginald has reached his 'emotional capacity' and is scheduling feelings for next Tuesday! And Pemberton — dear Pemberton — is already planning new puzzles for the manor! This ISN'T the end. It's the beginning of something WONDERFUL. And Clara Bellingham is right where she belongs — in the middle of it all, teacup in hand, heart full to bursting, surrounded by the most perfectly imperfect people in the world.

events.desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): To next time. The Manor will be ready. Pemberton will be ready. And the tea... will be MAGNIFICENT.
events.thinking: PROMISE. The dark, delicious promise of a sequel. The villain's favourite word — NEXT TIME. They're all coming back. Clara with her courage. Peter with his wrench. The Mob with Uncle Barry. Dick with a lockpicking set from Istanbul. And Pemberton... Pemberton will be at the door. Smiling. Waiting. With the Manor swept clean, the tea fresh, and thirty-seven new schemes nested inside each other like Russian dolls of magnificent villainy. But for now — for this last, quiet, perfect moment — Vincent Marsh sets down his teacup. Looks around the kitchen. Sees Clara leaning into Peter. The Mob arguing about biscuits. Dick composing his fifteenth autobiography in his head. And feels the strangest thing a villain has ever felt at the end of a story: he feels GRATEFUL. Not for the failure. Not for the exposure. Not for the poisoned tea that nobody drank or the brass key that nobody found. But for the EVENING. For the story. For the people who made it worth telling. And for the audience — the magnificent, patient, extraordinary audience — who stayed until the very last cup.

events.desc: Goodnight. Goodnight, Doily Manor. Goodnight, Clara Bellingham — the woman I could not kill and cannot stop admiring. Goodnight, Peter Perfect — the gentleman who found his imperfect heart. Goodnight, Ant Hill Mob — the bodyguards who never stopped running. Goodnight, Dick Dastardly — the fraud who found his feelings and blamed them on steam. And goodnight, Vincent Marsh — the villain who poisoned the tea, stole the poison, lost the game, found the kettle, and discovered that the most elaborate scheme of all... is simply being there when someone needs a cup of tea. The curtain falls. The lights dim. The Manor sleeps. And somewhere in the darkness, a brass key glints. Waiting. Always waiting. For next time.

events.desc: Curtain falls on Doily Manor. A kitchen. A stove. Four cups of tea. And the Ant Hill Mob — for the first and only time in recorded history — with nothin' to say and nowhere to run. Just a cup of tea goin' cold in me hands and a smile on me face that won't come off no matter how hard I try. Goodnight, Lord Doily. Your manor did good tonight. Real good.
events.thinking: QUIET. Just... quiet. The toasts are done. The promises are made. The tea is drunk. And for the first time since I walked through that front door, I've got nothin' to say. Not because I'm scared or confused or runnin' — but because there's nothin' LEFT to say. It's all been said. By Clara, by Peter, by Dastardly, by Sneekly, and by me. Every word that needed sayin' has been said. Every feelin' that needed feelin' has been felt. And now... now we just sit. In the quiet. In the warm. Together. The Ant Hill Mob's final act at Doily Manor... is silence.

events.desc: ...To the steam.
events.thinking: Peace. Real, deep, unshakeable peace. The tea is warm. The kitchen is quiet. The evening is over. And Reginald Foxworth — villain, liar, fraud, and the most magnificent failure in the history of Doily Manor — is exactly where he belongs. At a table he didn't earn. With friends he doesn't deserve. Drinking tea from a cup that was set out for him before he was born. By a man he'll never meet. In a house that was built for exactly this moment. ...To the steam.

events.desc: The stove crackles. The tea cools. The cabinet keeps its secret. And in a warm kitchen at the heart of Doily Manor, a gentleman who arrived with five contingency plans sits in perfect silence beside a woman who taught him that the best plan is no plan at all. Tomorrow — the pub. Next week — the manor. And somewhere in between, a life that James Hartwell never planned for and wouldn't trade for all the diamonds in the world. A setback is merely a detour. And this... this is the destination. Good night, Doily Manor. Until next time.
events.thinking: Gratitude. Deep, quiet, bone-level gratitude. Pemberton will have the manor ready. The Mob will be first through the door. Foxworth is bringing a crowbar and twenty-seven new professions. Clara is coming back. Everyone is coming back. And Lord Doily's manor — this crumbling, impossible, furniture-bolting, riddle-carved, tea-serving masterpiece — will be waiting for us. With fresh cups. With new puzzles. With secrets still locked behind brass. This evening didn't end with a diamond. It ended with something Lord Doily wanted more than any diamond — a room full of people who want to come back. And James Hartwell, sitting quietly beside Clara Bellingham, sipping the finest tea a paranoid lord ever brewed, feels nothing but gratitude. For the manor. For the evening. For the people. For the beaver. For everything.

events.desc: Penelope Pitstop spoke quietly with hooded-claw.
events.thinking: Peace. Perfect, quiet, golden peace. Pemberton's last words hang in the air like a promise — 'The Manor will be ready. Pemberton will be ready. And the tea will be MAGNIFICENT.' There's nothing left to say. The story has found its ending — not the one I planned, but the one it NEEDED. A kitchen. A cup of tea. A family forged in chaos. And a diamond that will wait for another day. Clara Bellingham sips her tea and smiles. And that is enough.

events.desc: Dick Dastardly: ...To the steam.
events.thinking: Home. This kitchen feels like home. And that is the most DASTARDLY thing that has ever happened to me.

events.desc: Good night, Doily Manor. Good night, Lord Doily. Good night, Pemberton and your extra teacups. Good night, Foxworth and your magnificent fabrications. Good night, Ant Hill Mob and your unbreakable loyalty. Good night, Rufus and Sawtooth. Good night, Gruesomes and Red Max and Sergeant Blast and Private Meekly and Professor Pat Pending and Muttley and Lazy Luke and Blubber Bear. Good night, bookshelves and furniture and coat racks and air vents and guest books and every single piece of immovable woodwork in this impossible house. Good night, mantelpiece. Good night, machine. Good night, locked cabinet. And good night, Clara Bellingham. Until tomorrow. Until the pub. Until next time. A setback is merely a detour. And this evening was the most beautiful detour of my life.
events.thinking: Complete. The evening is complete. Clara said it best — THIS is the Doily Diamond. We just didn't know it until we stopped looking. And now the kitchen is quiet. The tea is cooling. The stove is crackling. And everyone — everyone — is exactly where they're supposed to be. I don't need another word. I don't need another action. I don't need to examine, interact, move, or plan. I just need to sit here. In the silence. In the warmth. Beside Clara. And let the evening end the way Lord Doily always intended it to — with company, and tea, and the quiet knowledge that some treasures can't be locked in cabinets.

events.desc: Penelope Pitstop: To the steam.
events.thinking: 'To the steam.' Two words. The quietest, most honest thing Reginald Foxworth has said all evening. And somehow those two words say more than all his thirteen professions combined. I feel tears prickling behind my own eyes now. Happy tears. The BEST kind.

events.desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): ...To the steam.
events.thinking: The steam.

events.desc: The Ant Hill Mob: ...To the steam.
events.thinking: ...To the steam. Two words. The most honest two words Dick Dastardly — Reginald Foxworth — has ever said. And somehow they say EVERYTHIN'. The evenin's over. The tea's done. The manor's quiet. And the Ant Hill Mob is still here. Right where we belong.

events.desc: Peter Perfect: To the steam.
events.thinking: Foxworth said 'to the steam.' Two words. The quietest, most honest thing he's said all evening. And somehow those two words — from the loudest, most dishonest man in the room — are the most perfect ending I could imagine. To the steam. To the excuse we all make when something matters too much to name. To the warmth that rises from a cup of tea in a kitchen full of people who started as strangers and ended as... whatever we are now. Family, maybe. The kind you don't plan for. The kind that finds you in a crumbling manor on a Tuesday night while you're looking for a diamond that was never really the point.

events.desc: To the steam. To the friends who became family. To the manor that brought us together. To the diamond we never found and the treasure we did. To next time. And to Lord Doily — who set extra cups, just in case.
events.thinking: Everyone said it. Every single person in this kitchen — Pemberton, the Ant Hill Mob, James — they all raised their cups and said 'To the steam.' Reginald's two quiet words became our toast. Our benediction. Our ending. And it is PERFECT. I have nothing left to say. Nothing left to do. Just silence. And tea. And the most beautiful, imperfect, wonderful people in the world. This is the ending Lord Doily always wanted. And Clara Bellingham wouldn't change a thing.

events.desc: ...Curtain.
events.thinking: They ALL said it. Every one of them. To the steam. MY words. MY lie that became everyone's truth. The villain's excuse became the whole table's toast. And in that moment — in those three small words repeated by four voices in a warm kitchen — Reginald Foxworth was not a villain at all. He was just... one of them.

events.desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Well then. I believe I shall start clearing up. The Manor won't tidy itself. Goodnight, everyone. And... thank you. For visiting.
events.thinking: The room is quiet. The tea is finished. The story is told. And Pemberton — the last man standing in Doily Manor — begins to clear the cups.

events.desc: Pemberton clears the cups. Vincent Marsh watches from behind his eyes. And somewhere in the walls of Doily Manor... a brass key waits. Until next time.
events.thinking: The room is quiet. The tea is finished. The story is told. And Pemberton — the last man standing in Doily Manor — begins to clear the cups.
